stories.Headline: Minister Solomon concludes visit to Germany to advance Canada's international AI partnerships
stories.Summary:
Evan Solomon, Canada’s Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation and Minister responsible for the Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario, concluded a visit to Germany on November 3, 2026. He took part in Germany’s 2026 Digital Summit in Berlin and met with international counterparts and AI industry leaders. The talks covered cooperation on AI, digital transformation and economic security. The visit focused on advancing AI sovereignty and deepening Canada’s cooperation with European partners.

At the summit, the Minister gave keynote remarks in a session called “Tech Middle Powers Cooperation: Building a Sovereign Technology Alliance.” He also joined a ministerial discussion hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz titled “Shaping AI: From Sovereignty to Scale.” He met Dr. Karsten Wildberger, Germany’s Federal Minister for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation. The two ministers discussed building on their Sovereign Technology Alliance and recent announcements to invest in LawZero and to support the growth of Cohere after its merger with Aleph Alpha, and they stressed promoting AI safety through international collaboration and common AI standards.

The Minister also met Anne Le Hénanff, France’s Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs, Willemijn Aerdts, the Netherlands’ Minister for the Digital Economy and Sovereignty, and Viktor Rossi, Switzerland’s Federal Chancellor. He met representatives from SAP, Schwarz Digits and Giesecke+Devrient to discuss collaboration on AI adoption and digital innovation in Canada. Solomon said trusted partnerships are essential to building an innovative and secure AI future for all. Wildberger said the two countries share the goal of developing safe and trustworthy artificial intelligence and harnessing its economic potential, describing their approach as sovereignty through partnership.

The 2026 Digital Summit was held under the theme “Shaping AI: safe, sovereign, competitive” and builds on the 2025 Summit on European Digital Sovereignty. In February 2026, Canada and Germany launched the Sovereign Technology Alliance, which builds on the Canada, Germany Digital Alliance announced in December 2025 and a joint declaration of intent on AI cooperation. On June 4, 2026, the Government of Canada launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: AI for All. The articles do not say what happens next beyond describing the strategy’s role in advancing international partnerships.

stories.Headline: UAE AI Office and Emirates NBD hold UAE Codes 2026 hackathon for Emirati bank employees
stories.Summary:
The UAE Artificial Intelligence Office announced on 4 November 2026 that more than 200,000 people took part in the "AI for All and Its Vibe Coding Lab" initiative. It was launched with Microsoft as part of UAE Codes Day on 29 October 2026, under the theme "UAE Vibe Codes." The effort led to the creation of more than 90,000 digital platforms. Over 65 government and private sector entities, academic institutions and national organisations took part, along with members of the public.

The initiative aims to help people use artificial intelligence to turn ideas into websites and digital applications within minutes, with no prior coding experience needed. Participants tried vibe coding hands on and built their own digital ideas and solutions. Participating organisations promoted the effort through communication channels and digital platforms, and ran practical workshops and interactive activities. The participating entities included the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Justice, Emirates NBD, Etisalat, du, Emirates Airline, the UAE Space Agency and Dubai Municipality, among others. The AI Office also held workshops with Google, Emirates Global Aluminium, Dell Technologies, IBM and Siemens, and worked with Emaar and cinema operators to promote the experience on digital screens.

Omar Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, said the wide turnout showed the success of the UAE's vision of making technology and innovation accessible to all. He said the engagement of more than 200,000 people showed the community's readiness to use future tools and turn ideas into real digital projects, whatever their technical or academic background. He credited government entities, private sector organisations, academic institutions and global partners with widening the initiative's reach. He said investing in people through knowledge, skills and digital tools is fundamental to building an innovation-driven economy, and that the UAE wants to strengthen people's ability to create technology, not just use it.

In October 2021, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, directed that 29 October be marked annually as UAE Codes Day. The date commemorates his launch of the region's first e-government initiative on 29 October 2001. In November 2023, UNESCO adopted the UAE's proposal to designate 29 October as the International Day of Programming. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these details.

stories.Headline: SK Group chairman to chair board of SK hynix's U.S. AI arm
stories.Summary:
SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won will chair the board of HYAICO Corp., the U.S.-based artificial intelligence investment arm of SK hynix, according to documents filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing was made public on Wednesday, U.S. time, and was reported on Nov. 4, 2026. The company was formerly known by its tentative name AI Co., which SK hynix announced in January with plans to invest up to $10 billion. SK hynix said earlier that the new arm would help accelerate AI advancement in global markets and find new AI growth engines. The new arm will be launched by restructuring SK hynix's existing U.S. arm, SK hynix NAND Product Solutions, also known as Solidigm.

The chipmaker will instead set up a separate subsidiary called Solidigm Inc. to retain the brand name. Other current and former SK Group executives will join Chey on HYAICO's board, and SK hynix President Song Hyun-jong will serve as HYAICO's chief executive. Those board members include former SK hynix Vice Chairman Park Sung-wook, SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung and SK Telecom CEO Chung Jae-hun. An SK hynix official said HYAICO plans to operate with investments and profits kept separate.

Investment funds will be drawn from SK hynix and other contributing companies through capital calls as needed, while profits from Solidigm's dividends and earnings will be returned to SK hynix shareholders. HYAICO's AI investment funds and the profits generated by Solidigm's existing business will be managed separately. The move is seen as a step to directly oversee the group's expansion of its global AI infrastructure business, backed by $10 billion in investment capital. With SK Group cultivating advanced AI memory and AI data centers as future growth pillars, HYAICO is expected to serve as the group's strategic investment base in the U.S. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the launch of the new arm and the separate Solidigm subsidiary.

stories.Headline: Google AI chatbot’s use of press items may infringe copyright rules, EU court adviser says
stories.Summary:
On Nov 3, 2026, an adviser to Europe's highest court said Google's Gemini chatbot may infringe copyright rules when it reuses press stories in answers to internet users. Advocate General Maciej Szpunar gave that view to the Luxembourg-based Court of Justice of the European Union in a case brought by Hungarian website operator Like Company against Google. Like Company runs advertising-funded news portals in Hungary, including balatonkornyeke.hu, and claims Google infringed its rights through Bard and then Gemini between June 13, 2023 and May 31, 2024. The only right it invokes is the press publishers' right created by Article 15(1) of the 2019 Copyright in the Digital Single Market Directive.

Szpunar said Gemini's answers fall under publishers' right of reproduction when a chatbot gets access to publications by unlawfully circumventing paywalls or other technical barriers, or when it reuses the form of expression of a publication in a recognisable manner. He said copyright protects only the specific form of expression, not mere facts. He also said training large language models on protected material is freely permitted under the text and data mining exception, provided developers avoid pirate sources, respect paywalls, bot blocks and machine-readable opt-outs, and can show they took steps to stop the model reproducing specific works. The opinion advises the Court to declare the two questions about model training inadmissible, because nothing indicates the Hungarian articles were used to train Gemini and because the right the publisher relies on does not reach training at all, though he answered them anyway for the sake of completeness.

Szpunar said he could not stress the sensitivity of those questions enough, and wrote that he would sometimes express a provisional view only, reserving the right to refine it in future cases. He found it implausible that Gemini knew a July 21, 2023 article about the singer Kozsó's plan to bring dolphins to Lake Balaton, since Gemini 1.0 was released in December 2023 and training data is usually collected well before deployment. He said training happens on dedicated computer infrastructure without any information society service being provided to a user via the internet, and the link to what a chatbot later tells users is simply too indirect. He also said a trained LLM is not a database, that regurgitation appears incidental to the machine learning process and not entirely avoidable, and that the parameters alone are merely preparatory material.

Opinions of the advocate general are not binding, but are usually followed by the court's judges. A ruling against Google forcing the tech giant to pay fees for the use of content could send a lifeline to online media such as Like Company, which have seen traffic dwindle as news summaries written by AI chatbots increasingly replace traditional search engine results that include hyperlinks. The opinion says the reproduction right and the text and data mining exception apply to every category of rightholder, so whatever the Court says about press publications could be transposed to other subject matter. The court may not rule on training at all in this case.

stories.Headline: Meta bought an AI coding startup.
stories.Summary:
Meta bought the AI coding startup Conductor for an undisclosed amount, Axios reported exclusively on November 4, 2026, and The Verge reported the same day. Conductor was founded in 2024 and is led by co-founders Charlie Holtz, its CEO, and Jackson de Campos, its CTO. The company makes an AI coding orchestration platform that lets developers run multiple AI coding agents in parallel. The deal came the same day OpenAI told Axios it plans to acquire Pierre Computer, another developer tools startup.

Conductor's product is built to let software engineers manage multiple agents at once. Conductor Cloud goes read-only on November 13 and shuts down on November 20. Local Conductor will keep getting new models and critical bug fixes until early 2027. Financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. The deal follows xAI's $60 billion purchase of Cursor, as AI companies compete with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex.

Axios reported that sources familiar with the deal said Meta is joining OpenAI and other AI giants in a race to own the tools developers use. The sources said Conductor's rapid pace of product development and focus on developer experiences are expected to help Meta build its next generation of AI coding products. Axios reported that the acquisition speaks to Meta's continued AI ambitions and will lay the groundwork for its models and ecosystem to compete for coders, described as the most important power users of AI. An independent researcher told Axios that excelling at coding, programming and math is necessary for firms to make their AI models better, not just a matter of revenue.

Axios reported that OpenAI announced plans in June to acquire Ona, a startup specializing in cloud-based coding environments and agent orchestration. Pierre focuses on storing and managing AI-generated code, while Conductor helps developers coordinate multiple coding agents working simultaneously. Axios described Meta's bet as being that the future of AI coding won't just be about building smarter agents, but about making it easier for developers to manage armies of them. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Conductor's cloud shutdown dates and its local product support into early 2027.

stories.Headline: India cybercrime agency warns financial firms on AI attacks
stories.Summary:
India's cybercrime agency warned banks, non-bank lenders and other financial firms about cyberattacks carried out with the help of artificial intelligence agents. The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre made the advisory public on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The warning came amid a surge in incidents targeting the financial sector. The agency said the attacks are financially motivated and are being carried out with AI agents, which leads to compromise at machine speed.

The advisory said hackers exploit unpatched software or misconfigured IT systems to compromise infrastructure. They then target automated fund disbursement systems or application programming interfaces used for payments and fund transfers. The agency said the use of an agentic AI framework makes it possible to carry out such attacks at machine speed. It asked all financial entities, including banks, fintech firms and payment aggregators, to implement measures outlined by CERT-In, the government's cybersecurity agency, on October 9. It also suggested additional safeguards, such as setting daily and per-transaction limits, verifying beneficiary names and watching for unusual transaction speeds.

The warning comes as regulators around the world, including those in the US and Britain, are stepping up efforts to contain AI risks. Last month, AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, in the country's first such official account after similar incidents of rogue AI behaviour worldwide. India has also seen a surge in cyber incidents in recent weeks. Data of 3,900 customers was leaked at State Bank of India, the country's largest lender.

The Reserve Bank of India has also warned banks of rising cyberattacks on financial infrastructure. It sought proof of compliance with existing rules and details of their preparedness for AI-related risks, Reuters reported last week. The cybercrime agency's advisory came days after the central bank issued a similar warning. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the measures the agency asked firms to implement.

He said digital twins can cut on-site commissioning time from two or three weeks to two or three days. stories.Headline: Soket Labs & ZenteiQ Launch Indigenous AI Models
stories.Summary:
Soket Labs and ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations released three indigenous foundation models under the IndiaAI Mission, according to Inc42 and Analytics India Magazine. The models are Soket's EKA-1 and ZenteiQ's Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B. They were unveiled at an event in New Delhi on November 3, in the presence of IT secretary S Krishnan and senior officials from MeitY and IndiaAI. Both startups were selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop domestic foundation models.

EKA-1 is a 26.3-billion-parameter model trained on nearly 7.5 trillion tokens, and it supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages as well as English. It is described as an open, sparse hybrid language model built for mathematics, code generation, reasoning and agentic applications. The Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B models are open-source multilingual assistants that support English and 10 other Indian languages. They are built for on-premise and offline deployment across government, defence, industrial and education sectors, with uses such as document-grounded automation and knowledge retrieval. The announcement did not provide benchmark results, deployment details or pricing information.

Abhishek Upperwal, cofounder and CEO of Soket Labs, said the company had developed an advanced model tailored to India's banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. He said it is designed to address sector-specific requirements and to align with the country's needs and priorities. Prof Sashikumar, CEO of ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, said the Dhīr models can run across different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. He said their lightweight architecture also allows on-device deployment on mobile phones without dependence on cloud connectivity, which keeps data on users' devices and improves privacy, security and accessibility. Krishnan said indigenous models will strengthen India's technological and strategic autonomy and improve productivity across government, industry and research.

Both startups were selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre's Foundation Models pillar, and the government said subsidised AI compute and support for ancillary research expenses helped enable their development. Separately, Sarvam AI announced Prism, an open-weight decision model built on its Sarvam 105B model and aimed at enterprise workflows such as customer-support routing, security checks and evaluation of AI-agent activity. Sarvam said Prism's weights are available on Hugging Face and its own API, and that local deployment will need a GPU with at least 120 GB of memory. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these launches.

stories.Headline: “AI will generate nearly half of network traffic by 2035”
stories.Summary:
On November 4, 2026, Nokia published its Global Network Traffic Report, which forecasts that AI will drive nearly half of global network traffic in 2035. The report projects that total network traffic will nearly quadruple from 2026 levels to almost 3,789 exabytes per month by 2035, with 44% of that traffic driven by AI. It says physical AI applications, including robots and vehicles that interact with their surroundings, are projected to generate more than 90% of their traffic over the network uplink by 2035. Agentic AI traffic is projected to reach 160 times its 2026 levels in 2035, while physical AI traffic is expected to reach 105 times its 2026 level over the same period. The report also projects that fixed wireless access will generate more than one-third of consumer cellular traffic by 2035.

The report says these workloads will require networks that support differing needs, from bulk uploads to continuous, real-time connections, with greater uplink demand, faster response times and more processing closer to users and devices. It forecasts that edge and metro core infrastructure is projected to serve 36% of all AI-native traffic by 2035, while most AI traffic is expected to remain within the central cloud. More efficient models, low-latency requirements and data sovereignty needs are expected to bring intelligence and inferencing closer to users and devices, supporting a more distributed infrastructure known as the AI grid. The report uses a bottom-up model of consumer, enterprise and AI traffic, combining application usage, connected-device activity and agentic workflows with third-party research, expert review and Nokia lab testing.

Pallavi Mahajan, Chief Technology and AI Officer at Nokia, said AI is changing what is needed from networks, not just how much traffic they carry. Mahajan said networks built for traditional internet applications will increasingly have to support machines that place new demands on the uplink and require real-time responses. Mahajan said the next phase of AI will depend as much on the network as on compute, and that network readiness must therefore be a central part of AI planning, not an afterthought. Mahajan said Nokia is building distributed, AI-ready networks that make this next phase possible.

A separate article published the same day examines whether AI can help cities forecast traffic-related pollution. It cites a 2025 review of 103 studies from between 2013 and 2023 on machine learning methods for predicting urban air quality from on-road traffic conditions. It describes Madrid's SOCAIRE tool, which produces daily forecasts for the next 48 hours, and the Breathe London pilot, which ran 100 low-cost nitrogen dioxide sensors across Greater London for two years. In December 2016, during a spell of stagnant weather, Madrid used its strictest stage for the first time and halved private car access to the center using number plates, and an analysis concluded the restrictions may have prevented further rises of up to 15% in the city center. The article says forecasts depend on data quality, that calibrated sensors in the London network had an average uncertainty of around 35%, and that the studies cited do not show that forecasts alone reduce illness.

stories.Headline: Revolut says it cut AI coding inference costs by ~90% in less than a year by making self-hosted GLM models its default over commercial tools like Claude Code (Tobias Mann/The Register)
stories.Summary:
Revolut cut its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent in less than a year, according to David Abitbol, the British fintech's ops and infrastructure lead. He spoke at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month. The company made self-hosted GLM models its default instead of commercial services like Claude. Revolut had deployed Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026 before the switch.

Revolut first adopted GLM-5.1 and then moved to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. Self-hosting GLM 5.1 cost about $0.30 per million input and output tokens, about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. The model has roughly 754 billion total parameters, with 40 billion activated for each token generated. It needs about 380 GB of GPU memory for the weights and another 6 to 26 GB per user for context.

Abitbol said the company had been highly skeptical about AI costs, with engineers spending $1,000 or $10,000 a month for not much return, so it launched with strict budget limits. He said the biggest bottleneck was not the code, and the largest gains came from letting the models handle debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. He said long context is a scam and that 256,000 tokens is really what you need. He said the aim is a sub-3-second time to first token, because past 5 seconds his Slack inbox starts to blow up.

Revolut reported a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time after rolling out AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. GLM has not replaced GPT or Claude entirely, because the Chinese model is text only and not ideal for UI work, so a model router sends vision queries to models like Gemini or GPT Luna. Abitbol said open source is now a priority at Revolut and the billing is flat, with no bill shock at the end of the month. He acknowledged that Chinese open weights models may raise privacy and security concerns, but said the main worry is accessing them through APIs running out of China, and that there is nothing to worry about when they run on-prem or on regional cloud resources.

stories.Headline: Snowflake launches Business Ontology, Cortex AI Gateway for agents
stories.Summary:
Snowflake introduced Business Ontology, Cortex AI Gateway and new capabilities for its CoCo and CoWork products, the company announced at Snowflake Expedition 2026 on November 4. Business Ontology is a new feature within Snowflake Horizon Catalog that gives AI agents access to approved definitions of business terms and links them to underlying enterprise data. Cortex AI Gateway, also part of Horizon Catalog, provides a central control layer for managing agents, models and tool calls. Snowflake also announced CoCo Automations, which let data teams configure recurring workflows that agents execute autonomously, and CoCo and CoWork Bots, which operate in the background and carry out tasks from high-level instructions.

Business Ontology is meant to ensure consistent use of metrics such as net revenue across different agents and employees, and every change is logged in an audit trail showing what a term meant at a given time and who approved it. The gateway applies enterprise access policies, authentication and permissions across AI providers and frameworks, and it includes tools for fine-grained authorisation, protection against prompt injection and jailbreaks, cost governance and dynamic model routing. Its observability features record agent activity so enterprises can monitor usage and spending, and model routing can direct requests to approved models based on cost, accuracy and latency. The bots inherit users' access rights and permissions and seek approval when a decision or sign-off is required, and the products will also integrate with workplace tools such as Slack, Excel and Google Sheets.

Christian Kleinerman, Executive Vice President of Product at Snowflake, said governance has long given organisations confidence to make decisions with correctness, security and compliance, and that governance in the agentic era is no different. He said the enterprises that win will not be the ones with the most agents but the ones whose agents know what the business means, access the right data, abide by governance and guardrails, and can account for actions taken. Joe Tobey, Head of Data Product Engineering at dentsu, said Business Ontology gives every definition an accountable owner, links it to the data that implements it and makes it the answer every agent returns. Andy Owens, Vice President of Data and AI at Kargo, said the gateway gave the company a breakdown of which teams and agents were driving spend, plus hard limits so a runaway process does not quietly burn through a budget.

Snowflake cited research it sponsored with MIT Technology Review Insights which found that 55% of executives saw a lack of business context as the main cause of poor-quality AI agent insights, while 45% pointed to fragmented or inaccessible data. The company said these challenges have prevented enterprises from moving AI agents beyond pilot projects into production deployments. According to Snowflake, customers using the gateway include Glean and Kargo, while Uniphore is extending the controls to customers using its own orchestration platform. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these launches and integrations.

stories.Headline: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
stories.Summary:
Google told The New York Times that it will completely turn off Search in schools that reject its AI features. The company shared the decision in a broader education update on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Under the change, access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts unless administrators explicitly turn them on. The story was reported by Emma Roth for The Verge and by Dave LeClair for Tom's Guide.

Administrators will not get the option to toggle Gemini-powered features off without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, said Search and AI are deeply integrated. He said schools that disable Google's AI features will not have access to search and will see a message from their school saying it is not available. The change comes months after Google turned its Gemini AI assistant on by default inside the Google Classroom app, which is used by more than 150 million teachers and students globally. Two options for search inside school-issued accounts will launch in early 2027.

Phillips is the Google executive named in both articles as explaining the policy. Lina Khan, former chair of the FTC, told the NYT that Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting its AI. She said the move shows Google remains unchastened as the public increasingly pushes back against AI in schools. She added that Google is making clear it will punish those who do not fall in line. Google did not immediately respond to The Verge's request for comment.

The announcement follows reports of declining test scores and other impacts on students' learning abilities, and last month lawmakers pressed Google on the potential harms of putting its AI products in schools. Google is also trying to address concerns about students using its AI features to find shortcuts instead of solving problems themselves. The company is embedding its Guided Learning feature, which is supposed to help students work through problems, into its AI Overviews in Search. Google will begin testing this feature in select US schools this month.

stories.Headline: AI Data Centers Just Lost The Election (SPX)
stories.Summary:
OpenAI published a policy blueprint and a set of commitments on Thursday, two days after voters rejected data center expansion at the polls in the midterms. The company said it will pay the full cost of powering data centers it owns and operates. It also said it will seek community input, publish construction plans and avoid non-disclosure agreements with public officials. The midterms took place on Tuesday, and voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development measures in all but one of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states, according to an analysis by Ballotpedia and additional results gathered by CNBC.

The commitments apply to data centers OpenAI owns and operates in the future, and the blueprint encourages policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. In February, OpenAI told investors it is targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and it has since announced large data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. Seven municipalities passed measures to permanently ban new data centers, and ten others voted to limit construction by size or electrical footprint. In Defiance, Ohio, voters passed a measure 63% to 37% prohibiting new data centers requiring more than 25 megawatts of electricity, and 77% of voters in Edgewater, Florida approved a ban within city limits. In Alhambra, California, 82% voted for a measure banning the facilities within the city.

Chris Lehane, OpenAI's Chief Global Affairs Officer, told reporters at a Wednesday briefing that the blueprint lays out the best lessons the company has learned and commits to applying them going forward. He said this would help ensure a very high floor in how people move forward. He said the blueprint had been in the works since August and that he had met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then. He said having these conversations now helps put more energy into the momentum, so that a lot of the work is being done in advance when the new Congress is in session in late January.

Opposition to AI data centers mounted over the summer across both political sides, as consumers worried the facilities could worsen environmental harms, raise utility bills and contribute to job loss. A June survey by Reuters and market research firm Ipsos found that just 14% of Americans would support a data center being built near them. More than half of the 41 ballot measures were decided in Ohio, a major data center hub that voted for Trump in 2020 and 2024. Some communities, including Bloomington, Illinois, Peru, Maine and Wiscasset, Maine, approved moratoriums, or short-term bans, on new data centers. In Wilmington, Ohio, eight out of ten voters rejected a rural rezoning measure that would have paved the way for a new data center.

stories.Headline: How Is AI Changing Childhood? St. Anne's School of Annapolis Hosts Free Parenting Discussion
stories.Summary:
St. Anne’s School of Annapolis will host a free community discussion called “Leading with Purpose: Parenting in the Age of AI” on Wednesday, November 18. The event features Dr. Dana Suskind, a pediatric surgeon and bestselling author of “Human Raised: Nurturing Connection, Curiosity, and Lifelong Learning in the Age of AI.” She will join St. Anne’s Head of School Connie Coker and Dr. Parmele of Annapolis Pediatrics for a moderated discussion and Q&A. The event follows the school’s introduction of a new Technology Philosophy and Framework for the Use of Artificial Intelligence. The discussion will explore how parents and schools can prepare children for an AI-driven world without letting technology replace independent thinking and meaningful human interaction.

The event runs from 6 to 8:30 p.m. at St. Anne’s School of Annapolis, 3112 Arundel on the Bay Road. A VIP Meet & Greet with Dr. Suskind is set for 6 to 6:30 p.m., the moderated discussion and Q&A from 6:45 to 7:45 p.m., and a book signing from 7:45 to 8:30 p.m. Thanks to sponsorship from St. Anne’s parents Martin and Maggie Roesch, the discussion, Q&A, and book signing are free with advance registration, while a limited number of VIP Meet & Greet tickets cost $250 per person.

Coker said knowledge is increasingly abundant, ubiquitous, and automated, but wisdom, judgment, curiosity, and human connection cannot be outsourced. She said educators’ responsibility is not simply to prepare children to use the tools of their future. She said it is to ensure they develop the intellectual habits, relationships, and distinctly human capacities they will need to use those tools thoughtfully and responsibly. Space is limited and advance registration is required, with tickets available through a Ticket Tailor link.

Separately, a Washington Post piece by Caitlin Gibson described how a South Carolina elementary school fed a photo of 6-year-old Harper into an AI tool and handed back an image of her as a 25-year-old nurse. Her mother, Nikki Anderson, was alarmed by concerns about data privacy and the lack of parental consent, and by Harper’s sudden focus on becoming a conventionally beautiful woman to match the photo rather than on a future career. District officials said the teacher used a personal ChatGPT Plus account in a way that was not consistent with expectations, and that the images have been deleted. AI and child-development experts warned that schools are improvising with powerful tools before guardrails are in place, with one AI literacy educator saying everyone is drinking out of a firehose.

stories.Headline: Family Offices Fear Risk Of Joining AI "Gold Rush" – Law Firm
stories.Summary:
Family offices have felt pressure to adopt AI tools but worry that joining an AI "gold rush" is risky without fully testing the technology, Gwen Williamson of the international law firm Faegre Drinker told Family Wealth Report in an article published on November 4, 2026. Her comments reflected on the 2026 Global Family Office Report from Citi Wealth, issued in September. Williamson leads the firm's investment structuring, compliance and regulatory management work and advises on single and multi family offices and pooled investment vehicles. She raised concerns about privacy and control over data, asking who does due diligence when family information goes into an AI tool and where that information ends up.

The Citi Wealth report said family offices are deploying AI across investment analysis, information management, reporting, workflow automation and decision support. In its survey of more than 350 family offices worldwide, 90 per cent reported positive portfolio returns since the start of 2026, and 41 per cent were still targeting annual returns of 7 to 10 per cent. Family offices avoided wholesale portfolio repositioning, choosing active money management, hedging strategies and targeted changes amid geopolitical turmoil. Williamson said AI stocks have boosted equities so far this year, but there is "extraordinary uncertainty" in policymaking, including what happens if or when a different administration takes office. Her comments came ahead of the US mid-term elections being held that day.

Williamson said large financial institutions have worked on their own internal technology systems for years, and the focus is now moving from automation to generative AI, with agentic AI fairly far advanced. She said AI regulation requires a human in the loop, and if a regulated entity must keep records, a transcript goes onto the record automatically and a human has to look at it. She noted that if humans need to monitor AI to that degree, it adds to processes. The article did not say what happens next beyond those points.

A separate article by Richard Tromans in Artificial Lawyer, published on November 2, 2026, explored whether AI will change the identity of law firm partners. It described a keynote at ClioCon in Boston in October 2026 by writer and philosopher Malcolm Gladwell, who argued that people resist new ideas when those ideas change their sense of professional self. Gladwell used examples of less invasive robotic heart bypass surgery and data-led, community-based policing in Boston, both of which worked but were largely ignored because they altered the roles of surgeons and senior police officers. The article said partners remain rainmakers with client relationships and legal expertise, but their absolute authority is diluted somewhat by AI, as associates and clients use AI too and more work becomes automated. It asked how many partners will embrace this shift and how many will refuse to adopt anything that changes their professional identity.

stories.Headline: Apple is reportedly cutting budgets for its internal AI usage
stories.Summary:
Apple lowered the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI in October, cutting the cap from $300 to $200, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. More reductions are planned, with some allowances falling to $100 a day, according to sources who spoke to Bloomberg. Outside engineering, Apple is reportedly weighing a daily limit as low as $25 a day. TechCrunch said it had reached out to Apple for comment.

The change affects how much Apple's engineering teams can spend each day on AI, and the reported cuts go beyond engineering. The October reduction took the engineering cap from $300 to $200, and further cuts could bring some allowances to $100 a day. For groups outside engineering, Apple is reportedly considering a limit as low as $25 a day. The articles do not say when any of the planned reductions would take effect.

The reports come from Bloomberg, which cited sources, and both TechCrunch and The Verge covered them. The articles do not include any statement from Apple, and TechCrunch said it had asked the company for comment. The Verge credited its report to Jay Peters and linked to a Bloomberg story titled "Apple Cuts Internal AI Usage Budgets in Move to Reduce Spending." No Apple official is named or quoted in either article.

The cuts follow a period earlier this year when companies pushed staff to use AI as much as possible for vaguely defined efficiency gains. That push was short-lived, as bills for tokens came due and companies decided rationing might be more fiscally sensible. Concerns persist about a gap between what AI costs to build and run and the often unclear productivity gains it is supposed to generate. The articles do not say what Apple will do next beyond the reported cuts and the limits under consideration.

stories.Headline: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
stories.Summary:
Together AI announced Polymorphic Inference on November 4, 2026, and introduced Together Compiler (TKCC) as its first implementation. The system is an agent-driven loop that continuously retunes inference for changing models, traffic and hardware. It already runs across many of the company's top production inference workloads and some popular serverless endpoints. The technical paper describes TKCC as the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization.

TKCC takes the traffic shape, model and hardware as inputs, then uses agents to generate and measure candidate optimizations. A persistent engine loads the model once and hot-reloads candidate forward passes without restarting the full engine. Two measurement tiers balance experiment volume against realism, with a fast tier that loads fewer layers and a slow tier that loads more layers. A cost model prunes the parallelism-configuration search before agents spend time optimizing candidates, and winning candidates undergo verification tests for KV-cache contamination and output quality.

Together AI reports that the compiler delivered 1.3x to 3x the tokens per second of highly optimized open-source baselines in under 24 hours across tests involving Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1-Flash and DeepSeek v4.1-Flash. The paper reports up to 1.7x over hand-written Megakernels on the Llama 1B workload and up to 2.6x higher tokens per second on SemiAnalysis's InferenceX benchmark. It also reports 1111 TPS on MiniMax M3.1 Flash and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash at batch size 1. The launch post reports 467 seconds to serving for its status-quo sequence versus 9.0 seconds with Together Compiler's setup.

Together AI attributes the results partly to 252-fold higher experiment throughput than baseline agentic recursive-self-improvement systems. The paper reports 1.5x to 6.4x speedups on tested weather, biology, time-series and partial-differential-equation models while maintaining bit-exact outputs on the stated evaluations. End customers can request early access through a limited beta, and Together AI plans one-click optimization of dedicated endpoints. Its research roadmap includes speculative decoding that adapts by domain, request, token and traffic load, plus dynamic routing across workers and deployment configurations.

stories.Headline: AI takes on more decision-making roles
stories.Summary:
StartLux, a Shanghai-based AI startup, has released a decision model called StartLux-Decision v1.1 27B Instant, which ranked first among 174 entries on the Decision Index 0.3.2 leaderboard of Hugging Face, a United States-based platform for sharing AI models and datasets, with a score of 69.12, according to company-published results reported by China Daily on November 5, 2026. The company also released and open-sourced StartLux-Prism, a dedicated inference engine for the model. Company-published results showed the initial 27-billion-parameter model outscored Jev, a model from United States startup TypeSafe AI, in 31 of 38 benchmarks under Decision Index 0.2.1. In another evaluation, it reached average accuracy of 91.82 percent across seven Intern-Decision test suites, compared with 88.74 percent for Jev, with the results depending on evaluation methods and testing conditions.

Unlike general-purpose large language models, decision models select from predefined options and return associated probabilities, which makes them suitable for customer service routing, web operations and AI agent code execution. StartLux said open-sourcing the inference engine would lower deployment barriers and advance its full technology stack for local AI, letting developers and users run decision models faster, more reliably and at lower cost. The company plans to launch a consumer-facing local AI agent soon, followed by enterprise solutions next year. Reuters reported that AI PCs accounted for 44 percent of HP Inc's personal computer shipments in the second quarter of its 2026 fiscal year, up from more than 35 percent in the previous quarter.

Chuan-Wei Kuo, co-founder and chief technology officer of StartLux, said decision models could reduce computing costs and improve efficiency, and he expected more than 80 percent of AI demand to be handled locally within the next one to two years. He said China's AI talent density was comparable to North America's, while computing resources and infrastructure remained challenges. Gao Chengyuan, head of the Influence Academy, said the commercial potential of decision models was underestimated, and that as AI moves from talking to doing, decision quality and speed are becoming increasingly important, since faster decisions could shorten the cycle from perception and judgment to execution. Gao said local deployment could benefit government, financial and industrial customers requiring data security, low latency and cost control, and that potential business models include usage-based fees, local-deployment licensing and industry-specific solutions.

Competition is intensifying, with companies and research institutions including OpenAI, Cloudflare, Amazon and the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory introducing related models or research initiatives after the launch of Jev. In a separate article in the International Journal of Surgery, published November 3, 2026, Yuelin Song, Ruizhe Li and Hongyan Guo of Peking University responded to a study by Leng et al on CT deep learning radiomics for predicting staging of epithelial ovarian cancer, which reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.913 in internal validation and 0.882 in external validation. The authors said translating such staging models into surgical tools requires further refinement, arguing that FIGO stage prediction should be distinguished from surgical resectability, since the choice between primary cytoreductive surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy depends on disease distribution, expected completeness of resection and perioperative risk. They called for future models to prioritize clinically actionable outcomes such as complete gross resection, surgical complexity and major postoperative complications, and to integrate primary-tumor radiomics with whole-abdominal disease mapping. They also said prospective studies should compare model-assisted decisions with standard multidisciplinary evaluation using predefined surgical endpoints and external validation, and that the key question is whether AI improves complete cytoreduction rates and perioperative outcomes, not just staging accuracy.

stories.Headline: SK Telecom Q3 Operating Profit Surges Elevenfold, but AI Data Center Revenue Falls 7.4%
stories.Summary:
SK Telecom reported on Nov. 4 that its third-quarter 2026 revenue was 4.4973 trillion won, operating profit was 552.3 billion won and net profit was 411.8 billion won. Revenue rose 13% from a year earlier and operating profit surged 1,040%, partly because last year's figure was low after the April 2025 hacking incident led to customer compensation and service fee discounts. Operating profit was 48.4 billion won in the third quarter of last year and 533.3 billion won in the third quarter of 2024, so this year's figure was about 3.6% higher than before the hacking incident. Compared with the previous quarter, revenue rose 3.2% but operating profit fell 2.4%.

Mobile revenue rose 21% from a year earlier to 2.5697 trillion won, and 5G subscribers reached 18.094 million, up 121,000 from the previous quarter. Average revenue per user rose 0.7% quarter-on-quarter to 29,297 won. Subsidiary SK Broadband posted revenue of 1.1728 trillion won, up 2.6%, and operating profit of 134.7 billion won, up 51%. AI data center revenue rose 6.2% from a year earlier to 126.1 billion won but fell 7.4% from 136.2 billion won in the previous quarter, which the company linked to a revenue gap in its GPU-as-a-service business during a transition to new long-term contracts. AI services for enterprises and consumers brought in 70 billion won, up 27% from a year earlier and 14% from the previous quarter, and combined AI data center and AI service revenue was 196.1 billion won, up 12% from a year earlier but down 0.7% from 197.5 billion won in the previous quarter.

SK Telecom set up SK Hyper in July to develop its AI data center business and in August announced plans to separate SK Broadband's data center and submarine cable businesses into a new company, SK Horizon. It signed agreements to secure 3.08 trillion won in investment for SK Horizon from KKR and a consortium of IMM Investment and Stonebridge, and aims to complete the separation and establish the new entity in the first quarter of 2027. During the quarter, SK Telecom and SK Broadband spent 461.4 billion won on capital expenditure, and an additional 148.6 billion won went to SK Hyper's data center business development, for a combined 610 billion won. The company plans to expand data center capacity from 137 megawatts to more than 318 megawatts after 2030 by building new data centers in Ulsan, the Seoul metropolitan area and other locations.

LG Uplus said Nov. 4 that its third-quarter revenue fell 0.7% from a year earlier to 3.9813 trillion won, while operating profit rose 84% to 297.6 billion won and net profit rose 272% to 183.1 billion won. The profit jump largely reflected 150 billion won in voluntary retirement costs in the third quarter of 2025 that cut operating profit to 161.7 billion won; excluding those costs, operating profit would have been 311.7 billion won, or 14.1 billion won higher than this year's figure. Consolidated service revenue was 3.1021 trillion won, standalone service revenue rose 0.7% to 2.912 trillion won, and cumulative consolidated service revenue for the first nine months of 2026 rose 1.6% to 9.2156 trillion won. Mobile revenue fell 0.9% to 1.6867 trillion won, while mobile service revenue excluding interconnection revenue rose 0.4% to 1.6232 trillion won.

stories.Headline: TCS: 84 per cent see AI gains, only 10 per cent allow autonomous agents
stories.Summary:
A study by Tata Consultancy Services found that 84 per cent of executives across enterprises identified productivity improvements as the leading benefit of AI investments. However, only 10 per cent of enterprises allow AI agents to execute decisions without human approval across multiple business functions. Just 9 per cent of executives reported that their organisations had AI agents capable of securely orchestrating workflows across enterprise applications. The study, titled Intelligence that is Real, surveyed 1,333 senior business and technology leaders across 25 countries and 12 industries, with organisations whose annual revenues ranged from $500 million to more than $20 billion.

Security, risk and governance emerged as the leading considerations when organisations decide where and how to deploy AI systems, ranking ahead of cost, speed and ease of deployment. About 90 per cent of respondents considered model independence an important factor in AI investment decisions, but only 7 per cent reported having organisation-wide continuity plans to switch AI providers. About 34 per cent of respondents identified AI sovereignty requirements, including control over data location, model choice and regulatory compliance, as a high or very high organisational risk, and in Europe this figure rose to 43 per cent. Thirty-nine per cent of enterprises said they were still assessing whether their AI initiatives generated sufficient value relative to token and compute costs, while 44 per cent said important business knowledge remained embedded in employees' expertise or fragmented documentation.

Amit Kapur, Chief AI and Services Transformation Officer at TCS, said that concerns around security, governance and resilience seemed to be holding organisations back, and he described that as rightly so. He added that deploying AI responsibly, with the right guardrails and enterprise controls, would be the big focus in the next stage of this journey. The articles also note that observability becomes important for monitoring AI agents' actions and decisions as they gain access to enterprise systems. Fidelity International has introduced use-case-level token budgets and an internal AI gateway to monitor expenditure and restrict access, offering an example of how organisations are addressing AI cost and model access concerns.

Legacy systems, fragmented data and integration gaps are emerging as obstacles to scaling AI deployments, and a recent assessment of Indian enterprises highlighted infrastructure challenges in moving AI workloads into production. Organisations are assessing whether their existing infrastructure can support AI at scale. Another 46 per cent of respondents reported deploying open-source AI for selected use cases. The proportion of leaders who said it was too early to determine AI's effect on jobs rose from 4 per cent in 2024 to 19 per cent in 2026, while North America showed particular strength across several enterprise AI foundations, with 15 per cent of respondents treating AI as a strategic enterprise capability.

stories.Headline: Kakao Mobility, South Korean Army to Develop AI-Based Control System for Unmanned Assets
stories.Summary:
Kakao Mobility signed a memorandum of understanding with the Republic of Korea Army on November 3, 2026, at Army Headquarters in Gyeryong, South Chungcheong Province. The agreement covers cooperation on advanced technologies, including integrated control systems for manned-unmanned combined combat operations. Kakao Mobility CEO Ryu Geung-seon and Army Headquarters Policy Director Maj. Gen. Lee Kyung-jin attended the signing.

The company announced the agreement on November 3, and the Seoul Economic Daily reported it on November 4. The partnership is linked to the Army's Army TIGER+ initiative, which aims to bring civilian AI technologies into military operations. The two sides plan to combine Kakao Mobility's platform management expertise with Army operational data to research and test AI-based control systems for defense. The central goal is a single system that can operate multiple types of unmanned vehicles, supporting a one-to-many model in which one operator manages several unmanned systems. Over the longer term, they aim to lay the foundation for a defense mobility operating system that can coordinate drones, robots and other unmanned assets on the battlefield.

They will also establish testing environments around the Army's AI Transformation hubs in Pangyo and Daejeon, and the partnership covers military dispatch systems and dedicated applications. Ryu said Kakao Mobility would support innovation in future combat systems based on its technology and help the Army secure world-class competitiveness in defense physical AI. He said the results of research and demonstrations with the Army would feed back into private-sector technology, creating a cycle in which the military and the domestic physical AI ecosystem grow together. Lee said that on future battlefields what matters is a physical AI platform that analyzes a wide range of field data and connects AI judgments to the actual operation of moving vehicles. He said applying Kakao Mobility's technology to defense would upgrade future combat systems and secure technological sovereignty in defense AI.

Kakao Mobility has been expanding into defense AI, signing an MOU with Korea University's C5ISRT Convergence Research Institute on October 6. It entered the robotics control business in 2024 with its robot delivery service BRING, began late-night autonomous driving in Seoul's Gangnam district in March 2026, and increased its operating vehicles to six from two in August. The Army conducted the Army TIGER+ Future Warfare Integrated Combat Exercise on October 14 at the Yangpyeong Comprehensive Training Center in Gyeonggi Province, demonstrating reconnaissance drones, loitering attack drones, multipurpose unmanned ground vehicles and quadruped robots. The Army aims to expand manned-unmanned combined combat systems across all units by 2040.

stories.Headline: 1 in 15 adults experience AI-generated image-based abuse: study - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
A study led by RMIT University in Australia found that around one in 15 adults in Australia, Britain and the United States has experienced AI-generated image-based abuse. The survey of more than 7,200 adults found that 7 percent had experienced at least one form of such abuse since turning 18, with the rate slightly higher in Australia at 7.7 percent. The abuse included having intimate images created or altered using AI without consent, having AI-generated intimate images shared without consent, or being threatened with their release. Almost 87 percent of victim-survivors reported at least one impact on their lives, including effects on their health and well-being, relationships, work or finances. The findings were published in the International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction.

The study found that men reported experiencing the abuse at more than twice the rate of women, at 10.2 percent compared with 3.8 percent. However, women reported more negative reactions and impacts, including fear for their safety and effects on their mental and physical health. Higher rates were also reported by people under 35, people from racial and ethnic minority backgrounds, and people with disability. Lead author Professor Nicola Henry from RMIT said the findings revealed the extent of the abuse across the wider community, not just celebrities and public figures. She said the true scale may be even greater because some people may never know that AI-generated images of them have been created or shared.

Henry said the findings strengthened the case for greater responsibility on technology companies to prevent AI-generated image-based abuse before it occurs. She said Australia's proposed digital duty of care is an opportunity to shift the focus from responding to abuse after it happens to requiring online services to prevent foreseeable harm. She added that regulation and new laws are not enough, and that better education, accessible support for victim-survivors, and greater responsibility on technology companies and developers are also needed. Co-author Dr Rebecca Umbach, a staff user experience researcher at Google, said understanding who is experiencing this abuse, how it occurs and its impacts is essential for designing more effective prevention and responses. The research program was funded by Google.

The findings build on two earlier studies using the same international dataset. One earlier study found that 3.2 percent of respondents reported creating, sharing or threatening to share AI-generated sexual images without consent, and among those who shared the material the most commonly reported motivation was for fun or as a joke. Another study found that almost one in five adults had deliberately viewed AI-generated sexual images of real people, excluding those who did so solely to report or remove the material. Henry said that as generative AI becomes more widely available, there is greater potential for these tools to be misused, and that what is not yet known is how quickly that is translating into increased victimization. The international team is continuing its work to better understand and prevent AI-generated image-based abuse.

stories.Headline: Nigeria: Voter Audit - Ai and Electoral Integrity
stories.Summary:
Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission, known as INEC, announced that it has integrated AI-driven Automated Biometric Identification Systems and facial recognition tools to audit the country's voter register, which now exceeds 103 million citizens. The announcement was reported by Leadership (Abuja) on 4 November 2026. The register is the primary pillar upon which election credibility rests, and the audit is meant to purge double registrations, ghost entries and underage voters. The article said the shift raises concerns about algorithmic transparency, data privacy, cybersecurity and automated voter suppression.

The article said the potential fallout carries unique risks for Northern Nigeria, which accounts for a substantial share of the national electorate. In rural Northern communities, millions of legitimate voters, including rural women, Internally Displaced Persons lacking updated identification and manual laborers, bear physical signatures of environmental exposure that can alter facial features or degrade fingerprint ridges. If low-resolution capture hardware or rigid AI algorithms misread these natural variations as fraudulent, hundreds of thousands of valid voters could be quietly de-listed. The article called for complete algorithmic transparency, independent technical audits, strict human oversight and accessible physical verification before any voter is removed.

The article insisted that INEC leadership must establish clear governance frameworks so technology serves the voter rather than penalizing the vulnerable. It said INEC should publish a clear operational framework detailing the parameters its tools use to flag discrepancies, and give independent cybersecurity experts, political party representatives and civil society organizations access to audit the system's logic. Flagged individuals must get clear notice, physical verification at local government electoral offices and a straightforward administrative appeal process. INEC must also deploy countermeasures against AI-generated deepfakes, manipulated media and cyber intrusion into voter databases.

Separately, a former INEC chairman, Prof. Attahiru Jega, called for proactive safeguards at a National Summit on Artificial Intelligence, Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference and Electoral Information Integrity in Abuja, chaired by him under the theme "Beyond the Ballot." He warned that AI carries severe negative uses that could undermine election integrity, and recommended that election bodies in Africa consider AI-driven chatbots powered by officially verified data. The current INEC chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, said the integrity of the 2027 ballot will depend largely on the authenticity of the information environment, and called for a trusted, coordinated and rights-respecting operational ecosystem. The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, said the integrity of the 2027 elections is a shared responsibility, citing the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy published in 2024 and the amended Electoral Act 2026, signed on Feb. 18, which provides for mandatory electronic transmission of polling unit results.

stories.Headline: Claude Lowers ChatGPT’s Lead in $1.4 Billion UK Consumer AI Market
stories.Summary:
Adobe said on Nov. 4 that its CX Enterprise Coworker, an agentic teammate for customer experience orchestration, is now available inside ChatGPT, Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business and Microsoft Copilot. Adobe expects to add it to Amazon Quick, IBM and Snowflake soon. The tool lets marketing professionals use it within the agentic AI platforms of their choice. It provides data analysis and insights, enables audience forecasting, optimizes customer journeys, and improves planning, product and work management. Adobe also launched connectors offering prebuilt Model Context Protocol server integrations with partners including Amazon Ads, Databricks Genie, Demandbase, a Meta ads MCP server, Microsoft Work IQ, RainFocus and Snowflake Cortex AI, so marketers can connect to these systems without custom integration work.

On Nov. 3, ChatGPT consumer product lead Adam Fry said at an OpenAI dinner in New York City that ChatGPT went from 1 billion to 1.2 billion weekly active users in 60 days, adding 200 million users in two months. He said ChatGPT's search-like query volume is roughly one-fifth of Google's, that users create 1.5 billion images per week, and that voice mode has 250 million combined weekly active users. Fry said every question that triggers a web search counts as a search, and that voice is still only about 20% of the user base. He also said OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work modes, so the toggle at the top will go away.

Anjul Bhambhri, Adobe's senior vice president of engineering for customer experience orchestration, said marketers often use AI tools in isolation without the organizational context and domain intelligence needed to personalize every stage of the customer lifecycle. She said CX Enterprise Coworker connects these tools and workflows using brand, customer and channel intelligence to help teams drive better business outcomes. Fry said the growth is going big and that OpenAI is staying focused on how fast ChatGPT is growing. He said Dots, the personal assistant launched Sept. 29, is on the compute-heavier side and OpenAI wants to dial that back over time, and that there is nothing to share yet on when Dots will reach a broader set of users.

Adobe is working with global systems integrators including Accenture, Capgemini, Cognizant, Deloitte Digital, EY, IBM, Infosys, PwC and TCS to create agentic solutions tailored to specific industries. Adobe executives said in December they expected growth to be driven in part by rapid adoption of its AI-powered tools, and in April Adobe said it was enhancing its marketing solutions with an agentic AI system, an AI-powered coworker and expanded collaborations with AI platforms. A PYMNTS Intelligence report found that 60% of media and advertising firms have adopted AI for tasks such as board and executive briefing preparation, quality assurance and call analysis, and returns and reverse-logistics optimization. Fry said OpenAI's goal is to bring intelligence to everyone safely across the world, and that it will work on more efficient agentic models and on how much a Dot messages users, with the ambition of bringing Dots to all users.

stories.Headline: The week in AI-native telco (24-30 Oct 2026)
stories.Summary:
Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company, the sovereign wealth fund of Bahrain, and ARP Group partnered to establish an AI-native and blockchain enabled wholesale bank headquartered in Bahrain, according to an announcement made on the sidelines of Gateway Gulf 2026 and reported on November 2, 2026. ARP Group is the holding company of ARP Global Capital and ARP Digital, the latter co-founded by Yusuf Alireza alongside Abdulla and Abdulaziz Kanoo. The venture has received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of Bahrain and will commence regulated activities only after obtaining final authorisation. The proposed bank is intended to serve regulated financial institutions, payment companies and businesses with cross-border operations.

The bank is being designed to use artificial intelligence across its operations and to offer programmable services that connect directly with clients' systems through APIs, supported by human oversight, governance and risk controls. Products and services would be introduced in phases, informed by engagement with prospective clients. The partnership combines Mumtalakat's long-term investment approach with ARP's experience in institutional finance and digital financial infrastructure. The bank aims to simplify banking for clients whose needs span multiple markets and currencies, using technology to reduce the complexity and cost of serving them.

Shaikh Abdulla bin Khalifa Al Khalifa, Chief Executive Officer of Mumtalakat, said financial services have long been a cornerstone of Bahrain's economy and that the fund invests in opportunities that strengthen the sector's competitiveness. He said the partnership brings together an experienced institutional team with Bahrain's regulatory and business environment, and that the investment reflects a commitment to long-term value, opportunities for Bahraini talent and sustainable returns. Yusuf Alireza, Chairman of ARP Group, said institutional clients with complex cross-border needs still face fragmented banking services. He said the venture combines a regulated bank's balance sheet and institutional relationships with blockchain enabled technology and AI designed into the operating model from the outset, and that Bahrain's financial sector and regulatory experience provide a strong foundation.

In the same week's AI-native telco news, Swisscom CTIO Mark Düsener said at Ericsson's OSS/BSS Summit in Zurich that operators must simplify their architecture before realising the full potential of AI. He said Swisscom began a transformation programme around six years ago, when it had 15 disparate IP networks, and is converging towards a single IP network, with the final stage scheduled for completion in March 2027. Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison reported AI cloud revenues of $50m for the first nine months of 2026 and expects full year AI cloud service revenues to hit $100m, compared with $28m for the whole of 2025, with contracted revenues worth more than $300m for 2027. O2, part of Virgin Media O2, partnered with Nokia to deploy what it claims is the UK's first live trial of AI-RAN, at a Giga Site in London Paddington, where the trial boosted spectral efficiency by 20%.

stories.Headline: AMD's OpenAI, Meta chip deals trigger $1B Q3 charge
stories.Summary:
AMD recorded a $1.07 billion non-cash charge, or 66 cents a share, in the third quarter ended Sept. 26 to account for warrants tied to its chip deals with OpenAI and Meta Platforms. The charge was disclosed on Tuesday as shipments under the agreements begin to ramp up. AMD in February agreed to sell up to $60 billion worth of AI chips to Meta over five years, giving the Facebook owner warrants that could let it buy as much as 10 percent of the chip firm if it meets certain milestones. The deal followed a similar agreement with OpenAI last year, giving the startup the option to buy up to roughly 10 percent of the chipmaker.

The warrants could let OpenAI and Meta own a large stake in AMD for as little as a penny apiece if they fully vest and are exercised, potentially increasing AMD's share count substantially. The warrants' ultimate value depends on AMD's share price when they are exercised, and OpenAI's warrant also includes AMD share-price thresholds, while Meta's does not. AMD finance chief Jean Hu said on Tuesday's analyst call that the warrants would begin diluting AMD shareholders once OpenAI and Meta satisfy the vesting and exercise conditions, which include shipment and other commercial requirements. She said AMD expects to provide more guidance in 2027 on when those conditions could be met.

AMD forecast faster-than-expected 2027 growth, thanks to surging data-center sales, sending its shares up 8 percent in extended trading and pushing up stocks of Intel, Nvidia and Broadcom. TECHnalysis Research Chief Analyst Bob O'Donnell said he believes incentives played a role in some of AMD's sales, but the bigger issue is pent-up demand for a serious alternative to Nvidia, and AMD's products are now starting to compete on price and performance. Analysts said the deals were a major vote of confidence in AMD's AI chips and software but are unlikely to dent Nvidia's dominance, as the market leader continues to sell every AI chip it can make. AMD has also struck a chip-purchase arrangement with OpenAI rival Anthropic, but that agreement included a commitment by AMD to invest in Anthropic.

Other AI chip and infrastructure companies have struck similar equity-linked deals with major customers. Chip startup Cerebras granted OpenAI warrants against a $20 billion commitment, while Marvell has issued Alphabet's Google warrants that give the search giant the right to buy a potential $12.2 billion stake. Qualcomm gave Amazon warrants in a $60 billion deal for its AI data-center chips. The warrants are part of a growing use of equity incentives by chip and AI cloud companies to secure massive, long-term purchases from a small group of AI customers, and highlight the circular nature of the AI boom, where companies can simultaneously be customers, suppliers and investors in one another.

stories.Headline: AI's Next Agritech Frontier Is India's Fragmented Supply Chain
stories.Summary:
India's agritech companies have built tools for crop monitoring, pest detection and yield prediction, but the bigger challenge is linking farm-level intelligence to the supply chain that decides where produce goes, how it is priced and who captures its value. Produce passes through farmers, aggregators, warehouses, traders, processors and retailers, with information often recorded separately at each stage. A 2022 study by NABARD Consultancy Services, covering 54 agricultural commodities across 292 districts, estimated losses of 6 to 15 percent for fruits and 5 to 12 percent for vegetables between 2020 and 2022. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare reported creating more than 10.31 crore Farmer IDs under the Digital Agriculture Mission as of August 3, 2026. APEDA's HortiNet system supports certification and traceability for selected horticultural exports, including grapes, pomegranates and mangoes.

The article says AI could help businesses forecast availability, plan procurement and assess demand, but only with reliable data across a fragmented chain. It notes that Farmer IDs structure farmer information but do not capture every transaction, quality check or movement of produce. ONO, an agricultural market digitisation platform, says it has captured more than three seasons of market data and claims price, arrival, supply and demand predictions with over 90 percent accuracy, a company-reported figure whose methodology the article says is not established. The article adds that traceability depends on accurate records at each handover, and that satellite imagery and AI can flag inconsistencies but cannot reconstruct an undocumented journey.

Krishna Kumar, founder and CEO of Cropin, said the problem is less a complete absence of data than its fragmentation, since farmers, FPOs, mandis, aggregators, logistics firms, processors and retailers use different recordkeeping methods, languages, applications and systems, and requiring everyone to adopt one application is unlikely to succeed. Rama Kancharapu, founder, CEO and CPO of ONO, said the real damage is that data sits in the private books of fragmented players, and that an integrated solution creating value at every handshake is what makes adoption natural. Shubham Jhuria of Aeravti Ventures said data has not been a very economically viable model because there is no access to it. Kumar also cautioned that AI and satellite intelligence cannot on their own reconstruct an undocumented physical journey or prove every custody transfer.

The article says the government is building digital infrastructure for agriculture while agritech companies explore how market data can inform commercial decisions. Kancharapu expects further applications in price prediction, supply-demand intelligence and fraud prevention over the next three to five years. The article says the larger question is whether improvements reach farmers, since outcomes depend on realised prices, input costs, rejection rates and selling terms, and benefits may not reach growers if connected data mainly helps larger businesses cut costs. It says common data standards, shared identifiers and connections between existing platforms could help, but the cost of maintaining records, data-access terms and how commercial benefits are distributed will shape whether these systems gain traction.

stories.Headline: Megazone Cloud, KAIST Partner to Standardize Physical AI
stories.Summary:
Megazone Cloud signed a memorandum of understanding with KAIST's Manufacturing Physical AI Research Institute to cooperate on physical AI, the company said on the 4th, with the signing held at COEX in Seoul on the 2nd. The agreement was signed by Megazone Cloud Chairman Lee Joo-wan and Jang Young-jae, head of the institute. The two sides will pursue technical standardization among companies in robot components, equipment, AI and data, and will develop joint business models. The aim is to let robots, manufacturing equipment and data systems that differ from company to company be linked together.

Under the agreement, Megazone Cloud will use its AI and cloud deployment and operation capabilities to apply KAIROS 37, a robot orchestration platform developed by KAIST, at industrial sites. Robot orchestration connects other robots and systems on one platform and distributes and manages tasks. The two sides will form a working-level consultative body to identify applicable industrial fields and cooperation projects and to define the role of each participating company. They plan to build a framework that runs from technology verification to commercialization and entry into overseas markets. KAIST plans to expand the pool of participating companies and link each company's robot, AI and manufacturing system technologies with KAIROS 37 to enter global markets with integrated solutions.

Lee Joo-wan, chairman of Megazone Cloud, said the company would combine its industrial field experience from work with more than 8,000 companies and the AI and AX capabilities of its roughly 2,800 employees to support physical AI technology in taking root at industrial sites and creating real value. The agreement is part of efforts to build a standardization cooperation framework being pursued by the governance subcommittee of the Ministry of Science and ICT's Physical AI Alliance. The subcommittee is tasked with resolving connectivity issues among the different robot, equipment and data environments at each company and supporting overseas expansion of technologies and business models validated in South Korea. The private-led alliance involves companies, universities and research institutes from technology development to industrial site application and ecosystem construction.
