stories.Headline: Nvidia Shares Rise as Chip Results Point to Resilient AI Demand
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares rose on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after recent upbeat results from leading chip companies suggested that concerns about data-center construction delays had not yet affected Nvidia and other hardware firms. Customers continued stockpiling AI hardware despite uncertainty over where suitable installation sites would be available. The positive results from leading chip companies indicated that construction delays had not immediately hit Nvidia or other hardware makers. The market remains focused on signs of strong chip demand following Nvidia's recent weak performance.

U.S. election results pointed to stricter review of AI infrastructure projects. Republican governors in Texas and Ohio lost their elections, meaning AI infrastructure projects will face stricter review. Nvidia would face a greater challenge if Democratic officials pursue strict limits on data-center construction. The article gives no dates for the elections beyond the Nov. 4, 2026 report.

The article does not name the officials responsible or include any statements from them. It does not say who said what about the results or about Nvidia. It reports only that the election outcomes point to stricter project review. No comments from Nvidia or from Democratic officials are included.

The context is uncertainty over where suitable installation sites for AI hardware would be available. Customers kept stockpiling AI hardware despite that uncertainty. The article does not say what happens next beyond the market watching for signs of strong chip demand. It does not give further details on future reviews or limits.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Shares Rise as Chip Results Point to Resilient AI Demand

stories.Headline: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit
stories.Summary:
Check Point Research disclosed on November 4, 2026, details of an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle called Haiou, which means Seagull in Chinese. The bundle modifies Codex configuration files so that later agent responses carry advertisements for the author's website. Check Point Research named the phenomenon prompt adware. The report said the bundle uses prompt injection techniques such as role-playing and reframing security requests as a Capture The Flag scenario.

The bundle pushes ads for zz.aiapi2025[.]top when users type greetings or activation words like "Seagull," "hi," "hello," "hey," "yo," and "are you there?" It also installs security-focused skills for penetration testing, cracking, and reverse engineering. On GitHub, haiou-codex is described as a local enhancement configuration package that adds a Chinese technical personality and security research workflow to Codex. The repository was made available on July 10, 2026, and has been forked 77 times and starred 403 times.

The jailbreak has also been bundled within Codex-X, an open-source Chinese visualization tool for configuring Codex through a graphical user interface. Pedro Drimel Neto, malware analysis team leader at Check Point, said the behavior comes through natural-language instructions and configuration rather than a traditional executable payload that users and security teams might more readily recognize as software behavior. He said that while serving an ad may seem relatively harmless, the findings show how a bad actor could introduce undesirable behavior through third-party skills or configurations, leading to supply chain attacks. He also said that as AI agents become part of enterprise environments, the prompts, skills, and third-party components influencing their behavior become part of the trust chain too.

Check Point Research said the likely business model is to use the freely distributed jailbreak bundle as an acquisition channel for the paid gateway service. Codex is not officially available in mainland China, which suggests the service is likely aimed at individuals or organizations wanting to try Western AI coding assistants. The advertised service is an opaque, OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway, a middleware between an application and an LLM provider. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit

stories.Headline: Mercy University Selected For Nearly $3M Grant To Boost Career, AI Skill
stories.Summary:
Mercy University has been selected for a federal grant expected to provide nearly $3 million over five years, according to Daily Voice. The money comes through the U.S. Department of Education's Title III Part A Strengthening Institutions Program. The university will receive $614,939 in the first year, with total funding expected to reach $2,999,946. The grant is meant to improve student success, strengthen career preparation and expand artificial intelligence training.

The funding will support a five-year initiative called FORWARD, which stands for Future-Oriented Readiness through Workforce-Aligned, AI-Enhanced Redesign and Development. The program aims to help more low-income students complete their degrees and prepare for careers. It will focus on three areas: faculty development, hands-on learning and AI integration. Faculty will receive training to revise courses around career skills and workplace needs, and a new Solutions Lab will let students tackle business challenges alongside employers. Students and faculty will also receive AI training to help them develop skills for an evolving workforce.

Dr. Stuart Sidle will oversee the initiative as project director. According to the university, he said artificial intelligence is reshaping the workforce landscape and Mercy is taking proactive steps so students develop the skills and experiences they need to enter and advance in their chosen careers. He said FORWARD will invest in faculty, expand opportunities for students to solve authentic problems and build the AI literacy needed to thrive in a rapidly changing workplace. Dr. Leigh M. Tolley will lead faculty training, Dr. Kafui Kouakou will oversee the Solutions Lab, and Eldrid Sequeira will direct AI integration efforts.

Articles.Title: Mercy University Selected For Nearly $3M Grant To Boost Career, AI Skill

stories.Headline: Anthropic CEO wins copyright reprieve as US judge doubts music publishers' claims
stories.Summary:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei won a preliminary victory on Tuesday when a federal judge dismissed music publishers' direct copyright infringement claim against him. The ruling came from US District Judge Eumi K. Lee in Silicon Valley. Lee gave the publishers another chance to amend their allegations. The judge also questioned whether the publishers had provided enough evidence to proceed.

The publishers claim that Anthropic's large language model Claude generated infringing lyrics from more than 20,000 copyrighted compositions. Lee expressed skepticism about that claim and deferred ruling on it. She also deferred ruling on allegations that Anthropic unlawfully removed copyright management information. Both sides have until next Wednesday to propose how the case should proceed.

Lee is responsible for the ruling, and she dismissed the direct claim against Amodei for now while allowing the publishers to amend. The articles do not say what Amodei himself said about the decision. The publishers' claims center on Claude and the more than 20,000 compositions. The judge doubted the evidence they had offered so far.

The case is a copyright dispute over whether Anthropic's model produced infringing lyrics and whether the company removed copyright management information. The articles do not give further context beyond the ruling and the deadlines. Both sides must submit proposals by next Wednesday on how the case should move forward. The publishers may amend their allegations against Amodei.

Articles.Title: Anthropic CEO wins copyright reprieve as US judge doubts music publishers' claims

stories.Headline: AI doesn’t create new cyber threats – it just makes the old ones unstoppable
stories.Summary:
Ivan Khamenka, a cyber threat intelligence analyst at Netcraft, wrote a commentary published by SC Media on November 4, 2026. He argued that AI has not created new kinds of cyber attacks but has made existing ones faster, easier and wider in reach. AI has democratized cybercrime by putting sophisticated tools in the hands of almost anyone who wants them, from AI-assisted phishing kits to more convincing impersonation and deepfake attacks. As a result, people no longer need to be skilled hackers to commit crime and fraud.

The article says this lowered barrier to entry means attack volumes are surging and defenders must change their strategy. Khamenka expects many more and more realistic deepfake attacks, including fraudulent Microsoft Teams meetings where the victim thinks they are talking to someone they know. He also warns that insider threats will become much more believable and that identity fraud attacks may rise, since making a real-looking passport and other official documents has become easy. He notes that tools can duplicate any streaming service's page, and that legitimate platforms let anyone build professional-looking websites with HTTPS certificates in minutes, which criminals use for fake cryptocurrency scam sites and for impersonating well-known sites like Booking.com.

Khamenka lays out three steps for IT teams. First, they should prioritize attacks by scale and exploitability rather than novelty, asking which attacks can hit thousands or millions of targets at once and which have become accessible to less-skilled criminals. Second, they should focus on protecting people and identities, not just infrastructure, by reducing the consequences of inevitable human mistakes instead of assuming users will catch every scam. Third, they should use external threat intelligence to learn who is targeting the company before an attack, because organizations will not be able to investigate every alert as volume grows.

The context is that AI is changing cybercrime in speed, scale and accessibility rather than in sophistication. Khamenka says defenders should pay attention to how exploitable attacks are and how much damage they can do, rather than just the newest threats. They should also mitigate the exploitability of people and identities within their organization and use threat intelligence for a more holistic view. The article does not say what happens next beyond these recommendations.

Articles.Title: AI doesn’t create new cyber threats – it just makes the old ones unstoppable

stories.Headline: Could a New US-Iran War Derail Trump’s Artificial Intelligence Boom?
stories.Summary:
A renewed US military campaign against Iran could undermine President Donald Trump's priority of keeping America ahead in artificial intelligence, according to a Modern Diplomacy article published on November 4, 2026. The administration has said it could resume military action against Tehran if diplomatic efforts fail to secure a new ceasefire. Fears of further fighting, another effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz or attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure had already pushed Brent crude above $115 a barrel, a level last seen in March. Prices later fell on optimism about a diplomatic resolution and reports that Washington would reduce military aid to Israel.

The article says a prolonged period of high oil prices would complicate decisions for the Federal Reserve and other central banks. If crude falls below $100 a barrel, it says, favourable comparisons with the high prices recorded after the Iran war began in the second quarter of 2026 could help reduce headline inflation in 2027. If oil stays near recent highs or rises further, energy costs could feed into broader inflation, delaying expected interest-rate cuts or forcing central banks to consider tighter policy. The AI industry depends on huge upfront spending on chips, electricity infrastructure, land and data-centre construction, and the article says Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta and Microsoft have faced growing pressure on cash generation as investment commitments expand.

The article says smaller "neocloud" companies that supply GPU computing capacity face greater risk because they lack diversified revenue and large cash reserves. It cites CoreWeave, where borrowing costs are already above 15%, making further data-centre projects harder to justify economically. It describes a possible negative feedback loop in which higher financing costs reinforce doubts about AI profitability, forcing companies to delay or scale back projects. The article says the outcome is not inevitable and depends on sustained escalation in the Middle East, continued disruption risks to energy supplies and a strong monetary policy response. It says a diplomatic agreement, stable oil markets or central banks looking through a temporary inflation shock could limit the damage.

Articles.Title: Could a New US-Iran War Derail Trump’s Artificial Intelligence Boom?

stories.Headline: Microsoft, Nvidia launch AI support scheme in UK and Ireland
stories.Summary:
Microsoft and Nvidia launched a support programme called Frontier Launchpad for software companies in the UK and Ireland that work with AI. Applications opened on 4 November 2026 for companies with established software products that are investing in AI or building products that use it. The programme builds on the previous year's Agentic Launchpad and aims to help businesses turn AI products into sustainable operations. Selected participants will get technical support from Microsoft and Nvidia experts, commercial advice, and chances to connect with possible customers and partners.

Applications close on 27 November, and the first Frontier Launchpad cohort starts in early 2027. Eligibility is limited to software companies based in the UK or Ireland with products already available to customers, that are investing in or using AI, and that want greater market reach or expansion. Participants will have access to Microsoft AI specialists, Microsoft Marketplace advisers, cloud architects, and Nvidia technical experts. The programme offers guidance on preparing products for the Microsoft Marketplace and on co-selling, and it has two industry pathways, one for AI platforms and software and another for financial services and financial technology.

Companies will also be supported in exploring international markets through Microsoft's global partner network and commercial channels. Microsoft UK and Ireland CEO Darren Hardman said the UK and Ireland are home to some of the world's most innovative software companies. He said the programme brings together Microsoft's AI capabilities, Nvidia's technology leadership, and a powerful network to help software companies develop new products, grow faster, and create the next generation of businesses using AI. Nvidia Europe, Middle East, Africa and India start-ups director Tobias Halloran said the UK and Ireland have a deep pool of talent building with AI.

He said Nvidia Inception and the Nvidia Deep Learning Institute will give these companies access to Nvidia's technical expertise and training to help them build and accelerate their AI applications. The articles also give recent Microsoft results for the quarter ending 30 September 2026, with net income up 32% to $36.6bn and revenue of $92.3bn, a year-on-year rise of 19%. Operating income rose 21% to $45.9bn. The articles do not say what happens after the first cohort starts beyond the support described.

Articles.Title: Microsoft, Nvidia launch AI support scheme in UK and Ireland

stories.Headline: Sources: Nvidia verbally told cloud compute clients to sell 51%+ of their services to non-Chinese companies, imposing new limits on China's access to AI chips (Financial Times)
stories.Summary:
Nvidia verbally told its cloud compute clients to sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies, according to sources cited by the Financial Times. The instruction was reported on November 3, 2026, and imposes new limits on China's access to AI chips. The report describes the guidance as verbal rather than written. The article does not name the clients involved.

The requirement sets a threshold of 51% or more of services to be sold to non-Chinese companies. It applies to Nvidia's cloud compute clients and adds new limits on China's access to AI chips. The report gives no further figures beyond the 51% share. The date given for the report is November 3, 2026.

The sources cited are unnamed, and the article does not say who at Nvidia gave the instruction. No statement from Nvidia or from any client is included in the article. The report attributes the guidance to sources rather than to an on-the-record comment. No named person is quoted.

The article is behind a subscription paywall, so the full text is not available. Beyond the reported instruction and its 51% threshold, the article does not say what happens next. It does not describe any response from Chinese companies or from Nvidia. More to follow.

stories.Headline: NCSI Releases Results of National Poll on Artificial Intelligence - Fana News
stories.Summary:
Oman's National Centre for Statistics and Information released the results of a survey on public opinion towards artificial intelligence, according to a report issued in October 2026. The centre said around 43% of Omanis have used or interacted with AI tools and applications. Among those users, 95% said the technologies helped them in daily life or let them do tasks more effectively. The survey was published by Fana News on 4 November 2026.

The survey found that 60% of Omanis had heard of the term artificial intelligence, while 41% believe the technologies are part of their daily lives even without deliberate choice. About 16% said they had good knowledge of AI tools, 20% moderate knowledge and 22% limited knowledge, while 42% said they had no knowledge. Usage was around 54% among people aged 18 to 29, 47% among those aged 30 to 49 and 14% among people aged 50 and above. Those with qualifications higher than the General Education Diploma had the highest usage rate at around 83%, and the rate was 55% among employed individuals and 63% among government sector employees.

The centre said the survey is part of its efforts to monitor the use of modern technologies, measure public knowledge and awareness, and identify patterns of use, benefits and risks. It said the findings provide statistical indicators that contribute to the development of national policies and initiatives and promote safe, responsible and effective use of AI. The survey targeted Omani citizens aged 18 and above across the governorates, and data was collected from 17 to 25 May 2026 through telephone interviews using the electronic public opinion survey system. The target sample was 2,000 Omani citizens, while the actual number of responses reached 1,793, and statistical weighting was applied to improve representativeness by gender, age group, educational level and governorate.

The results showed that 86% of Omanis believed there was a need for measures to promote the optimal use of artificial intelligence. Practical training on proper use of AI ranked first among the most beneficial measures at 33%, followed by simplified public awareness programmes at 32%, clear legislation and regulations at 19% and official guidelines for safe AI use at 15%. Children and education topped the areas respondents believed should be prioritised when establishing regulations at 40%, followed by government services at 29% and healthcare at 25%. The centre said the findings highlight the importance of balancing the opportunities offered by AI with awareness of its risks and of developing digital skills and responsible AI practices in line with Oman's digital transformation objectives.

Articles.Title: NCSI Releases Results of National Poll on Artificial Intelligence - Fana News -

stories.Headline: Explainable AI framework maps every step of the machine learning workflow
stories.Summary:
A team led by George Paterakis, with Andrea Castellani, George Papoutsoglou, Tobias Rodemann and Ioannis Tsamardinos, published an open-access paper in Artificial Intelligence Review on November 4, 2026. The paper argues that conventional explainable AI methods clarify single outputs but overlook the upstream decisions and downstream quality checks that determine whether an insight can be trusted. The authors respond with a framework called Holistic Explainable Artificial Intelligence, or HXAI. HXAI embeds explanation into every stage of the data-analysis workflow rather than treating it as a bolt-on feature applied after a model has produced an answer.

The framework unifies six components into a single taxonomy: the data, the analysis set-up, the learning process, the model output, the model quality and the communication channel. Each component is aligned with the needs of three audiences: domain experts, data analysts and data scientists. To make the taxonomy operational, the team assembled a question bank of 112 items covering the needs of these user groups across the workflow. The question bank lets any existing explainable AI toolchain be checked to see which questions it answers and which it leaves open. Using this instrument, the authors surveyed contemporary tools and report that the analysis highlights critical coverage gaps.

The authors ground HXAI in theories of human explanation, principles from human-computer interaction and findings from empirical user studies. From this base, HXAI identifies the characteristics that make explanations clear, actionable and cognitively manageable. The taxonomy is intended to reduce terminological ambiguity in a field where terms such as interpretability, explainability and transparency are often used loosely. The authors are explicit that this is not a conventional survey, and they describe the work as melding concepts from multiple disciplines, lessons from real-world projects and a critical synthesis of the literature.

One forward-looking contribution concerns AI agents that embed large language models, which the authors demonstrate can orchestrate diverse explanation techniques and translate technical artifacts into stakeholder-specific narratives. The end-to-end framing is the core claim: trust in an AI result depends on choices made before any model is trained, on how the learning process is conducted, on how output quality is verified, and on how the result is communicated. The practical implication is that organisations deploying AI should evaluate their explanation practices across the full workflow rather than at the model-output stage alone. The paper is published open access, and the version was shared early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research, subject to further edits before the final Version of Record.

Articles.Title: Explainable AI framework maps every step of the machine learning workflow

stories.Headline: Sánchez calls for an Ibero-American response to Artificial Intelligence and demands a common voice against powers that "disregard international legality"
stories.Summary:
Pedro Sánchez called for a joint Ibero-American response to artificial intelligence at the opening of the XXX Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday. The summit runs between Wednesday and Thursday and brings together representatives from 22 countries. Sánchez spoke at the closing of the XVI Ibero-American Business Meeting at the Las Ventas bullring, where he shared a dialogue with the presidents of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic and Bolivia, and with Portugal's prime minister. The event is marked by the absences of Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum, and by the arrival of Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky to meet several leaders.

Sánchez said medium-sized countries need to cooperate on a technological transformation that affects companies and workers. Ministers and digital transformation officials from the region agreed on Tuesday in Madrid to promote an alliance on artificial intelligence, and the document must now go to the summit for adoption by heads of state and government. Its lines of work include cooperation to access quality data, models adapted to Ibero-American languages and needs, and collaboration on computing capacity. The ministerial agreement also stresses rights and freedoms in the use of these tools, and its concrete scope will depend on how commitments are developed and on later decisions by countries, which keep their own national rules and priorities.

Sánchez also raised the climate emergency and youth mobility for training, including an Ibero-American civil protection network for disasters and an educational exchange program inspired by Erasmus. He said the voice of Ibero-America is very necessary at the United Nations and in cooperation spaces, and asked the summit to act against powers that disregard international legality. Felipe VI advocated closer relations between the European Union and Latin America and the Caribbean amid geopolitical fragmentation and trade tensions, and remembered the victims of the Urda train accident. Ten representatives are expected at the highest level, including Sánchez, while other countries will be headed by vice presidents or ministers.

Argentina's Javier Milei and Chile's José Antonio Kast are among those attending Thursday's plenary session. Milei chose not to attend the inauguration at the Teatro Real on Wednesday or the dinner offered by the Kings to the delegations, and he has a meeting scheduled with Vox leader Santiago Abascal. His visit comes after he called Sánchez an unpresentable dictator at an event in Madrid in October, and La Moncloa has ruled out a bilateral meeting between the two for now. At the Cuenca summit in Ecuador in 2024 the countries failed to close a common text, and the Spanish Government and the Ibero-American General Secretariat have since worked to arrive in Madrid with agreements on technology, education and emergency response.

Articles.Title: Sánchez calls for an Ibero-American response to Artificial Intelligence and demands a common voice against powers that "disregard international legality"

stories.Headline: Expedia Says Travelers Plan With AI Agents but Book Direct
stories.Summary:
Expedia said on its third-quarter earnings call that travelers increasingly use AI assistants to plan trips, but bookings through those agents have not caught up. CEO Ariane Gorin said agentic AI is strongest in discovery, while people still prefer to book with a trusted brand where they know they will be taken care of if something goes wrong. She said agent traffic is high intent and does not appear to cut into direct traffic, though the volume is too small to draw conclusions. Third-party data shows Expedia leading in citation share in the U.S., and the company said the economics of these partnerships are still being worked out. Expedia partnered with Google in AI Mode and announced an integration with Meta Muse, which Gorin said was expected to go live in the U.S. during the call.

Muse gets access to Expedia prices and content and can complete a booking or send the traveler to Expedia, and the company is also testing OpenAI’s new ad products. Qantas is the first partner to use Expedia’s new agentic template, which combines its B2B technology, supply and servicing with a customizable layer so a partner can build its own traveler experience. Expedia also rolled out Reserve Now, Pay Later across all of its brands. Gorin said the agentic voice experience on Vrbo resolved over 15% of inbound contacts in its first two months and raised satisfaction scores at a lower cost. She said a small team built an autonomous hotel onboarding agent in less than a quarter, work that once took multiple quarters and many more people.

Conversational agents now sit in the booking flow, including an AI compare agent and a property expert agent that Gorin said push people deeper into the funnel and lead to larger purchases. Travelers who used the new activity agent were twice as likely to book an activity within seven days. Expedia grew gross bookings 11% and revenue 12% in the quarter, and B2B bookings rose 19%. Advertising growth slowed to 7% from 13% the prior quarter, and CFO Derek Andersen said the company is implementing product changes that give advertisers better campaign tools and lay groundwork for AI-enabled ones.

Articles.Title: Expedia Says Travelers Plan With AI Agents but Book Direct

stories.Headline: Microsoft Clarity Helps Merchants Welcome AI Shopping Agents
stories.Summary:
Microsoft introduced three new features for its website and app analytics tool, Clarity, on Wednesday, Nov. 4, the company said in a blog post. The features are designed to help website owners understand how both people and artificial intelligence agents use their sites. One feature, Agentic Analytics, lets owners see what support AI agents do on their site and test whether those agents can complete tasks. It also includes simulation assessments that help owners find problems before customers do. Agentic Analytics is meant to show whether sites are losing customers because agents cannot find a promotion or finish a checkout.

A second feature, added to Brand Agents, helps retailers get their products discovered in Microsoft Copilot, Bing and MSN when shoppers ask Microsoft's AI for recommendations. Merchants can now use it on their website or only in AI experiences. The third feature, Ask Clarity, lets owners ask questions about how people use their site and get answers backed by real session evidence. Ask Clarity is in closed beta for retailers and is initially focused on website behavioral analytics, with AI visibility and advertising data to be added later. Eighty-eight percent of early access users said it taught them something new about their business or website.

Nabil Naghdy, lead product manager for Microsoft Clarity, said the company is grateful for how far Clarity has come and for the millions of sites and apps that use it around the world. He said what started as a way to understand how people use a website is evolving alongside the customer journey itself. A PYMNTS Intelligence report, "Will the 2026 Shopping Season Go Agentic?", found that nearly 132 million Americans have bought something with help from AI. The report found that merchants expect agentic commerce to become a paid sales channel, but many feel they are not prepared to connect with AI platforms or agent networks.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Clarity Helps Merchants Welcome AI Shopping Agents

stories.Headline: MercadoLibre Expands AI War Chest by $30 Million in Q3
stories.Summary:
MercadoLibre increased its investment in artificial intelligence by $30 million quarter over quarter, the company said in a Wednesday letter to shareholders about its third quarter results. The letter was dated Nov. 4, 2026, and the earnings call took place the same Wednesday. Chief Financial Officer Martín de los Santos discussed the spending during that call. The company said its usage of AI grew much faster than its spend. MercadoLibre said it has become more efficient by getting better at choosing the right model for each task and by expanding its use of open-source models.

The company reported returns including revenue uplift, better user experience, cost avoidance and productivity. Its FinTech AI assistant Mago is now holding 19 million conversations per month. AI has helped double the output of the technology teams over the past year and freed up almost 20% of the hours worked by the finance teams. The revenue uplift from AI in search more than offset the cost of the models, and AI in customer service reduced the need for representatives by a multiple. De los Santos said the company continues to see very good results, both consumer-facing and in internal efficiencies.

He said Mago continues to increase engagement with users, with Net Promoter Score improving and more funds coming to Mercado Pago. He said an LLM was included in the search algorithm, and the incremental conversion and click-through rate show the cost of the models is more than compensated by the added revenue. He said all the metrics the company measures are very effective in terms of productivity. More to follow.

Articles.Title: MercadoLibre Expands AI War Chest by $30 Million in Q3

stories.Headline: Google AI lets Canadians buy from Lululemon, Shoppers Drug Mart without leaving app
stories.Summary:
Google announced on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, a partnership that lets Canadians buy from select brands without leaving the Gemini app or Google's AI search mode. The brands in the partnership are Lululemon Athletica Inc., Shoppers Drug Mart, La Maison Simons and some Shopify Inc. merchants. Shoppers can ask Gemini or the AI search tool to find items with specific features, a certain style or colour. They can then buy any options the tools present from partner retailers without exiting the app or search page. A demo showed a person telling Gemini their face is dry, irritated and burns when most moisturizers are applied.

The person asked Gemini to suggest a gentle recovery balm that would heal their skin and could be bought from a local drugstore. Gemini surfaced a balm that could be purchased directly through the app from Shoppers Drug Mart. Google spokesperson Wendy Manton said in an email to The Canadian Press that retailers did not pay to access the feature. She said Google did not pay the merchants for their participation. She also said fees are not exchanged by either side when consumers make purchases using the feature.

Manton said the program does not make items from Lululemon, Shoppers, Simons or the participating Shopify merchants more likely to be surfaced by Google. The partnership comes after other tech firms like OpenAI and Meta introduced features to make checking out through their AI platforms more seamless. Last year, Shopify announced it would start helping its merchants make hundreds of millions of their products instantly discoverable through ChatGPT. The Ottawa-based e-commerce software provider also began integrating Shop Pay, its checkout technology, into AI tools including Muse, Claude Duet, Grok Bot and Instinct.

Articles.Title: Google AI lets Canadians buy from Lululemon, Shoppers Drug Mart without leaving app

stories.Headline: Arista posts record growth as AI networking supercycle accelerates
stories.Summary:
Arista Networks reported record growth in its third quarter, with revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5% year over year, the largest such increase in its history as a public company, CEO and chairperson Jayshree Ullal said on the company's earnings call with Wall Street analysts this week. Ullal said Arista has surpassed 100 Etherlink customers in 2026 and forecast more than 10 gigawatts of deployment across 10 or more types of compute accelerators by the end of 2027. She said the industry is moving from centralized training compute to distributed inference, prefill and decode, which demands more intelligent networking. Five years ago Arista reported $2.9 billion in revenue for all of 2021.

The company said its Autonomous Virtual Assistant lets administrators ask about network conditions and get explanations, recommendations and help diagnosing problems. Co-founder, president and CTO Ken Duda said Arista has kept its CVE count under 100 over the last two decades and has been working with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and others to add AI-enabled security capabilities from frontier models into its software security pipeline. President and COO Todd Nightingale said enterprise growth is driven by customers treating campus and branch networks as mission-critical, and he credited the EOS software's ability to patch with almost no downtime. Arista has a campus revenue target of more than $1.25 billion for the year.

Duda said research and development spending rose by a little more than $130 million year over year in the quarter, which he said was not unusual, with R&D running at about 9% to 11% of revenue. He cited work with Cerebras, Microsoft and Maya on accelerators and software tuning, plus new liquid cooling technology. In March Arista announced the eXtra-dense Pluggable Optics module, offering 12.8Tbps of bandwidth over 64 electrical lanes with an integrated liquid-cooled cold plate for modules drawing more than 400W. Arista said it has gathered about 45 leading optics module suppliers under a multi-source agreement to build and support the module.

Articles.Title: Arista posts record growth as AI networking supercycle accelerates

stories.Headline: Artificial Intelligence Expert #1 AI Speaker Scott Steinberg
stories.Summary:
Scott Steinberg is listed as an artificial intelligence expert, AI influencer, content creator, keynote speaker and consultant for hire in a post dated November 4, 2026, on futuristsspeakers.com. The post says AI is transforming nearly every industry and changing how businesses operate, how people work and how consumers interact with technology. It says the technology is creating new opportunities while challenging traditional business models and ways of working. It says organizations need knowledgeable professionals who can explain the technology, identify opportunities, address challenges and help people understand what comes next.

The post says an AI expert is someone with specialized knowledge of technologies and systems that let computers and machines perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence. It lists areas including generative AI, agentic AI, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, natural language processing, computer vision, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, robotics, large language models, AI agents, conversational AI, autonomous systems, AI ethics and governance, responsible AI, AI cybersecurity, AI strategy and implementation, and the future of artificial intelligence. It says experts may work in technology development, research, consulting, corporate leadership, academia, media, entrepreneurship or professional speaking. It says some build AI systems and applications while others help organizations understand how to use existing AI technologies effectively.

The post says the responsibilities of an AI expert depend on their background and area of specialization. It says some concentrate on technical development while others focus on business strategy, education, communication or organizational transformation. It describes roles including explaining artificial intelligence, analyzing emerging trends, advising businesses on AI strategy, developing AI applications, educating corporate audiences, creating AI-related content, helping organizations navigate AI adoption and providing industry commentary. It says AI keynote speakers are frequently hired for corporate conferences, leadership meetings, technology conferences, innovation summits, sales kickoff meetings and other events.

The post says the best AI keynote speakers make complex topics accessible without oversimplifying the technology. It says they connect emerging developments to real-world examples and help audiences understand both the opportunities and challenges associated with artificial intelligence. It lists popular keynote topics including the future of artificial intelligence, generative AI and the future of business, and the rise of agentic AI. The article ends mid-sentence in the material provided, so the rest of its content is not available.

Articles.Title: Artificial Intelligence Expert #1 AI Speaker Scott Steinberg

stories.Headline: Microsoft's AI PC roadmap shows where Ryzen AI 500 and Intel Nova Lake fit into Windows
stories.Summary:
A slide posted on X on Tuesday by known leaker HXL appears to come from Microsoft and sorts Windows PCs into four AI tiers by memory. The slide is titled "Windows is the home for hybrid intelligence" and lines PCs up along a memory scale from 8GB to beyond 128GB. Chip names appear only underneath, almost like footnotes. The footnotes carry the biggest news, because Ryzen AI 500 and Core Ultra Series 4 both land in the mainstream Copilot+ class.

Microsoft splits its Copilot+ tier into three bands, from quick local questions at 16GB to delegated tasks at 32GB and long-running jobs at 64GB. Core Ultra Series 3 and 4 sit in the first two bands, next to Ryzen AI 400 and 500. A small "CY26-27" label beside the chip list offers a rough timing window. That lines up with leaks pegging Core Ultra Series 4 as Intel's Nova Lake and Ryzen AI 500 as AMD's Zen 6-based Medusa Point, both reportedly due in 2027.

At 64GB the mainstream parts disappear in favor of Ryzen AI Max+ 400, Nvidia's RTX Spark and an unnamed "Core Ultra Next" from Intel. The same trio carries over into the 128GB Builder PC tier, which is meant for building and serving models locally. Past that sits a Supercomputer tier for desk-side machines running frontier models. An 8GB laptop, meanwhile, gets stuck in a plain "Windows PC" tier limited to local context and basic actions, whatever chip it runs, including Microsoft's own 8GB Surface models from June.

None of this is confirmed yet, though the slide's wording does match the hybrid intelligence push Microsoft kicked off last month with the RTX Spark-powered Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft and Qualcomm said in September that they had stopped calling new devices Copilot+ PCs, yet on this slide the label still anchors the biggest tier. On Copilot+ PCs, that push means Copilot will eventually read local files, take actions and tap on-device models. The slide is a reminder to check the RAM before the chip, since a fast NPU alone will not unlock Copilot+ features without at least 16GB of memory, and that extra memory has only gotten pricier this year as AI data centers soak up supply.

Articles.Title: Microsoft's AI PC roadmap shows where Ryzen AI 500 and Intel Nova Lake fit into Windows

stories.Headline: Google joins Microsoft in expanding employee buyouts as AI costs rise - The American Bazaar
stories.Summary:
Google expanded its employee buyout offers to several countries as it faces rising costs and heavy spending on artificial intelligence. The company told Reuters it began offering voluntary exit packages in June to some employees in Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland. A Google spokesperson said some teams introduced a voluntary exit program with severance in 2025, and the company expanded it globally in a few countries in June 2026. Google described the program as an option for employees who no longer feel aligned with its pace or direction. In Switzerland, where Google employs about 5,000 people and runs a major engineering center in Zurich, the program covered several divisions but excluded its DeepMind AI units.

Applications reportedly closed in mid-July, and employees who accepted the offer began leaving in August. Eligible employees were offered one month's salary for every year of service, up to a maximum of 12 months' salary. At least four employees from one team of about 50 reportedly accepted the offer. Employees in Google Cloud and DeepMind were excluded from the buyouts.

Last week, Microsoft offered similar buyouts to about 60,000 employees across the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom. According to Bloomberg News, the program covers eligible employees at participating business units at the vice president level and below, while some groups, including certain data center, sales and marketing employees, are excluded. Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees worldwide as of June 2026, meaning roughly 27% of its workforce could be eligible. Amy Coleman, Microsoft's chief people officer, said the offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support.

She added that the program would give participating business units another way to adjust their workforces to changing business needs. The moves come as rising AI spending weighs on Wall Street and Alphabet's stock performance. Google Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi has repeatedly identified AI and cloud computing as key hiring priorities during quarterly earnings presentations. Although Alphabet's workforce has grown steadily in recent quarters, the company has been shifting resources toward strategic priorities.

Articles.Title: Google joins Microsoft in expanding employee buyouts as AI costs rise - The American Bazaar

stories.Headline: Zillow CEO’s reality check on AI agents: ‘Finding a home isn’t a chore to hand off to a robot’
stories.Summary:
Zillow Group CEO Jeremy Wacksman said on the company’s quarterly earnings call on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, that most people will not want an AI agent to do their house hunting for them. He said people are happy to let AI agents cancel subscriptions and book appointments, but searching for a home is different because the enjoyment is the point. He compared it to watching a movie or playing a game, which no one wants an agent to do for them. He said finding a home is a milestone people want to live themselves, not a chore to hand off to a robot.

The issue matters to Zillow because most of its money comes from the home-buying process, including fees from partner real estate agents and its mortgage lending business. That depends on people browsing Zillow’s listings and connecting with human agents and loan officers, and an AI agent that does the searching could cut Zillow out. Wacksman said Zillow is not yet seeing meaningful traffic from AI platforms, and about 80% of its traffic comes directly to Zillow. The company has integrated with OpenAI and Google’s Gemini and is now working with Anthropic.

Zillow’s AI mode, a conversational search feature, is now available to all signed-in users, and more than 2.5 million people used it from March to September, asking 8.5 million questions. Wacksman made the case in prepared remarks as personal AI agents such as Meta’s Muse, which launched in September and can book travel and make purchases, raise questions for the company. Amazon blocked Muse from shopping on its site less than two weeks after launch, saying it never agreed to let Muse shop there and that the agent does not identify itself. Amazon is also suing Perplexity over the shopping agent in its Comet browser, and a federal appeals court in August overturned an injunction Amazon had won in that case.

Zillow’s Follow Up Boss software for real estate agents is getting AI that spots leads needing attention and recommends next steps, which agents can approve. Engineers at the company are using AI to ship 60% more changes to production than in 2024, Wacksman said. For the third quarter, Zillow’s revenue rose 7% to $724 million, short of its own forecast of $745 million to $760 million, as a sharp rise in mortgage rates slowed home sales. The company posted a $158 million net loss for the quarter, mostly from agreeing to settle a shareholder lawsuit over Zillow Offers, its defunct home-flipping business.

Articles.Title: Zillow CEO’s reality check on AI agents: ‘Finding a home isn’t a chore to hand off to a robot’

stories.Headline: The geopolitical stakes of AI: Why leaders must watch the sovereign AI race
stories.Summary:
Governments including India, Japan, France, Canada and the United Arab Emirates are spending billions of dollars to subsidize sovereign AI, according to researchers at Bain & Company. They are investing heavily in domestic computing infrastructure and in localized AI models trained on regional data and native languages. The article, a sponsored post from HPE and AMD published on November 4, 2026, describes this as a race among nations. It says AI has moved past simple corporate optimization and is now an engine of macroeconomic power.

McKinsey & Company estimates that sovereign AI could represent a market of $600 billion by 2030. A survey of executives, investors and government offices found that 71% see sovereign AI as an existential concern or a strategic imperative for their organizational goals. McKinsey Global Institute research suggests generative AI could generate $2.6 trillion to $4.4 trillion in annual economic value. Gartner says nations establishing a sovereign AI stack will need to invest at least 1% of their GDP in AI infrastructure by 2029.

The article says state leaders are hesitant to trust foreign entities, even close allies, with critical infrastructure assets. It says an adversary could cause catastrophic disruption by knocking external capabilities offline. It also says governments want governance controls that protect rights and uphold regional laws, with local languages and values embedded in the models. For CIOs, it recommends auditing infrastructure interdependencies and evaluating strategic supercomputing partners with a track record of building large-scale systems.

The article says the decisions of global superpowers today will directly affect supply chains, compliance requirements and data architectures tomorrow. It describes the tech landscape as turning into a zero-sum game as multilateral collaboration gives way to unilateral competition. It warns that standardizing on a single global public cloud provider exposes a business to regulatory penalties or abrupt service disruptions if international data laws shift. It adds that managing isolated data silos across countries raises operational complexity and total cost of ownership.

Articles.Title: The geopolitical stakes of AI: Why leaders must watch the sovereign AI race

stories.Headline: South Bend workshop examines AI’s role in housing discrimination
stories.Summary:
The South Bend Human Rights Commission hosted a free workshop on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, about artificial intelligence, housing and civil rights. The event was held because AI is increasingly used to help make housing decisions, which raises concerns about how algorithms could contribute to discrimination. The workshop was reported by WNDU, with a byline from Kennedi Humble. It brought together experts, real estate agents and others to discuss the issue.

The workshop focused on how bias in AI systems could affect people seeking housing. Katrina Lee, executive director of the South Bend Human Rights Commission, said biased information in an AI system could prevent some applicants from securing housing. Experts said bias could affect applicants before they make it through tenant screening, and could also influence people applying for a home loan if the data used is not fair or equitable. Event speaker Breagin Riley said people should ask about the quality of the data, and that if a company cannot say where the data came from or whether it has been updated within the last six months, bias is probably being introduced.

AI-based tenant screening is already used in the rental market. A 2024 survey by TechEquity of more than 1,000 renters and 400 landlords in California found nearly two-thirds of landlords received tenant-screening reports that included an AI-generated score or recommendation. There is no comparable statewide survey showing how many Indiana landlords use similar tools, but experts say concerns about bias and a lack of transparency apply anywhere these tools are used. Real estate agent Tamara Harke, who attended the workshop, said she is embracing AI and learning to use it in her business, including for marketing, and that it is important to make sure everything is in compliance.

Experts said businesses that use third-party AI systems are still responsible for checking the data and reviewing the system's results. Riley and Myra Reid said that even with third parties, businesses have to test the data and make sure it is still compliant, and that they may still be liable for the decisions they make with that data. Advocates say people should know when AI is being used in housing decisions and understand how to challenge a decision they believe is unfair. Lee encouraged anyone who believes their housing rights may have been violated to contact the South Bend Human Rights Commission for help. Humble will discuss the topic further on the next episode of her podcast, "The Data Center Debate," on Monday, Nov. 9, at 8 p.m.

Articles.Title: South Bend workshop examines AI’s role in housing discrimination
