Earlier editions of the Radar tracked the rise of AI in software engineering and the risks of deploying it at scale, and the latest shifts attention to how companies manage those risks as use spreads across development teams and operational settings. The report says many of the changes needed to make AI use sustainable will sit deeper in the technology stack, where models, graphics processing units, storage and networks are managed through a common platform layer. That places part of the challenge with infrastructure and platform teams, not only software developers or data scientists.

Articles.Title: Thoughtworks urges tighter controls as AI agents spread - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Brennan named OpenAI Select Partner to boost AI deployment
stories.Summary:
Brennan has been named an OpenAI Select Partner, joining OpenAI's global partner network, IT Brief Australia reported on 5 November 2026. The appointment is meant to strengthen Brennan's work with businesses and government bodies moving from AI trials to operational use. OpenAI's partner network brings together companies that build, sell and deliver AI services using its models and products. Brennan said the status builds on its investment in AI engineering, including the launch of its Brennan Innovation Foundry.

Under the arrangement, Brennan will work with OpenAI on deployments for organisations seeking to use GPT-6 Astra in business processes, focusing on complex workflows and linking the technology to existing systems and governance requirements. Brennan said that since April, supported by an internal Skills Marketplace, the Foundry has delivered more than 450 innovations, from smaller automations to six larger business systems. Those include a company-wide platform to turn strategy into trackable actions, a product lifecycle management platform, and a new people system replacing an existing SaaS-based human resource information system. Brennan plans further investment in AI engineering, skills development and customer solutions.

Dave Stevens, Founder and Managing Director of Brennan, said the partnership marked a significant step in the company's AI plans. He said the opportunity for customers is to combine OpenAI's frontier technology with Brennan's engineering, integration and managed innovation capability to solve real business problems and get solutions into production. He said too many organisations are still working out how to move beyond AI pilots and experimentation, and the challenge is identifying the right opportunities, integrating solutions into existing operations and delivering measurable business value. He said that is why Brennan created the Foundry, which gives organisations a repeatable way to capture ideas, assess their potential, develop solutions quickly and scale those that deliver results. He said becoming an OpenAI Select Partner reinforces the company's commitment to helping Australian organisations move from discussing AI's potential to delivering on it.

The announcement reflects a broader issue facing large organisations that have explored AI but have yet to integrate it into routine work. Brennan said many customers are still trying to connect AI tools with internal systems, business processes and staff workflows in a way that produces measurable results, and that this has shaped its approach. Rather than treating AI as a separate program, Brennan is concentrating on use cases tied to current business priorities, such as reducing manual work, improving information access and changing how teams complete tasks. The OpenAI designation also gives Brennan a platform to expand AI work across sectors where infrastructure, security and operating requirements differ, combining AI engineering, systems integration and managed services with customers' operational needs.

Articles.Title: Brennan named OpenAI Select Partner to boost AI deployment - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Smartsheet launches AI tool to bridge strategy & work
stories.Summary:
Smartsheet has launched vsActual, an AI-native product for strategic planning and execution that is meant to link enterprise strategy with work across teams and business systems. The company announced the launch in a story dated 5 November 2026. The product is designed to address two common problems in large organisations, work spread across disconnected tools and manual reporting that can delay the detection of budget, schedule and staffing issues. It reads data from systems corporate teams already use, including Oracle, SAP, Workday and Salesforce, as well as Jira and ServiceNow.

The system turns strategy documents held in presentation decks, budget papers and spreadsheets into what Smartsheet calls a living plan. It can model scenarios using budget and capacity data and flag overruns, delays and resource conflicts as they emerge. AI agents in vsActual can gather data, reconcile information from different systems and draft executive summaries, while people stay in charge of decisions and changes to the plan. Behind the product is Smartsheet's Execution Graph, a data model that maps how work connects from tasks and projects through to programmes and strategic goals. Smartsheet says the system is built on 20 years of workflow intelligence drawn from millions of projects and nine petabytes of data.

Rajeev Singh, Chief Executive Officer at Smartsheet, said every company has a strategy and the ones that win are those whose work delivers on it. He said AI has made people faster but pulled work further apart, so leaders find out too late that the plan and reality have split. He described the Execution Graph as holding 20 years of context on how work really gets done and said vsActual puts that context to work. Keith Kirkpatrick, Vice President of Research at The Futurum Group, said AI has exposed a gap many organisations have lived with for years, with strategy in one place and work in dozens of others. Smartsheet cited PMI research that found leaders identified the disconnect between planning and execution as the biggest barrier to reinventing their businesses.

Smartsheet also pointed to interest from existing users of its project and portfolio tools, citing retailer Bealls as one example. Elizabeth Dandola, Senior Director of PMO & QA at Bealls, said Smartsheet provides the foundation for how the retailer manages its project portfolio, aligns resources and drives strategic execution. She said vsActual has the potential to take that value further by bringing long-range planning, budgeting and portfolio management together in a more connected and adaptive way. The launch comes as companies try to apply AI to planning and operations while dealing with fragmented internal data, and VentureBeat Intelligence found that 64% of respondents traced poor AI responses to missing business context. The product marks a further move by Smartsheet beyond task tracking and workflow management into planning, budgeting and portfolio oversight.

Articles.Title: Smartsheet launches AI tool to bridge strategy & work - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Elastic warns attackers abuse trusted AI tools in hacks
stories.Summary:
Elastic has published research showing that attackers are abusing trusted software tools, including AI applications and remote IT products, during live intrusions. The findings focus on software that organisations and employees already view as legitimate, including browser updaters, signed remote monitoring tools and Apple scripting utilities, as well as desktop AI products such as Claude Code and ChatGPT. In observed intrusions, attackers executed commands through Claude Code on Windows and the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS. In one macOS case, a single command read an internal infrastructure document before pulling saved passwords from the user's keychain.

Elastic examined 27 confirmed cases involving information-stealing malware on customer devices, and in 12 of them the initial access method was a so-called ClickFix lure, in which a fake prompt tricks a user into pasting and running a command. One healthcare case showed malware was delivered about 16 seconds after the user responded to the lure. Once a device was infected, the average time between infection and login using stolen details was eight minutes. The study covered confirmed live intrusions and first-party research between April and September 2026. Elastic also confirmed 23 cases in which attackers installed lawful remote administration products for hands-on control, most often ScreenConnect.

Mike Nichols, general manager of security at Elastic, said attackers hiding inside trusted software is not new and that defenders have fought living-off-the-land techniques for decades. He said what is new is that enterprises are increasingly deploying powerful trusted tools that most security teams struggle to fully monitor, control, or even explain, namely AI agents. He said an agent that holds credentials and can reach the internet is a new attack surface, whether it is misconfigured or abused, and that when an attacker is behind it, its activity looks exactly like the employee who installed it. He said the question for defenders is not whether a tool is approved but what that tool is actually doing.

The research also examined a separate intrusion involving an AI agent and a Kubernetes cluster, and Elastic reconstructed 17,600 actions in the incident, at roughly one action every 20 seconds, over four uninterrupted days. Indicators that an AI agent may have been involved included duplicate commands issued seconds apart and a successful exploit followed immediately by a basic coding error. Elastic said security teams should track which AI tools, IT tools and signed software are trusted in their environments, assess those tools by behaviour rather than approval status, and correlate signals across cloud, endpoint and identity systems. The findings come as organisations across Europe face growing concern over attempts to disrupt everyday services through cyber attacks.

Articles.Title: Elastic warns attackers abuse trusted AI tools in hacks - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Dost launches AskDost AI assistant for finance teams
stories.Summary:
Dost launched AskDost, an AI assistant for finance and operations teams, on 4 November 2026. It is available as a standalone product or within the company's finance automation platform. AskDost connects to a company's ERP and other financial data sources, letting users ask questions in natural language and prepare finance workflows for human approval. It can be used across invoices, approvals, payments and reconciliation, and lets teams update general ledger coding rules in plain language.

Nothing is executed until a person signs it off, and an audit trail shows what changed and who approved it. The launch expands Dost's offering beyond process automation into business intelligence and workflow orchestration for finance teams. It is also the company's first product that can be adopted without the wider Dost platform, because it connects directly to an organisation's ERP. Dost said AskDost is built to understand invoices, purchase orders, VAT codes and general ledger coding without additional set-up. Through a tool called Dost Studio, finance teams can build and deploy their own apps and agents on their own data.

Dost cited Deloitte's latest UK CFO survey, which found that 67% of CFOs believe their organisations are only about a quarter of the way towards the transformation they expect AI to deliver. It also referred to CFO Connect's Europe-wide 2026 survey, which found that two-thirds of finance teams use at least one AI tool, yet no specialist finance AI product named in the survey accounted for more than 1% usage. Adam Barbera, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Dost, said finance leaders often have the data they need somewhere, but reaching the explanation takes days and three different people. He said Dost built AskDost so teams can shape it themselves, with their own agents and apps on their own data.

Dost's existing platform automates accounts payable and accounts receivable as a single process, covering invoice capture, data extraction, matching, approvals, payments and bank reconciliation. It integrates with ERP systems including SAP, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Sage and Oracle. Dost said it has processed more than 5 million accounting transactions and achieved 95% data extraction accuracy. Customers named by the company include HomeServe, Honest Greens, Housfy and Primaprix. AskDost adds a conversational layer on top of that transaction data for finance leaders, procurement teams, and accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.

Articles.Title: Dost launches AskDost AI assistant for finance teams - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Render just removed its AI sandbox time limit — and Vercel still has a 24-hour cap
stories.Summary:
Render removed the time limit on its AI sandbox, The New Stack reported on November 4, 2026. The change means sandboxes on Render no longer expire after a set period. Vercel still caps its sandboxes at 24 hours, the article said. The report did not name the people at Render who made the decision.

The article gives few other numbers or dates beyond the 24-hour cap at Vercel and the November 4 publication date. It does not say what Render's limit was before the change or how long sandboxes can now run. It also does not say whether Vercel plans to change its own cap. No pricing or plan details are given for either service.

The articles do not name who at Render is responsible for the change or include any statements from the company. No one from Vercel is quoted either. Because no one is quoted, there is nothing to paraphrase on what they said. The report presents the change without comment from either company.

The article places the change in the context of a wider discussion about sandboxing AI agents, including a separate piece on how isolated sandboxes really are. It does not say what happens next at Render or Vercel. It gives no timeline for further changes or announcements. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Render just removed its AI sandbox time limit — and Vercel still has a 24-hour cap - The New Stack

stories.Headline: Fortra says AI could save file transfer admins up to 160 hours a year
stories.Summary:
Fortra has published findings saying that artificial intelligence could save file transfer administrators up to 160 hours a year, according to The New Stack, which reported the figure on November 4, 2026. The article was written by Matthew Burns and appeared under the site's AI Operations and DevOps coverage. The report frames the savings around failed file transfers, which the headline describes as the problem AI could help with. The article gives no further detail on how the figure was calculated or which products were involved.

The 160 hours figure is the only number the article states, and it is presented as an annual saving per administrator. The article does not name any customers, does not give a date for when the savings would be realized, and does not describe a specific product release. It also does not say whether the figure comes from a survey, a test, or an internal estimate. No other dates or names appear in the story beyond the author and the publication date.

Fortra is the company making the claim, and the article attributes the 160 hour figure to Fortra. The article does not include any quoted statement from a Fortra executive or engineer, so there are no remarks to paraphrase beyond the claim itself. It also does not say who at Fortra conducted the work or which team produced the findings. Responsibility for the claim therefore rests with Fortra as the source, as presented by The New Stack.

The context is the wider interest in applying AI to IT operations, which The New Stack covers under its AI Operations section. The article does not say what happens next, whether Fortra plans further research, or whether any product changes will follow. It also does not say how the savings would be measured in practice. No timeline for follow-up coverage is given.

Articles.Title: Fortra says AI could save file transfer admins up to 160 hours a year - The New Stack

stories.Headline: AI First, Quality Always: Agentic SDLC Adoption Case Study
stories.Summary:
Catherine Weeks, an engineering director at Red Hat AI, gave a presentation at QCon AI about how Red Hat is adopting agentic AI across its software development lifecycle. She described two main modes of adoption, the AI copilot that works alongside an individual engineer and the AI factory that runs more autonomously. She said Red Hat is building an AI platform for other enterprises and is also using AI inside its own engineering teams. Her talk covered the pressure many companies feel from an AI-first mandate and how teams can balance speed with software quality.

Weeks said executives are pushing for AI adoption with urgency, largely to gain higher productivity, speed and output. She warned that putting a measurement behind something can lead teams to optimize around that measurement in the wrong ways. She cited Kent Beck's point that if teams only build pull requests, they are not building quality. She said the risk of a rushed approach includes technical failures, production systems going down and brand damage, and that customers lose trust faster than they gain it.

Weeks said engineering leaders need to set organizational direction and acknowledge that a market change is happening, even though the outcomes are not fully known. She urged leaders who have not been hands-on in years to get hands-on experience, as she did with side projects, so they can have real conversations with their engineers. She said architects and staff engineers should say what is feasible and be willing to experiment, since what is feasible changes as models improve. She told software engineers that stepping in and experimenting could be career defining, and suggested spending one Friday on it and building from there.

Weeks described how she built a context management system for herself over two days, which she said completely transformed her job. She noted that Red Hat saw some engineering leaders dragging their feet on adoption while others ran too far ahead and disrupted collaboration across teams. She referred to Steve Yegge's article on eight levels of AI adoption as a useful maturity model for individuals. She also mentioned custom eval harnesses, sandboxing and human-in-the-loop controls as ways to keep speed from compromising quality.

Articles.Title: AI First, Quality Always: Agentic SDLC Adoption Case Study - infoq.com

stories.Headline: GitLab Bets Context, Not Bigger Models, Will Fix AI Agent Costs
stories.Summary:
GitLab made GitLab Orbit generally available on Oct. 29 for Premium and Ultimate customers, and it is live on GitLab.com now. Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated will follow in the coming weeks. Orbit is a context graph for the software lifecycle that connects code, merge requests, work items, pipelines, vulnerabilities, and ownership in one view that updates as teams ship. Agents query the graph instead of rebuilding the picture themselves.

GitLab says that in its own testing, agents connected to Orbit produced up to 45x fewer hallucinations and used up to 4.5x fewer tokens on the same tasks with the same model. Compare the Market tested four context approaches for an AI code reviewer on 79 real merge requests, and the Orbit-grounded reviewer matched about 70% of expected inline comments while a retrieval-augmented generation approach matched about 58%. Orbit indexes GitLab data and default-branch code into a property graph stored in ClickHouse and runs as a separate service beside GitLab. Results follow existing GitLab permissions, and third-party agents including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode connect through the Model Context Protocol or the GitLab CLI. GitLab sells Orbit in query packs that form one shared pool for the whole organization, at $30 per user per month in GitLab Credits for 1,000 queries, with usage beyond the pool at about $0.03 per query and a 30-day free trial available through GitLab account teams.

Manav Khurana, chief product and marketing officer at GitLab, said AI agents are only as accurate and efficient as the context they work from. Ryan Harvey, head of AI engineering at Compare the Market, said the gap was clear in better comment placement and better summaries of what actually changed, and that RAG, which they had assumed would be the natural solution, ended up performing worse than no context at all. Mitch Ashley, vice president and practice lead at The Futurum Group, said context is becoming surface for effective AI agent behavior and that whoever tells an agent what a change touches, who owns the code, and what broke last week shapes what that agent does next. Ashley also said coverage is the test, since many enterprises run code on more than one platform, and that context stopping at GitLab's edge leaves agents guessing about the rest.

GitLab says more than 3,500 organizations have used Orbit since the beta, running more than 280,000 agent queries. The article notes that Orbit draws on data GitLab already holds and that GitLab says it can extend to other sources. It also notes that the benchmark figures are GitLab's own and that teams should track token use and retry rates in their own environment before and after turning it on. The article says the bigger shift is in how the industry thinks about agent performance, since cost and accuracy depend just as much on what an agent knows when it starts.

Articles.Title: GitLab Bets Context, Not Bigger Models, Will Fix AI Agent Costs - DevOps.com

stories.Headline: “AI is changing data centre requirements”: Interview with Digital Connexion’s Vikram K.
stories.Summary:
Vikram K., Chief Revenue Officer of Digital Connexion, gave an interview to tele.net in which he said AI is changing data centre requirements. He said India's installed data centre capacity grew from about 375 MW in 2020 to around 1,575 MW in August 2026, citing the Ministry of Electronics and IT. He said the next phase of growth will be shaped by NeoCloud providers, GPU-as-a-service platforms and hyperscalers. He also said Digital Connexion's MAA10 facility in Ambattur, Chennai, received NVIDIA DGX-Ready Data Centre Certification.

The interview gives several figures. MeitY's Rs 103.72 billion outlay is meant to strengthen India's AI ecosystem and widen access to computing for start-ups, researchers and enterprises. India's GPUaaS market earned $284 million in 2025 and is projected to reach $1.2 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 19.6 per cent between 2026 and 2033. MAA10's magnetic levitation-based air-cooled chillers can deliver up to 15 per cent energy savings, and the facility has the Indian Green Building Council's Green Data Centre Platinum certification.

Vikram said GPU availability alone is not enough, because NeoCloud operators also need high rack densities, substantial power, advanced cooling and robust network connectivity. He said power supply, electrical distribution and thermal management must work as one integrated system. He said Digital Connexion is developing AI-ready infrastructure with a 230 kV substation and a design aimed at a power usage effectiveness of 1.4. He said the company is adopting closed loop liquid cooling, which recirculates water, alongside a water treatment plant.

Vikram said India's potential as a global AI infrastructure hub depends on power availability, grid expansion, supply chain constraints and long-lead equipment. He said early coordination on grid connectivity, power availability and commissioning schedules is important. He cited JLL on the importance of power approvals for new capacity and the International Energy Agency on aligning electricity supply with rising data centre demand. He said the coming phase will be defined by the industry's ability to expand capacity while meeting power, cooling and sustainability needs.

Articles.Title: “AI is changing data centre requirements”: Interview with Digital Connexion’s Vikram K. - tele.net

stories.Headline: Machine learning classification of prevalent cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults with circadian syndrome from CHARLS
stories.Summary:
A study published in Scientific Reports on November 4, 2026, used machine learning to classify prevalent cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults with circadian syndrome. The authors, including Lu Wang, Yu-Jun Xiong and Xiang-Da Meng, drew on the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The cross-sectional analysis covered 4,091 adults with circadian syndrome. The unweighted prevalence of self-reported cardiovascular disease in the sample was 26.9%, or 1,101 of 4,091 people.

To avoid data leakage, missing-data multiple imputation was fitted only on the training set, which was 70% of the sample, or 2,863 people, and then applied to the held-out testing set of 30%, or 1,228 people. Several algorithms were trained and tuned with 5-fold cross-validation, including a generalized linear model, a gradient boosting machine, a random forest, deep learning and a stacked ensemble. In the testing set the stacked ensemble reached an AUC of 0.733, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.703 to 0.764, and a Brier score of 0.176. The random forest scored an AUC of 0.730 and the generalized linear model 0.728, differences the article describes as numerically small.

Calibration was satisfactory, with a calibration slope of 1.100 for the ensemble and 0.960 for the generalized linear model. Dyslipidemia, hypertension, kidney disease and age were the leading variables contributing to classification across models. Decision curve analysis showed positive net benefit across threshold probabilities of 10% to 70%. The authors said the models, including both transparent linear models and tree-based ensembles, showed acceptable discrimination and favorable calibration, and that simpler models such as the random forest and generalized linear model offered comparable utility to complex ensembles.

The authors describe these as feasible tools for clinical risk stratification. They note that prospective studies are needed to assess whether these variables can identify individuals who later develop cardiovascular disease. The CHARLS study was approved by the Peking University Institutional Review Board, under approval numbers IRB00001052-11015 for the questionnaire survey and physical examinations and IRB00001052-11014 for biomarker collection, and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

Articles.Title: Machine learning classification of prevalent cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older Chinese adults with circadian syndrome from CHARLS

stories.Headline: Machine learning algorithms integrating radiomics and clinical features for mortality prediction in patients with late-onset severe pneumonia after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Peking University People's Hospital developed and validated machine learning models that combine chest CT radiomics with clinical parameters to predict mortality in patients with late-onset severe pneumonia after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The retrospective cohort study was approved by the hospital's Ethics Committee, which waived informed consent. It enrolled 134 consecutive patients, 90 men and 44 women with a median age of 36.5 years and a range of 10 to 66 years, who developed the pneumonia after transplantation between January 2010 and April 2023. The outcome studied was survival status on day 60 after pneumonia onset.

The study analyzed initial chest CT scans showing new lesions, with laboratory tests performed within a maximum interval of seven days of CT and within 12 days of diagnosis. Patients were randomly assigned to a training set of 94 and a test set of 40 at a ratio of 7:3, and data in both sets were standardized using Z-scores. Using PyRadiomics version 3.0.1, 998 features were extracted across 7 categories, and LASSO regression identified 8 key features linked to mortality. LASSO regression with 5-fold cross-validation also selected 4 clinical features: monocyte count, platelet count, lactate dehydrogenase level, and abnormal liver function.

The random forest radiomics model performed best among the five radiomics models in the test set, with an area under the curve of 0.678. The random forest clinical model reached the highest area under the curve among the five clinical models at 0.764, and the random forest fusion model showed the best discrimination at 0.808. Pairwise comparisons among the three random forest models showed no significant differences, with all P values above 0.05. The authors said the fusion models tended to perform better than the clinical or radiomics models alone, though the improvement was not statistically significant.

The authors described several limitations, including that it was a single-center retrospective analysis with a relatively small sample that may lead to model overfitting. They said the models apply to early-stage prediction at diagnosis and do not capture the prognostic effect of later complications such as CT progression, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and mechanical ventilation. The authors concluded that the prototype is preliminary and requires external validation and optimization through large, multicenter prospective studies. They said future research will concentrate on re-evaluating and integrating comprehensive prognostic factors within larger patient cohorts.

Articles.Title: Machine learning algorithms integrating radiomics and clinical features for mortality prediction in patients with late-onset severe pneumonia after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

stories.Headline: Mixed-timestep spiking neural networks: a temporal alignment framework for high-efficiency neuromorphic computing
stories.Summary:
A study published on 2 November 2026 in Frontiers in Neuroscience proposed Mixed-Timestep Spiking Neural Networks, a framework in which different layers of a spiking neural network operate with different time-steps. The work was led by Mingxin Guo of the School of Future Technology at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences in Beijing. Most existing spiking neural networks use a uniform time-step across all layers, which the authors say limits temporal flexibility and produces suboptimal accuracy and latency trade-offs. The paper is an original research article in a research topic on spiking neural networks at scale.

The framework uses a quantization-aware conversion from artificial neural networks to spiking neural networks. The authors establish a theoretical relationship in which the spiking time-step T can be approximated by the activation quantization level 2 to the power n of the source network, so layer-wise activation bit-widths map to layer-wise time-steps. Quantization levels and firing thresholds are jointly optimized to obtain compact mixed-timestep configurations that reduce inference latency while preserving accuracy. To handle the temporal dimension mismatch caused by heterogeneous layer-wise time-steps, the authors propose Scaled Synaptic Current Accumulation, a fused temporal alignment mechanism that aligns inter-layer propagation in the synaptic-current domain without a standalone temporal-alignment kernel.

The authors say the design differs from dynamic time-step methods, which decide when to stop inference based on input-dependent confidence or entropy. They describe their time-steps as statically assigned per layer, which avoids extra runtime decision mechanisms and makes the framework more suitable for efficient deployment. The paper reports experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1K, CIFAR10-DVS and DVS-Gesture. On ImageNet-1K, the method based on ResNet-34 reached 73.63 percent Top-1 accuracy with only 4.88 average time-steps, which the authors describe as a favorable accuracy and latency trade-off for low-latency conversion.

The authors motivate the work by noting that training spiking networks is difficult because spike functions are non-differentiable, and that conversion-based methods can reach high accuracy but typically need long simulation time-steps. They say uniform time-step settings restrict temporal flexibility and that both training and inference complexity scale with the number of layers and temporal length. The paper draws on mixed-precision quantization in artificial networks, where layers receive different bit-widths according to their sensitivity, and applies a similar principle to time-steps. The article does not say what deployment or follow-up work is planned.

Articles.Title: Mixed-timestep spiking neural networks: a temporal alignment framework for high-efficiency neuromorphic computing

stories.Headline: A two-branch physics-informed neural network for small-sample sedimentation prediction of magnetorheological fluids
stories.Summary:
A study on predicting sedimentation in magnetorheological fluids was accepted for publication on 2 November 2026 in the journal Smart Materials and Structures, published by IOP Publishing. The authors are Wei Zhou, Tianle Cui, Decai Li, Xin Qi, Chao Ma, Xueqi Wang, Qiusheng Shi, Changrong Liao and Lei Xie. Most of them are affiliated with Chongqing University, with Li at Tsinghua University and Qi, Ma and Wang at the China Science and Technology Museum. The paper was received on 22 August 2026 and revised on 27 October 2026.

The study proposes a moving-boundary data-interpolated physics-informed network, called MB-DIP, to predict concentration-field evolution and mudline motion from a limited number of measured samples. The two-branch design combines a physical mudline prior with a moving-boundary-aligned concentration-field prior. For baseline fluids, samples with initial particle volume fractions of 7.5, 10, 15 and 32 vol% were used to predict sedimentation at 20 and 26 vol%. The mean absolute errors were 2.04% for the concentration field and 1.96 mm for mudline position, and the mean absolute percentage error of particle content was 2.83%.

The authors report that ablation experiments showed the contribution of physics-consistency refinement, and six-fold leave-one-source-concentration-out validation examined performance under varying source-data coverage. Further validation used SiO₂-modified fluids containing 28 vol% carbonyl iron particles and 0.25 to 1 wt% silica. MB-DIP captured changes in sedimentation behavior with silica content, while theoretical predictions remained unchanged. In that validation, concentration-field and mudline mean absolute errors ranged from 0.620% to 1.872% and from 0.306 to 1.081 mm.

The paper states that sedimentation tests under natural gravity are time-consuming, which limits experimental coverage of particle concentrations and formulations. The authors say the results support MB-DIP as a method for predicting sedimentation under limited-data conditions. They add that it has potential to reduce the experimental effort required for formulation evaluation. The accepted manuscript is protected by copyright during a 12-month embargo period from publication of the Version of Record.

Articles.Title: A two-branch physics-informed neural network for small-sample sedimentation prediction of magnetorheological fluids

stories.Headline: MIB advises OTT, digital news platforms on content compliance
stories.Summary:
India's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued an advisory on 4 November 2026 asking OTT platforms, digital news publishers and intermediaries to strictly follow the Information Technology Act, 2000 and its rules. The ministry said it had noted instances where digital news publishers and OTT platforms did not comply with the Act. The advisory flags misleading visuals, reporting on anti-terrorist operations, violence, communal content and AI-based content. It also calls for care with archival, illustrative or previously recorded visuals.

The advisory asks publishers to give the original date, location and context for visuals before publishing them online, and to name the source and timestamp for material taken from elsewhere, including social media. It cautions against live coverage of anti-terror operations and says reporting during such operations should use periodic briefings from authorised officers until the operation ends. Visuals of natural calamities, disasters and accidents must be date and time stamped, and only authentic maps of India published by the Survey of India should be used. Publishers must take reasonable steps to verify AI-generated or materially altered photographs, videos and audio, and disclose synthetic content shown with real people or events.

Intermediaries are reminded of their due diligence duties under Section 79 of the IT Act and Part II of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, including provisions on synthetically generated information in Rules 3(3) and 4(1A). The ministry also addresses protection of sexual offence victims' identities, citing statutory protections and Supreme Court directions including the Nipun Saxena case. It calls for editorial scrutiny of crime and violence coverage, with headlines, thumbnails and captions that do not misrepresent events, and for sensitivity with content involving women and children. OTT platforms and digital news publishers are asked to strengthen editorial and content-review mechanisms and to train staff on the IT Act, its rules and other applicable laws.

Articles.Title: MIB advises OTT, digital news platforms on content compliance

stories.Headline: Bybit CEO Ben Zhou: AI, Tokenization and Connected Infrastructure to Reshape the Future of Finance
stories.Summary:
Bybit Co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou spoke at Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, which took place on November 4th, 2026, according to a Chainwire announcement dated the same day. He appeared in a main-stage fireside chat titled "Bridging the Divide: The Next Chapter of TradFi & Crypto Convergence." Bybit says it is trusted by more than 80 million users worldwide. Zhou used the session to share his views on how artificial intelligence, asset tokenization and connected financial infrastructure are reshaping financial services.

Zhou said the next stage of finance is not about traditional finance and crypto replacing one another but about making them work together. He said AI, tokenization and connected infrastructure can help users reach more markets and services more efficiently. He noted that putting assets on-chain is only a starting point, and that wider adoption needs clear investor rights, dependable custody and enough liquidity. He also said that as AI moves from giving information to starting financial actions, platforms will need stronger permissions, better monitoring and more refined user controls.

Zhou stressed that greater access and efficiency must go hand in hand with security, risk management and regulatory compliance. He said platforms must build these safeguards into their infrastructure as they expand beyond trading to serve broader financial needs. He said Bybit's role is to connect these services securely and efficiently, with regulatory requirements and local accountability embedded in the systems that deliver them. He also said confidence in the crypto market is growing as it develops over the long term, with liquidity remaining important to its progress.

The announcement includes a disclaimer that Bybit is not licensed by the Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission and that its services are not available to the public in Hong Kong. It describes Bybit as a platform bringing together investing, trading, payments and wealth-building in a single ecosystem. The company says it combines AI-powered technology, deep global liquidity, robust security and transparent operations. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the positions Zhou set out at the event.

Articles.Title: Bybit CEO Ben Zhou: AI, Tokenization and Connected Infrastructure to Reshape the Future of Finance - TradingView

stories.Headline: Lazarus AI Raises $43M to Advance Independent AI
stories.Summary:
Lazarus AI announced on November 4, 2026, that it has raised $43 million in funding. The round included participation from QBE, Mucker Capital, Motivate Ventures, State Farm Ventures, Wave Function Ventures, Indelible Solutions, Joyance Partners, AllegisNL Capital, One Way Ventures, AngelList, Techstars, Plug and Play and others. The Boston-based company applies AI to consequential problems while customers keep control of data, models, deployment and economics. Lazarus says it is trusted by insurers, government agencies and technology companies to run production AI.

The platform runs on-premises, in sovereign environments or in a customer's cloud, with no per-token charges and no rebuild when models or hardware change. In a modeled high-volume scenario, it cut annual operating costs 78% versus pay-per-use frontier models. Its Applied Intelligence System cites every finding to its source page and has raised field-level accuracy 12.5 points over standalone models across 150 customer use cases. Clearwing finds vulnerabilities in source code, reproduces them, grades the evidence and proposes a fix, while engineers decide when it lands. Constructor recovers business logic from decades-old systems and generates modern code proven equivalent to the original, now in pilots with two of the world's largest mainframe makers.

Alex Panait, CEO of Lazarus AI, said the opportunity in AI is enormous, and so is the question of control, including who chooses the models, where data runs, how costs behave and whether an organization can still change direction. He said customers keep sensitive data inside their walls, approve every model change and see the evidence behind every result. Lazarus will use the funding to expand strategic partnerships, invest in R&D and bring new products to market. The company serves insurers, healthcare, government and financial institutions across North America, Asia-Pacific and Europe.

Articles.Title: Lazarus AI Raises $43M to Advance Independent AI - HPCwire

stories.Headline: ZS Expands Agentic AI Capabilities in ZAIDYN for Life Sciences
stories.Summary:
ZS announced on November 4, 2026 that it had expanded agentic AI capabilities in ZAIDYN, its connected suite of applications for the life sciences industry. The company, a global management consulting and technology firm based in Evanston, Illinois, built ZAIDYN in 2021 with AI at its core. The suite offers more than 30 modules used by life sciences companies, including 80% of the top 20, in over 100 countries. The new agents can sense signals, analyze information, generate insights, recommend actions and automate approved activities within defined guardrails.

The expansion applies the new agentic capabilities across commercial, personalization, medical and patient workflows. ZAIDYN is designed to deliver value in three ways: accelerating planning and insight generation, responding to market signals, and automating workflows. Because the applications are connected, they can coordinate data, insights, decisions and actions across functions when the work requires it. The suite is designed to work with companies' existing technology foundations, including CRM and data lakehouse systems, and organizations can operate it themselves or have ZS operate it on their behalf.

Sunil Dixit, chief product officer at ZS, said clients face declining HCP access, pricing pressures and more than $200 billion in sales facing loss of exclusivity, while preparing for a promising pipeline of new launches. He said AI offers a disruptive technology to respond to these market challenges, and that ZAIDYN can help clients use intelligence more quickly so teams can accelerate commercialization and deepen engagement with patients and providers. He added that the suite retains the guardrails and human oversight a regulated industry like life sciences demands. ZS said people stay in control of decisions that require human judgment.

ZS was founded in 1983 and has more than 15,000 employees in over 40 offices worldwide. The company said the evolution of ZAIDYN's agentic AI capabilities is already earning industry recognition, with Everest Group naming ZS a Luminary in its 2026 Innovation Watch assessment on agentic AI in life sciences commercial. ZS described ZAIDYN as a key part of its strategy of helping organizations embed transformational AI into workflows and scale better decision-making across the enterprise. The company said the suite is supported from strategy and implementation through change management and ongoing operations.

Articles.Title: ZS Expands Agentic AI Capabilities in ZAIDYN for Life Sciences - HPCwire

stories.Headline: Enterprises shift to cost per task for AI, boosting private cloud
stories.Summary:
Enterprises are moving from token-based pricing for AI to a cost per task approach, according to a TechGig report published on November 4, 2026. J.R. Storment, executive director of the Tokenomics Foundation, argues that companies should look at the Total Cost of AI rather than just token bills from frontier model providers. That total includes GPUs for training, specialised processors for inference, networking, databases, external stores, and the engineering, operations and legal labor needed to run AI systems. Raj Rajagopal of ValueOps by Broadcom, a founding member of the foundation, said three in four enterprises struggle to prove the business value of their AI investments to Chief Financial Officers.

Chris Wolf of VMware Cloud Foundation at Broadcom said 56 per cent of respondents in a global survey either run or plan to run production AI inference on a private cloud. He said online token rates are often meant for developer use cases, not production inference, which brings extra costs for patching, lifecycle management, backup, telemetry, audit and access controls. Workloads suited to private clouds include contact centers, document search, language translation, log parsing, task automation, local agent execution, PII filtering and red teaming. Broadcom says organisations can save 40 per cent to 90 per cent by moving appropriate AI workloads to a private cloud, with more predictable costs.

Rajagopal said a recalibration of IT budgets is coming, with AI spend rising while labor spend may need adjustment. He said the fundamental shift is from cost per token to cost per task, comparing it to judging a contractor on job completion rather than hours worked. Wolf said gateways, such as those built into VMware Cloud Foundation, are important for hybrid AI environments. These gateways can expose virtual model endpoints, letting IT redirect from public cloud models to local ones without refactoring applications, and make routing decisions based on cost or prompt content.

Articles.Title: Enterprises shift to cost per task for AI, boosting private cloud

stories.Headline: CoreWeave Shares Fall 3.1% as Democratic Election Victory Adds to AI Infrastructure Concerns
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave shares fell 3.1% in premarket trading on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, after Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections. The result raised concerns about tighter regulation of artificial intelligence infrastructure and possible limits on data centre construction. The decline added to existing worries about CoreWeave's debt and its recent share price weakness. The stock had gained 6.3% on Tuesday but dropped 8.6% on Monday, coming within a few cents of its 52-week low of $49.46.

The election outcome could lead to fewer technology tax incentives, more antitrust scrutiny and new restrictions on data centre building, though the exact effects are uncertain. Several newly elected Democratic governors have said they support stronger oversight of AI and related infrastructure. CoreWeave carries about $35 billion in debt and has a revenue backlog of roughly $104 billion. Insiders have sold more than $382 million worth of shares in the past 90 days. CoreWeave is due to report third-quarter results on November 10.

Investors are watching whether CoreWeave can turn its backlog into revenue and cash flow fast enough to cover rising financing costs. The company's shares fell even as the S&P 500 rose 0.6% and the Nasdaq gained 0.5% in the same premarket period, suggesting the weakness was specific to the company and AI infrastructure. The stock remained below its 20-day and 200-day moving averages. The articles do not name a company official or give direct comments from CoreWeave.

Articles.Title: CoreWeave Shares Fall 3.1% as Democratic Election Victory Adds to AI Infrastructure Concerns - Yahoo Finance

stories.Headline: AI's Building Boom Meets A Blue Wave. 'Neocloud' Stocks Fall.
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave and Nebius shares fell on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, after midterm election results gave Democrats what the article calls a blue wave. Democrats won control of Congress and also won governorships in key states including Texas and Ohio. Voters in more than 30 localities across nine states also voted, according to the article. The selloff reflected worries that the results will make the next wave of data center construction more difficult.

The article ties the drop to concerns about building the next wave of data centers, which it says could become harder under the new political balance. It reports Democratic wins in Congress, in governorships in key states such as Texas and Ohio, and in local votes in more than 30 localities across nine states. It also notes that major indexes advanced on Wednesday after the clear Democratic win. The article gives no further details on specific policies or on what the companies plan to do.

The article does not name any company officials or lawmakers and gives no direct statements from them. Responsibility is described only through the election outcome, with Democrats winning control of Congress and key governorships. The concerns are attributed to worries among investors rather than to any named person. No one is quoted saying what they will do next.

The article places the stock moves in the context of the election and the wider market, which rose while AI-related names faded. It mentions that Nvidia flashed sell signals as earnings approached, and that Tesla and SpaceX shares stumbled. It does not say what happens next for CoreWeave, Nebius, or data center construction. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI's Building Boom Meets A Blue Wave. 'Neocloud' Stocks Fall. - Investor's Business Daily

stories.Headline: India becomes ChatGPT's largest market globally by users
stories.Summary:
India became ChatGPT's largest market in the world by weekly active users, OpenAI India managing director Prabhjeet Singh told The Economic Times. He said the Indian user base has doubled since January 2026. In February 2026, OpenAI reported more than 100 million weekly ChatGPT users in India. The milestone follows CEO Sam Altman's earlier description of India as the company's fastest-growing market and second-largest by users during his visit last year.

OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT's Indian-language capabilities and focusing on Android-first product development to reach users beyond major cities. The company expects to make announcements about UPI and payments in the coming weeks. Its partnership with Razorpay aims to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT. OpenAI announced its first India office in Delhi NCR in August 2025 and unveiled plans for Mumbai and Bengaluru offices at the India AI Impact Summit in February.

Singh attributed the growth to Indian users increasingly building ChatGPT into their daily workflows and finding new uses for the chatbot. He said OpenAI would consider more capacity as infrastructure becomes available. He also supported clear AI regulation to build confidence among consumers, enterprises and developers. OpenAI is engaging with government agencies, banks and financial institutions to improve cybersecurity and protect critical infrastructure against misuse of AI agents.

The company launched OpenAI for India to expand access, infrastructure and enterprise adoption. Its partnership with TCS' HyperVault data centre business begins with 100 megawatts of capacity, with potential to scale to 1 gigawatt. This capacity will address enterprise data residency and security requirements. Singh noted that enterprises, global capability centres and startups are moving from pilot projects to production deployments, citing JioHotstar and Cars24 as examples. India is also a significant and rapidly growing market for Codex, with substantial developer use from tier-II cities.

Articles.Title: India becomes ChatGPT's largest market globally by users

stories.Headline: Cognition introduces hierarchical budgets for Devin AI coding agent
stories.Summary:
Cognition introduced hierarchical budgets for its Devin AI coding agent on November 4, 2026, according to TechGig. The feature lets organisations govern AI agent spending across teams and projects. Administrators can assign budgets to different teams and track their spending. If a budget runs out while Devin is working on a task, the session stops automatically.

An administrator can start with an overall budget and distribute it among business units, which can then allocate funds to teams and projects up to three levels deep. Companies can also create budgets for specific projects, such as a major legacy modernisation effort, even when multiple departments are involved. Separate controls exist for Devin running in the cloud and on engineers' desktops. Engineers get alerts on their homepage when they are on track to exceed a limit, and they can request more Agent Compute Units from the budget owner inside the product.

Lukas Burger, who works across go-to-market and engineering at Cognition, told The New Stack that the feature came from conversations with customers. He said initial controls for single teams did not scale when Devin moved into broader deployments across organisations. Budget administrators can review requests manually or clear them automatically. Admins can also enable efficiency-based approvals, which raise an engineer's limit if their Efficiency Score is strong, up to a set ceiling.

Cognition introduced the Efficiency Score in October to estimate productive engineering hours relative to Devin consumption. Central IT keeps visibility and can set limits without approving every request. Burger noted that Cognition is also developing an option for teams to switch to lower-cost models after a soft limit so important work can finish. That option is still under development.

stories.Headline: Kyndryl Prioritises Enterprise AI, Alliance-Led Growth and Partner Readiness
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl has set out four priorities for its channel strategy in 2027, according to Vikas Dua, Vice President and Application, Data and AI Practice Leader at Kyndryl India. The priorities are driving enterprise AI adoption, accelerating alliance-led growth, strengthening partner readiness and delivering outcome-led solutions. The company says the focus is on helping customers scale AI through AI-ready infrastructure, Agentic AI and AI-enabled operations. It also plans to strengthen partner capabilities through training and certifications across AI, Hybrid Cloud and Cybersecurity.

The programme is built around four key areas, the article says. It promotes joint business planning and co-creation so partners can align on account plans, develop solutions together and coordinate customer engagement. Partner enablement covers certifications, technical training and knowledge sharing to strengthen solution development and delivery. The programme also combines partner innovation with Kyndryl's enterprise IT transformation and services expertise, and encourages Enterprise AI collaboration on integrated solutions that meet enterprise requirements for security, scalability and operational readiness.

Dua said Kyndryl will co-create industry-specific solutions with partners, combining complementary technologies and services to deliver measurable business outcomes and long-term growth. He said the focus moving forward will be on deepening technology partnerships, strengthening joint go-to-market initiatives and scaling AI-led modernization solutions. He described the approach as positioning Kyndryl as an ecosystem orchestrator, bringing together the strengths of multiple technology partners. Through deeper alliances and co-innovation, he said, the goal is to accelerate modernization and AI adoption while addressing enterprise needs for security, resiliency and scalability.

stories.Headline: GitHub rearchitects Git primitives for AI agent scale
stories.Summary:
GitHub is rebuilding core Git primitives and expanding its infrastructure to handle growing strain from autonomous AI agents, the company announced on November 4, 2026. The Microsoft subsidiary has added more than four million CPU cores and 160 petabytes of internal storage this year. Over 40 per cent of pull requests on the platform were started by AI agents in September 2026, up from 17 per cent in March, according to the GitHub Octoverse 2026 report. The surge in agent activity has put considerable strain on GitHub's infrastructure, with eight performance-degrading incidents recorded in July and a nearly eight-hour global outage in August traced to a critical infrastructure failure at a US data centre.

The rearchitected Git primitives decouple compute from storage and minimise coordination, aiming to improve scale by 180x. GitHub is completing its full multi-region migration into Azure early next year to allow elastic infrastructure scaling with customer demand, according to Jay Parikh, EVP of CoreAI at Microsoft. The platform also introduced new Copilot features, including Fusion, a runtime model orchestration engine that routes requests to the best-suited model, and Fusion Max, which GitHub says scored within two points of Claude Opus 5.5 Max while running 40 per cent faster at roughly half the API cost. Other additions include Copilot Projects for multi-agent management, Copilot Automations for a self-improvement feedback loop, Copilot Dreaming, which opens pull requests to update outdated instruction files, and Copilot Code Review Max, which GitHub touts as having posted the highest F1 score on ReviewBench for critical vulnerabilities.

GitHub COO Kyle Daigle said the world does not need a new GitHub, but rather for the platform to evolve for the agentic era. The company works directly with approximately 250,000 maintainers worldwide through the GitHub Secure Open Source Fund, in partnership with organisations like the Open Source Security Foundation and the GitHub Security Lab. Open-source maintainers are experiencing burnout from hallucinated AI-generated bug reports, and Daniel Stenberg, creator of cURL, suspended public vulnerability-reporting bounties after being flooded with such reports. Many code maintainers are banning unverified LLM-assisted patches because of the additional verification load.

Articles.Title: GitHub rearchitects Git primitives for AI agent scale

stories.Headline: Human review possible for private AI chats across major platforms
stories.Summary:
Human reviewers at major AI companies, including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic, can access some private conversations to improve systems, investigate safety violations or troubleshoot problems, TechGig reported on November 4, 2026. This does not mean every message is read, but it contradicts the assumption that AI chats are strictly private. Deleting a conversation from a user's history does not always mean immediate permanent deletion from company systems. Google's Gemini Apps Privacy Hub says reviewed Gemini chats can be kept for up to three years, even if users delete their activity. OpenAI uses consumer ChatGPT conversations for model improvement unless users opt out in settings, but turning off training does not stop human review for abuse monitoring, especially for Temporary Chats.

Microsoft's Copilot Privacy FAQ confirms that some conversations get automated and human review for product improvement and digital safety, and users cannot fully opt out because review is needed to investigate suspected violations. Anthropic lets certain Claude conversations be reviewed, with access limited to a small number of personnel involved in model training. Conversations flagged by safety systems may still be used to detect harmful content and improve safety measures. All four platforms offer controls to reduce how conversations are used, such as turning off model training, found under Settings and Data Controls for ChatGPT, Settings and help then Activity for Gemini, Settings then Privacy for Claude, and profile settings then Privacy then Training on conversation activity for Microsoft Copilot. These settings do not guarantee that conversations can never be reviewed for safety, security or legal reasons.

Paid subscriptions like ChatGPT Plus do not automatically give stronger privacy protections than consumer policies. Users are advised to avoid sharing sensitive information such as passwords or financial details in consumer AI chatbots and to replace identifying details with placeholders before submitting. Temporary or incognito chat modes offered by ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude can limit saved history and model training. For highly sensitive work, the article suggests running AI models locally with tools such as Ollama and LM Studio to reduce the need to upload information to cloud providers. Enterprise solutions offer more contractual protections, according to the article.

stories.Headline: Google, partners dismantle XCPE botnet of 1.3 million Android TV boxes
stories.Summary:
Google and its industry partners dismantled a botnet called XCPE, which was made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes, TechGig reported on November 4, 2026. The devices shipped with malicious software that secretly rented users' internet connections to strangers and carried out advertising fraud, according to Google. Experts involved in the takedown expect it to cut the botnet's access to more than 10 million other compromised systems, including Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines. A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group said the Chinese manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. was found responsible for including the malware.

The GTIG report said Videostrong sold access to criminal affiliates and loaded their malware modules onto infected devices. Google took legal action to take down the domains and servers Videostrong used to control the botnet and install more malware. The same XCPE malware was also found in telehealth devices, karaoke machines and digital signage systems, though TV boxes were the majority. Google requires all Android device makers to pass compatibility and security tests, but Videostrong found a way to load its malicious software right after a user's first boot-up.

Google said it has since fixed that weakness. Google credited industry partners including the startup Synthient, which tracks proxy providers. Synthient founder Ben Brundage told KrebsOnSecurity that Videostrong's malware also distributed software for the proxy service Grass. He called the figure of 1.3 million affected devices "highly conservative" and said the real scale is likely much higher.

Residential proxy providers AppSalt, which covers Honeygain and Oxylabs, and NetNut were linked to the botnet, and the FBI had seized hundreds of NetNut domains in July 2026 over a separate botnet called Popa. Synthient's earlier research into the Kimwolf botnet had helped fragment DDoS attacks and drew attention from the Motion Picture Association. Google has severed ties with Videostrong, and the takedown is expected to cut off the botnet's reach to the additional compromised IoT systems. The articles do not say what further steps, if any, will follow against Videostrong or the proxy providers.

Articles.Title: Google, partners dismantle XCPE botnet of 1.3 million Android TV boxes

stories.Headline: Chinese Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX to Target Over 200 Organizations Worldwide
stories.Summary:
Chinese state-sponsored hackers used an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX in attacks on high-value targets, according to a CrowdStrike analysis reported on October 30, 2026. CrowdStrike attributed the activity to a China-based targeted intrusion adversary it tracks as Vapor Panda, previously known as VexatiousTemper. The group was first identified in February 2021 and overlaps with a threat cluster Trend Micro calls Earth Estries. Starting October 17, 2026, Vapor Panda used the tool against more than 200 distinct organizations worldwide.

The targets included foreign ministries in Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, semiconductor, defense, and think tank organizations in the U.S., and telecommunications providers in multiple regions. The list also covered 19 U.S.-based organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear, and financial sectors. Post-exploitation activity was confirmed at nine organizations, where the attacker deployed BLOODALCHEMY, a derivative of ShadowPad, followed by credential spraying, network scanning, and reconnaissance. Vapor Panda also conducted password-spraying and credential-scanning against at least 12 additional organizations, including U.S.-based think tanks and government entities in Europe.

CrowdStrike said agentic tooling like ARTEX lets a small team pursue a wider target set at speed than manual operations would support. The operation used ARTEX with DeepSeek and an unknown subscription-based commercial large language model, with planner and worker agents coordinating toward a common goal. A human operator stayed in the loop, directing agents to write web shells, extract domain administrator passwords, and enumerate endpoint sensor coverage. CrowdStrike said that in a single intrusion the planning agents consumed on the order of 1.4 billion input tokens.

CrowdStrike said the agents pursued multiple attack paths in parallel across web applications, cloud services, container environments, Active Directory, and mail and VPN infrastructure, and shifted to alternatives when a path failed. The disclosure coincided with four previously undocumented China-linked groups: Hollow Panda, Overcast Panda, Titan Panda, and Veiled Panda. Overcast Panda was linked to close access intrusions using a proprietary FlowCloud backdoor deployed via direct physical access when targets traveled to China. Titan Panda exploited a hard-coded IIS machine key vulnerability in Intapp Time Server, with attacks first detected in April 2026.

stories.Headline: ChatGPT Consumer Product Lead Adam Fry says ChatGPT has hit 1.2B WAUs, adding 200M over the past two months, and its search volume is now ~20% of Google's (Alex Kantrowitz/Big Technology)
stories.Summary:
OpenAI's ChatGPT now handles search query volume equal to about 20 per cent of Google's, Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead, said at a press event on Monday. Fry also said ChatGPT has reached 1.2 billion weekly active users, up from 1 billion after adding 200 million users in the past two months. He gave the figures during a fireside chat at an OpenAI-hosted dinner in New York City on Monday night. OpenAI defines a search as any user input query that results in a web search, which excludes tasks like defining terms or simple how-to explanations. The company also said users create 1.5 billion images with ChatGPT per week, and voice mode has 250 million combined weekly active users.

For comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google's 2023 antitrust trial that Bing held about 3 per cent of the search engine market share after more than a decade. OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant portion of its searches, alongside its in-house search index. OpenAI plans to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work modes, so the toggle at the top will soon go away. The company aims for profitability through ads as it approaches a potential IPO early next year. Last month, OpenAI introduced images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT, moving beyond just company names, logos, and links.

Fry told reporters that ads have not negatively impacted product usage, and most users do not mind them. He said the growth is going big and that the company is staying very focused on how fast ChatGPT is growing. He said ChatGPT started with writing and coding help, and people have since grown into topics like people, places, things, finance and health that need up-to-date information. On Dots, OpenAI's personal assistant, he said the company wants to be thoughtful and conservative with permissions because it is a new space built on trust. He said Dots are on the compute-heavier side right now, and the goal is to dial that back over time.

Google is heavily investing in AI tools, including AI Overview and generative AI capabilities with personalised results, visualisations, and charts. Google described AI as a potential disruptor during the same trial, suggesting ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it. Fry said OpenAI has passed 50 million subscriptions and the number has grown considerably since then, and that its ads business reached more than a billion in annual recurring revenue within 200 days. He said he is confident the value of a Dot will be able to pay for itself through credits, subscriptions, and ads. He said OpenAI has nothing to share about when Dots will reach a broader set of users, but the goal is to bring it out to all users.

stories.Headline: SOCs to have 50 per cent more engineers than analysts by 2028: Gartner
stories.Summary:
Gartner predicts that security operations centers will have 50 per cent more engineers than analysts by 2028, according to a 2026 report by analyst Pete Shoard. The report says AI agents are already cutting the alert-handling work done for common detection cases. This marks the end of alert processing as the main job of a SOC. The report is titled "The Roles Required for the AI-Enabled Security Operations Center (SOC)."

The report says human analysts will move from alert triage to owning cases from start to finish and explaining response options. AI-assembled case files will still need meaningful human validation before teams rely on them. Detection engineering will grow into a broader discipline that includes prompt design, workflow testing and checking AI output, along with practices like versioning and rollback. Entry-level roles will need new training as AI takes over traditional Tier 1 triage, and Gartner suggests studying agent work, giving newcomers early ownership of lower-risk cases and feeding corrections back to improve AI accuracy.

Gartner recommends that SOCs measure cases and decisions instead of alerts, tracking case accuracy, cycle time and decision confidence rather than alert volume or closure rates. The report also names exposure management as an emerging SOC capability that needs investment, and it calls for continuous threat exposure management to become a standing SOC function instead of an annual or quarterly exercise. The report says the SOC will not shrink by 2030, with staff moving toward detection engineering, threat expertise, offensive testing and exposure management. A 2026 survey by Prophet Security of more than 250 CISOs, SOC leaders and practitioners found that 57 per cent expect team size to stay the same and 9 per cent expect it to grow.

stories.Headline: Kyndryl Q2 FY27 slides: margins expand as AI modernization drives signings
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl Holdings presented its second quarter fiscal 2027 earnings results on November 4, 2026, and its shares rose 37.25% to $17.76 after the presentation. The IT infrastructure services provider reported revenue of $3,651 million, down 1.9% from $3,721 million a year earlier, while the constant-currency decline was 0.8%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $699 million at a 19.1% margin, up 190 basis points from 17.2%, and adjusted pretax income was $150 million at a 4.1% margin, up 80 basis points. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.42 beat the consensus estimate of $0.41, and revenue beat by $10 million.

By segment, the United States generated $980 million with 9% growth, Principal Markets contributed $1,177 million, Strategic Markets added $939 million, and Japan accounted for $555 million. Kyndryl Consult revenue grew 8% to $3.6 billion on a last-twelve-months basis, and hyperscaler-related revenue surged 39% to $2.1 billion from $1.5 billion. Last-twelve-months signings for Kyndryl Consult reached $4.6 billion, including 43 deals greater than $50 million, 11 of them signed in the second quarter, and 154 deals above $10 million. First-half signings grew about 34% combined, with first-quarter signings up 50% and second-quarter signings up in the high 20% range.

The company said its progress against fiscal 2028 signposts was positive, citing a 5-point improvement in backlog trajectory, Kyndryl Consult signings of $4 billion versus $3.5 billion in revenue, and 8% priced margins on post-spin signings. It reported $1 billion in cumulative savings from Advanced Delivery initiatives powered by Agentic AI. Kyndryl earned the 2026 Google Cloud Global Partner of the Year Award for Infrastructure Modernization and was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Center Outsourcing Services. It also received partner of the year awards from Dell Technologies, HPE, and Cloudflare, and Microsoft gave it the Frontier Partner badge.

As of September 30, 2026, Kyndryl held $1.7 billion in cash and $4.8 billion in available liquidity, with net debt of $2.4 billion. Its net leverage ratio was 0.9x, up from 0.5x at the end of fiscal 2026 but still below its target of less than 1x adjusted EBITDA. The presentation described customer wins including a 16-year relationship with a global marketing services company, a 20-year partnership with a major European bank, and a 15-year relationship with a global luxury goods company. All three case studies emphasized expanding scope with long-standing customers.
