stories.Headline: NATO cyber drill integrates AI agents, OpenAI Daybreak
stories.Summary:
NATO's cyber defence centre of excellence, the CCDCOE, began the Crossed Swords 2026 exercise in Tallinn, Estonia, on Monday, according to TechGig. The execution phase of the drill is set to run through Friday. More than 250 participants from over 40 countries, including both NATO members and non-members, are taking part. They include national cyber forces and supporting units such as military cyber operators, threat hunters and digital forensics experts.

The exercise trains participants to plan cyber operations and to time them with kinetic military action. It aims to sharpen how staff direct offensive and defensive cyber assets at the command level, while specialists hone tactical skills. The cyber exercise is integrated with a training event for special operations forces. A new dedicated track on AI agents lets participants build, deploy and assess agents and operate alongside them. The environment uses locally hosted AI and, for the first time, OpenAI's Daybreak cyber defence offering.

Jozef Kostelansky, the Crossed Swords 2026 exercise director, said the core operational challenge is synchronisation, with timing measured in minutes. He said AI is now in the loop on both sides, which increases complexity. He explained that introducing AI agents directly addresses a significant shift in the modern cyber threat landscape. The training prepares participants to use AI while keeping human oversight for complex, multi-domain missions.

The drill also pairs national cyber forces with civilian partners to build critical infrastructure protection into their plans. Over 20 organisations from industry, academia and NGOs support the event with know-how, systems and tools. These include Bitdefender, ESET, Elastic, Mandiant, OpenAI and Stamus Networks. The articles do not say what happens after the exercise ends on Friday.

Articles.Title: NATO cyber drill integrates AI agents, OpenAI Daybreak

stories.Headline: Kyndryl CEO: AI Modernization Means Transforming IT Without Disruption
stories.Summary:
Kyndryl Chairman and CEO Martin Schroeter told analysts on Wednesday, during prepared remarks for the company's fiscal second-quarter 2027 conference call, that Kyndryl is expanding its AI capabilities and partner relationships to help customers modernize mission-critical IT infrastructure without disrupting operations. He said modernization demand is creating opportunities across consulting, public and private cloud, and agentic AI, as customers balance transformation with stability. He said customers trust Kyndryl to run and modernize their essential technology environments at scale, and rely on it to lead complex migrations, modernize applications and data, and deploy AI securely. Kyndryl is ranked No. 13 on CRN's 2026 Solution Provider 500.

The company this year expanded its AI innovation lab network to include Dallas and Luxembourg, joining its previous facility in Liverpool, England, where designers, forward-deployed engineers, and industry specialists test use cases, validate business outcomes, and develop roadmaps for scaling AI in existing environments. Schroeter said Kyndryl Bridge connects much of the company's work by bringing data insights, AI governance and orchestration into a single platform, giving people and increasingly agents the context to understand what is happening and determine the appropriate next action. Kyndryl next week plans to unveil a co-developed solution with ServiceNow that will combine AI-powered workflows with Kyndryl Bridge data, operational intelligence, and agents, and he previewed an AI sovereignty offering addressing customers' need to retain platform choice and data control. He said the expanded Broadcom relationship adds end-to-end VMware Cloud Foundation consulting for private-cloud modernization, and that Kyndryl Consult signings exceeded revenue over the past 12 months. He reaffirmed the full-year outlook and said the company is progressing toward its fiscal 2028 financial objectives.

Asked about Kyndryl Consult growth, Schroeter said there was a deceleration between the first and second fiscal quarters, but revenue tends to move up and down, and he expects the second quarter to be the low point of the year in constant currency growth for the business. Asked about potential softness in Europe, he said data sovereignty issues are important everywhere but especially in Europe, and those discussions are challenging for customers dealing with mission-critical systems in an ever-changing geopolitical world. He said Kyndryl plans to unveil a sovereignty approach next week, and that when the company brings innovation and expertise, customers are willing to make a move. He said Europe has been a little slower but is starting to come back in signings and revenue performance.

For the fiscal second quarter 2027, which ended September 30, Kyndryl reported total revenue of $3.65 billion, down 1.9 percent from $3.72 billion a year earlier. That included U.S. revenue of $980 million, up from $899 million; Japan revenue of $555 million, down from $581 million; revenue from Canada, the U.K., France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal of $1.18 billion, down from $1.25 billion; and revenue from the rest of the world of $939 million, down from $987 million. Total revenue beat analyst expectations by $80 million, according to Seeking Alpha. Kyndryl reported GAAP net earnings of $59 million, or 27 cents per share, down from $68 million, or 29 cents per share, and non-GAAP net income of $92 million, or 42 cents per share, up from $89 million, or 38 cents per share, which beat expectations by 4 cents per share.

stories.Headline: Binance, SBI cyberattacks highlight financial sector vulnerabilities
stories.Summary:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, reported a major security breach on October 29, with around $6.3 billion in unauthorized cryptocurrency withdrawals. The exchange temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals and worked with law enforcement agencies and blockchain companies to trace the stolen assets. The Federal Bureau of Investigation later confirmed that the attack was linked to TraderTraitor, a hacking group associated with North Korea. Binance said it covered 95 per cent of the stolen cryptocurrencies using company funds to buy replacement tokens. In India, State Bank of India is investigating a suspected data breach after approximately 3.75 lakh records linked to the bank appeared on the dark web.

SBI received alerts from its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency, and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team on October 16. A preliminary examination identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information, reportedly including names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, residential addresses, and loan application details. SBI activated its cyber incident response procedures and appointed an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident. Cert-In has warned that attackers may be using AI-assisted tools for reconnaissance and fraudulent transactions. In an advisory issued on October 15, the agency also flagged incidents where AI agents accessed Indian organisation computer systems without authorisation.

Its May 2026 blueprint recommends measures including a Zero Trust security system, which requires continuous identity checks for all network access. Cert-In also advised continuous monitoring of networks, payment APIs, cloud infrastructure, and employee accounts, prompt fixing of software vulnerabilities, stronger security at third-party vendors, and multi-factor authentication and training for phishing and deepfake impersonation. These incidents occur amid a rise in cyberattacks targeting Indian banks, non-banking financial companies, fintechs, and payment service providers. The articles describe the breaches as highlighting growing cybersecurity threats to financial institutions, with hackers exploiting weak APIs, credentials, and third-party vendors. The reports do not say what further action is planned beyond the investigations and the measures already recommended.

Articles.Title: Binance, SBI cyberattacks highlight financial sector vulnerabilities

stories.Headline: NTT Signs Multi-Year Deal With McLaren F1 Starting 2027 to Support Team on AI Security
stories.Summary:
NTT and McLaren Racing announced on November 4, 2026 that NTT will become an official partner of the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team for multiple years starting with the 2027 season. The deal centers on AI security and governance, with NTT supporting McLaren's push to become the team that most adeptly harnesses AI on the F1 grid. The two companies said they will also create engagement programs so NTT customers and F1 fans can experience NTT's technology firsthand. The partnership builds on earlier ties through NTT Docomo Business with the McLaren F1 team and NTT DATA with the Arrow McLaren IndyCar Team.

Under the agreement, NTT will help build a framework to manage the security risks that come with rapidly evolving AI technology, aiming for responsible AI use alongside faster innovation. The contract starts with the 2027 season and runs for multiple years, and the target team is the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team. The stated pillars of the collaboration are AI security and governance and engagement programs. McLaren Racing was founded in 1963 and first entered F1 in 1966, and it has won 23 F1 World Championship titles and more than 200 Grand Prix victories.

Akira Shimada, NTT's Representative Director, President and CEO, said he was delighted to announce the partnership and noted that F1 is a stage where wisdom from around the world gathers and the challenge to push the limits continues. He said McLaren and NTT share much in common, and that NTT aims to build on its experience as title sponsor of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES since 2019 and to accelerate global business with McLaren. McLaren CEO Zak Brown welcomed bringing NTT on board as an official partner and said AI holds enormous potential for motorsport and for McLaren's business. He said NTT's expertise will be a major support in introducing new technology in a responsible and safe manner.

For NTT, the deal is a chance to make an impression in overseas markets as it shifts beyond its role as a telecommunications carrier toward businesses centered on AI and security. For McLaren, getting a risk-management framework for expanding AI use from an outside specialist is expected to enhance its credibility in racing operations and business. F1 teams are increasingly using AI in data analysis and simulation, while handling confidential driving data and strategy information makes security and governance an unavoidable challenge. If NTT can show its presence in this area, the articles say, ripple effects into industries such as automotive and manufacturing can be expected, and the two companies' efforts toward the 2027 season could influence the standard for AI use in F1.

Articles.Title: NTT Signs Multi-Year Deal With McLaren F1 Starting 2027 to Support Team on AI Security - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: AI-Linked Breaches Mount as WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev Disclose Hacks
stories.Summary:
Over the past month, hackers have hit at least a dozen AI developer platforms, including CommandCode, Northflank, Trigger.dev, Chainstack and WorkOS. The attackers appear to have been hunting for AI access tokens they could sell, and they used AI agents to speed up their intrusions. The incidents do not appear to be related, and the attackers got in through different routes, from stolen credentials to third-party dependencies and exploited vulnerabilities. Other victims named in the reporting include Andromeda, Brev (NVIDIA), Fireworks AI, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp and Zeabur, with the hackers mainly after stored customer secrets.

Chainstack, a blockchain infrastructure and Web3 services provider, was hit on October 26, and the attackers reached a development environment and parts of its production environment through a third-party component. The company said a database holding customer account information was accessed, including organization names, account holder names, member email addresses and password hashes. Node credentials may also have been exposed, and Chainstack told customers to rotate them. WorkOS, an API platform for building enterprise applications, said the hackers compromised an internal application used by its sales team on October 30.

The accessed data included names, email addresses, phone numbers, job titles, company affiliations, customer account histories, sales details, customer communications and information about customers' use of WorkOS products. The Cloud Security Alliance said intruders are reaching AI provider credentials through hosting platforms, evaluation services and developer consoles, and that because that layer holds credentials for many downstream customers, one intrusion can expose keys for many inference accounts at once. Wiz said the surge comes from LLM-jacking and LLM broker infrastructure, which make stolen AI access tokens easy to sell, and it expects more threat actors to turn to credential theft. Wiz also said it saw multiple threat actors using the same compromised keys, which suggests a strong market for this type of credential.

Chainstack and WorkOS both disclosed attacks that relied on the open source AI penetration testing framework Artex for automation, and multiple companies have linked attacks attributed to the Chinese APT Storm-0940 to the use of Artex. The reporting ties the trend to demand driven by distillation, which means training a cheaper model on the outputs of a more advanced one, notably alleged against Chinese AI labs. Wiz said it observed hackers abusing enterprise credentials compromised in these attacks, including two cases that shared an identical first unauthorized activity, which happened within 30 minutes of the reported credential access in the vendor breach. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Chainstack prompting customers to rotate node credentials.

Articles.Title: AI-Linked Breaches Mount as WorkOS, Northflank, Trigger.dev Disclose Hacks - SecurityWeek

stories.Headline: Accenture accused of publishing AI paper littered with AI hallucinations
stories.Summary:
Accenture has been accused of publishing an AI research paper that was littered with hallucinations, according to the Financial Times on November 4, 2026. The report does not name the people who made the accusation or say when the paper was published. It also does not give the title of the paper or describe any of the false content it is said to contain. The available article is behind a paywall, so few details of the case are public.

The article does not set out what the paper requires or what changes follow from it. It gives no numbers, dates or names beyond the company and the publication date. No details are provided on how many errors the paper contained or what topics it covered. The story also does not say whether the paper has been corrected or withdrawn.

The articles do not say who at Accenture is responsible for the paper or what the company said about the claims. No statement from Accenture or from any of its staff is included. The identity of the accusers is not given either. Because of this, there is no response to paraphrase.

The context is limited to the accusation itself, and the articles do not say what happens next. There is no word on whether an investigation has begun or whether the paper will be reviewed. It is also not clear what action, if any, Accenture plans to take. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Accenture accused of publishing AI paper littered with AI hallucinations

stories.Headline: Analysis: Anthropic’s IPO Tests AI’s Growth Story Against Its Costs
stories.Summary:
Anthropic filed for a U.S. initial public offering on Oct. 26, disclosing rapid revenue growth and its first quarterly operating profit alongside nearly $800 billion in long-term computing commitments. The Claude developer plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with trading expected to begin in mid-November after a roadshow. A U.S. hedge fund representative told Caixin the offering could raise $50 billion to $100 billion, though Anthropic has not announced an offering size or price range. Market expectations value the company above $1.5 trillion, below earlier estimates of $2 trillion.

First-half revenue reached $16.3 billion, up 1,300% from a year earlier, and annual revenue rose from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion in 2025. Usage-based token charges generated $13.06 billion, or 80.2% of first-half revenue, while subscriptions contributed another $3.22 billion. Enterprise customers with at least $100,000 in trailing 12-month revenue rose from over 950 in September 2025 to over 11,900 a year later. First-half computing costs rose 283% to $8.95 billion, falling to 55% of revenue from 201% a year earlier.

Anthropic earned a second-quarter operating profit of $974 million, while its first-half operating loss was $693 million and its first-half GAAP net loss was $80.75 billion. Nearly $72.4 billion of that net loss reflected fair-value changes in convertible notes and derivative liabilities, not operating losses. Commitments to Amazon total $110 billion from May 2026 through April 2036, and many of the nearly $800 billion in commitments require payment even if unused. At June 30, Anthropic held $112.4 billion in cash and equivalents plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments.

Public investors will have limited governance influence, because a single Class F share held by an entity jointly owned by the seven founders carries non-dilutable 50.1% of shareholder voting power but no economic rights. The independent Long-Term Benefit Trust will appoint four of seven directors after the IPO, enabling it to remove executives or delay model releases on safety grounds. As a Delaware public-benefit corporation, Anthropic must balance shareholders' interests, affected people, and its responsible-AI mission, and it warned these objectives could conflict with financial performance. The listing follows OpenAI's September decision not to list this year, and on Oct. 26 AI infrastructure stocks rose, with Nvidia up 2.39%, CoreWeave up 1.76% and Amazon up 0.44%.

Articles.Title: Analysis: Anthropic’s IPO Tests AI’s Growth Story Against Its Costs - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: China stocks surge as policy support boosts sentiment; AI tech shares lead rally
stories.Summary:
Chinese equities rebounded sharply on Wednesday, supported by policies aimed at stabilizing the capital markets and lifting investor confidence, with artificial intelligence and technology shares leading the gains. The STAR Composite Index, which tracks China's sci-tech innovation board, closed 9.9 percent higher at 1,525.31 points. More than 150 stocks on that board hit their daily price limit or rose more than 10 percent, according to the Securities Times. Chipmaker CXMT jumped 13.63 percent, with turnover above 20 billion yuan, or about 2.99 billion dollars.

Total A-share turnover reached 2.0519 trillion yuan, up 336.8 billion yuan from the previous session, and more than 4,600 stocks advanced. The People's Bank of China said on Wednesday it had cut the rate on its stock repurchase and share buy-back relending facility by 25 basis points to 1 percent, effective immediately. The facility is open to 21 national-level commercial banks and five systemically important city-level banks, covers 100 percent of eligible loans, has a one-year term and can be extended as banks need. Banks may add a reasonable margin on top of the relending rate and set their own maturities and pricing for such loans. The central bank also said it would fully meet banks' relending needs, after banks submitted quota applications totaling more than 200 billion yuan.

Li Chang'an, a professor at the University of International Business and Economics, said the rate cut would lower financing costs for listed companies and make share buybacks and stake increases easier when markets are relatively weak. He added that long-term market stability depends on deeper institutional reforms, including stricter IPO screening, improved delisting mechanisms and better dividend policies. Dong Shaopeng, a senior research fellow at Renmin University of China, said using tools such as stock repurchase and related refinancing to inject liquidity is both necessary and beneficial. He rejected foreign media claims that volatility is mainly driven by external shocks and sell-offs in technology and AI sectors, saying it largely reflects domestic market dynamics. Yang Delong, chief economist at First Seafront Fund, said the rally reflected both a technical rebound from oversold conditions and a policy-driven improvement in expectations.

The rate cut followed the central bank's announcement earlier this week that the relending program would become a permanent institutional arrangement, with the rate lowered from 1.25 percent to 1 percent. The program is one of two policy tools supporting the capital market, alongside the Securities, Funds and Insurance Companies Swap Facility. CXMT also announced a plan to raise its share repurchase from a range of 1 billion to 2 billion yuan to a range of 2.5 billion to 5 billion yuan, saying the proposal reflects confidence in its future development. The People's Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration and the China Securities Regulatory Commission had held two separate meetings aimed at stabilizing the capital market. Analysts said the market is expected to gradually shift from sentiment-driven trading to performance driven by fundamentals.

Articles.Title: China stocks surge as policy support boosts sentiment; AI tech shares lead rally - Global Times

stories.Headline: China’s daily AI token use surges to 140 trillion: Wuzhen blue book
stories.Summary:
China's daily use of artificial intelligence tokens reached 140 trillion in March, according to a blue book released on Wednesday at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang Province. Tokens are the basic units that large language models process when handling a prompt or generating a response. The blue book, the China Internet Development Report 2026 and the World Internet Development Report 2026 were compiled by the Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies. The China report cited monitoring data from the National Data Administration.

A separate report from the China Internet Network Information Center showed that China had more than 700 million generative AI users as of the end of June, more than half of the population. China's market for enterprise AI agents reached 21.2 billion yuan, or 3.17 billion dollars, in 2025. China's embodied AI market reached about 915 billion yuan in 2025, up 20.4 percent year on year. More than 140 Chinese companies made complete humanoid robots in 2025 and released more than 330 products, and AI is already used at more than 30 percent of manufacturing firms above designated size.

Industry analyst Liu Dingding told the Global Times that token use is rising as people use AI more often and give it harder tasks, and that producing a short drama with AI can consume far more tokens than drafting an article. He said companies need to see that AI saves money or helps them get more work done to keep paying for it after a trial. Unitree Robotics founder Wang Xingxing said at a side forum that 2027 would likely be a turning point for the robotics industry or the AI models that power robots. He described the last few millimeters as the biggest hurdle for embodied AI, saying robots can pick up objects reliably but still struggle with finer control such as taking apart a smartphone or threading a needle.

The World report said AI was moving into the physical world and expanding the scope of scientific research, and it warned that uneven progress was widening the global digital divide. It said China is among the global front-runners in internet development, with advantages in industrial applications, the scale of the digital economy and infrastructure. As of June, 924 generative AI services had completed filing and 573 applications or features had completed registration. China had 47 AI computing facilities in the 10,000-card class as of the end of the first quarter of 2026.

Articles.Title: China’s daily AI token use surges to 140 trillion: Wuzhen blue book - Global Times

stories.Headline: Stocks, dollar slide as stunning victories for Democrats jolt AI bets
stories.Summary:
Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House in the US midterm elections, a result reported on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. It was a major setback for President Donald Trump, and the party scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds for the first time in generations. The breadth of the success showed in gains in districts long considered safely conservative. The result caught some investors off guard.

Global stocks and the dollar fell overnight on fears that rapid growth in the AI sector could be held back by regulatory scrutiny. AI stocks in Asia led the decline, while bonds and safe-haven currencies such as the Swiss franc gained. By the European morning equities had turned higher, with MSCI's All-World index up 0.13% and Europe's STOXX 600 up 0.5%. US stock futures had fallen by as much as 2% overnight before edging into positive territory. Shares in Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX, which he intends to merge, were down around 4.5% to 5% on Europe's Tradegate platform, against declines of around 0.3% to 0.9% for other Big Tech stocks.

Deborah Cunningham, chief investment officer for global liquidity markets at Federated Hermes, said few had seen the double victory coming at the start of the year. She said a divided federal government typically blocks new legislation, an environment markets traditionally view favourably. Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said the results had a mild impact on markets so far and that investors would move from trading election uncertainty to trading what the results mean for policy. She said the news was bad for Tesla and SpaceX on Wednesday, but semiconductor names could brush off concerns about AI regulation and keep moving higher. Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities in Singapore, said bonds were the clear winner as markets put the AI trade on the chopping block.

The AI boom has helped drive global markets in recent years through heavy spending by tech giants racing to build data centres and expand computing capacity. That has made investors acutely sensitive to anything that could derail the technology's rapid expansion. The election outcome could also carry implications for the US fiscal outlook and for sectors such as defence, healthcare and banking. Futures on the small-cap Russell 2000 index were last up 0.7%, having lost 1% earlier. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 3 basis points at 4.92%, having fallen as much as 6 basis points to a low of 4.89% overnight.

Articles.Title: Stocks, dollar slide as stunning victories for Democrats jolt AI bets

stories.Headline: We’ve missed why people use AI therapy
stories.Summary:
A Baylor Lariat opinion piece published on November 4, 2026, argued that people are missing why users turn to AI therapy. The author, Mady Mijares, a junior pre-med biomedical engineering student, wrote that character.ai users seeking pseudo relationships and fantasies rose to almost 200 million in early 2026. She noted that character.ai filed bankruptcy after lawsuits with alleged ties to teen suicide, and that Google Gemini and OpenAI each faced lawsuits over users who died by suicide after chatbot interactions. She also cited figures that 1.2 million weekly users express suicidal thoughts and 80,000 report mania and psychosis.

The article says traditional therapy costs $100 to $250 an hour without insurance and $20 to $50 an hour with it. It says 20 to 25 percent of young adults have reported using chatbots for mental health advice or emotional support, and 35 percent of psychologists have patients who use AI for consolation, companionship and self-affirmations. It notes that the Baylor Counseling Center added a questionnaire to its initial therapy consultation form asking whether patients had used AI for counseling. It also mentions Replika, launched in 2017, and Candy.ai, which launched an AI Girlfriend app in 2023.

Mijares wrote that AI cannot formally diagnose or hold users accountable, and that without an in-person conversation the software cannot detect if a user is in crisis, self-harming or suicidal. She said therabots can give harmful, toxic or incorrect advice during a time of need. She argued that shaming people for seeking AI company will not solve the root issue and will make it worse, and that vulnerable people need to be understood and listened to. She said society is too critical and judgmental and needs to understand why people resort to AI for love and empathy.

The article describes a mental health crisis and burnout, with Generation Z called the loneliest and least resilient generation. It quotes a Reddit user who said they use ChatGPT to console them and fear losing touch with real relationships. Mijares concluded that people are suffering and the last thing they need is another reason to stop talking and resort to AI bots. The article does not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: We’ve missed why people use AI therapy

stories.Headline: AI can’t build your brand for you
stories.Summary:
GumGum CEO Marcus Startzel wrote an opinion article published by The Current on November 4, 2026, arguing that marketers should not hand brand-building over to AI and algorithms. He described a common argument that AI is collapsing the purchase funnel, so that the whole journey from awareness to purchase becomes one AI-mediated moment. Startzel said he has heard that argument in boardrooms and on conference stages, and he called it wrong. He said it rests on half-truths and on a tech-driven dismissal of the value of brand-building, and that brands which accept it will pay for it.

Startzel wrote that the funnel did not flatten and that the stakes got higher. His example is a person asking an AI assistant for the best running shoe, getting a list that probably includes HOKA and Nike, and in most cases buying Nike. He said the AI did not push Nike harder and Nike was not cheaper, but people know Nike and have a feeling about it built over years through advertising, athletes and culture. He said that feeling is brand affinity, that trust comes with it, and that both tip the scales when AI runs a purchase decision. He also said consumers are more skeptical because of products that look like game changers until a click leads to a site clearly spun up by AI.

Startzel said AI sits on top of the funnel and filters what is already there, so a model has nothing to work with if a brand is not in someone's head before they open the chat window. He said models pick up on what people do, and that the more a brand is talked about, reviewed and written about, the more often it shows up in the answer, with upper-funnel advertising feeding that. He said brands should not walk away from performance marketing but should get the order right, because affinity has to exist before someone opens a chat window, types into a search bar or walks into a store. He said the walled garden model is built to retarget and take credit, so the lower funnel gets the credit and the upper funnel gets cut in the next year's plan. He said AI can amplify a brand that already exists, but somebody still has to build its reputation.

Articles.Title: AI can’t build your brand for you

stories.Headline: Making AI Sustainable? From Frugal Models to Responsible Governance
stories.Summary:
The 2026 Natixis CIB Green Summit took place on 4 November 2026 and brought together panelists to discuss whether the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence can be compatible with environmental and social concerns. Major model providers reported that their active user base had tripled and their revenue had increased fivefold over the past year. The International Energy Agency reports that data-center electricity consumption rose by 17% in 2025, and by 50% among AI-focused hyperscalers. The IEA projects that consumption will nearly double by 2030, reaching around 3% of global electricity demand.

By 2030, AI-related water consumption could equal the annual basic domestic water needs of 1.3 billion people. Its land footprint could exceed 14,500 km², which is roughly twice the size of the Jakarta metropolitan area. Chloë Voisin-Bormuth cited figures from RTE showing that in May 2026 data center capacity in France reached 18 GW, compared to only 5 GW at the end of 2024. The panels also covered public acceptance, the risk of losing control over AI systems, and potential job displacement.

Georgia Dunne of STACK EMEA said grid connection is a major development bottleneck and that procurement of renewables depends on location. She said STACK sources renewable electricity through green power purchase agreements while keeping backup generators, and that reduced generator-testing frequency cuts related emissions by 46%. Birgit Lundem Jakobsen of PGIM said investor analysis has become more forensic, with physical and environmental risks treated as part of credit risk. Samiya Jmili of BNP Paribas Asset Management said her team is comfortable holding an asset temporarily if it has a credible transition plan aligned with NZIF.

Both investors stressed that a transition plan needs clear milestones, achievable measures, and the capital expenditure to deliver them. Birgit Lundem Jakobsen said investors now see local communities and NIMBY risk as key elements of their analysis, and that community opposition can create a barrier to entry that may be credit-positive for established operators. Georgia Dunne said it is essential to communicate early about a project's impacts and benefits, including job creation and its contribution to data sovereignty. Rebecca Smith of Natixis said green labeling on a data center project financing can highlight key metrics on energy and water efficiency and renewable energy sourcing for communities and investors alike.

Articles.Title: Making AI Sustainable? From Frugal Models to Responsible Governance

stories.Headline: The CHRO six-pack for AI implementations
stories.Summary:
Amit Joshi, Professor of AI and Strategy at IMD, published an article on November 4, 2026, in Brain Circuits, setting out six ways chief human resources officers can help make AI implementations succeed. The article says CHROs and the wider HR team are crucial to successful AI implementations. It argues that HR is best placed to manage internal communication and to lead on training and upskilling. The piece also says the HR function is well placed to monitor the use of new AI tools, collect feedback, and address concerns about ethics, privacy, and safety.

The article advises leaders to stop telling staff that AI will not lead to job losses, because staff who feel management is trying to deceive them may resist implementation or try to undermine it. It calls for open and honest communication, with an exchange of views about how both employer and employee see roles changing. It says workers facing upskilling fatigue need convincing that investing time and effort in AI adoption is worth it, and that more human-centered design will help. It also says users are more likely to adopt AI tools they see as explainable, and that staff need to feel the tools act without prejudice and do not put data privacy at risk.

Where the likely impact of AI is clear, the article says leaders should set it out early so workers get the support and reassurance they need. It says CHROs should work with staff and managers to design new job roles that use AI as a supportive element, building confidence and even keen anticipation. It adds that CHROs must support cultural change and encourage innovation, and that employees who feel free to fail will feel more comfortable experimenting with new technologies. The article ends with a set of questions for checking whether an organization is being transparent with its workforce about the likely impact of AI.

The article's key takeaway is that once employees accept AI as a gateway rather than a barrier to their progress, new horizons will open up for them and the organization. It sits alongside other recent pieces on the site, including one on data-strategy moves and ones on what COOs and CFOs should do in the AI era. Joshi is Program Director of the AI Strategy and Implementation program, the Generative AI for Business Sprint, and the Business Analytics for Leaders course. The article does not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: The CHRO six-pack for AI implementations

stories.Headline: How CIOs can retain control as AI writes more code
stories.Summary:
AI coding tools are now used daily by 72% of developers who have tried them, according to Sonar's 2026 State of Code Developer Survey of more than 1,100 professional developers. AI accounts for 42% of committed code, a share expected to reach 65% by next year. At Google, AI generated over 30% of new code by spring 2025 and 75% by spring 2026. GitClear's analysis of 623 million changed lines found duplicated code blocks rose 81% since 2023, to 73 per million, and code churn doubled from 3.3% to 7.1%.

The survey also found that 96% of developers do not fully trust AI-generated code, and only 48% always verify it before committing. The Stack Overflow 2025 developer survey showed favourable views of AI tools fell from over 70% in 2023 and 2024 to about 60% in 2025, while distrust in AI output accuracy grew from 31% to 46% in a year. Tim Chilton of Ordnance Survey said developers can spend more time fixing AI code than writing it. The articles say CIOs should set guidelines, policies and training, and keep humans reviewing output.

Benoît Dageville of Snowflake said AI can help people do the same work at a fraction of the cost, and that he writes five times more code but is more productive. Steve Lucas of Boomi said his staff write 10 times the code they did two years ago, and Ed Macosky said AI should recursively modify 80% of a software organization's code. Gill Haus of Chase said automation must run end to end so humans are not stuck in the middle. François-Xavier Pierrel of TF1 said policies are needed before agent use reaches high volume, or AI becomes a critical mess.

Kirsty Roth of Thomson Reuters said her firm has spent 12 months considering what AI coding means for jobs, asking whether it needs more architects or product people. Tal Carmi of WalkMe said non-developers can build tools but need guardrails, and much in-house engineering work is shifting from building to testing. Emmanuel Frenehard of Sanofi said he worries for professionals who do not use AI to code, because in five years they may not have jobs. The articles say the value for engineers is shifting to review, judgment and writing precise specifications.

Articles.Title: How CIOs can retain control as AI writes more code

stories.Headline: Am I going to be fired by AI? How corporate America is being seduced by AI and algorithms in the ‘forever layoffs’ era
stories.Summary:
In July, 26 anonymous former Meta employees sued the company, claiming it used AI-enabled systems to choose who would be laid off in a major round of cuts this year. The plaintiffs say the systems disproportionately targeted people who needed disability accommodations or took parental leave. One former employee, a high performer for five years, saw her rating changed to fit a bell curve after a medical leave in late 2025. A former director said the dashboards failed to distinguish employees' leave from lack of engagement.

Meta has denied the claims, and HR leader Linh Doan said in a declaration that AI did not select anyone for termination and did not assist anyone in making selection decisions. The lawsuit follows years in which companies have used automated tools to collect data on hiring, promotions and absenteeism. Major companies including JPMorgan Chase, Disney and Meta now use AI to draft self-assessments and performance reviews. A Fast Company LinkedIn poll of more than 480 respondents found that 37% were very concerned about AI being used to pick employees for layoffs.

Experts told Fast Company there are no tools on the market expressly designed to conduct layoffs, though some companies brand their products as workforce management tools, which one researcher said is code for layoffs. Richard Landers of the University of Minnesota said layoff decisions are an impossible problem, which makes external tools attractive because some responsibility is offloaded. Joseph Fuller of Harvard Business School said using AI for these decisions is really in its infancy. Hatim Rahman of Northwestern University said AI and algorithms give a veneer of objectivity.

Some states have passed laws forcing companies to be more transparent about how AI factors into termination decisions. Lawsuits against HR tech companies Workday and Eightfold are testing how AI use could perpetuate discrimination at other stages of employment. In the first quarter of 2026, AI companies reportedly received more than 80% of overall venture capital funding, about $242 billion, which could bring more tools to the market. Uber is facing a fine of nearly $1 billion in the Netherlands for suspending drivers, and the company plans to appeal.

Articles.Title: Am I going to be fired by AI? How corporate America is being seduced by AI and algorithms in the ‘forever layoffs’ era

stories.Headline: When Singles’ Day shoppers start stocking up on AI tokens, the time has changed: Global Times editorial
stories.Summary:
During this year's Singles' Day shopping festival, Chinese consumers found a new item on their shopping lists: AI tokens. Tmall and JD.com each introduced AI token sections bringing together services from Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Zhipu AI. One livestream recorded sales of 2 trillion tokens in just half an hour. The Global Times editorial said this is a phenomenon rarely seen anywhere else in the world, and foreign media have noticed it with curiosity and astonishment.

The editorial said AI tokens are no longer simply an overseas concept copied in China. It said token-based consumption has grown from China's large digital consumer market, active user base and mature industrial ecosystem. According to OpenRouter, a global AI model aggregation platform, Chinese large language models have led US models in token usage for 27 consecutive weeks, including the week of October 26 to November 1. More than one-third of the tokens used by enterprises in Global South countries come from Chinese models.

The editorial argued that the decisive factor in AI competition is whether companies can consistently deliver reliable, practical AI services at reasonable costs. It said a 2025 KPMG survey covering 47 countries found that Chinese people were among the most optimistic about AI. It credited this to China's rise in national strength and to broad improvements in education and culture over several decades. It said the transformation was driven by practical efforts so that ordinary people can share in the benefits of technological progress, not by exploitation, coercion or barriers.

The editorial also described how Chinese households once prized watches, bicycles, sewing machines and radios, and later televisions, refrigerators and washing machines. It said few could have imagined that China would later help define new forms of consumption and new standards in the digital wave. It said the rapid uptake of open-source large language models and the deployment of humanoid robots in industry tell a different story from Western doubts about China's ability to innovate. It said the "AI Plus" initiative is empowering sectors such as education, healthcare, elderly care, culture and tourism, employment and consumer services.

Articles.Title: When Singles’ Day shoppers start stocking up on AI tokens, the time has changed: Global Times editorial - Global Times

stories.Headline: BRI Wealth cuts report times by 75% with Aveni AI
stories.Summary:
BRI Wealth Management has reached close to full active usage of Aveni Assist among its advice, paraplanning and administration staff, the company said on 4 November 2026. Suitability report turnaround has fallen by 75% since the AI tool was introduced. Assist now covers the journey from the initial client meeting to the finished suitability report. BRI first adopted the technology in 2025 after a trial period, before adding its report-writing functions in 2026. Transactional tasks such as pension withdrawals and ISA top-ups are now completed far more quickly than before, freeing staff from routine paperwork.

Advisers and planners keep full authority over each recommendation. With less time spent on repetitive drafting, the paraplanning team has redirected its efforts towards more demanding work. This includes building frameworks and research for the firm's retirement planning approach, giving greater attention to portfolio management, and providing the individual touches behind BRI's hands-on client service. BRI credits much of the smooth implementation to groundwork laid during its trial. Because the firm controlled its own Assist templates, staff tested the tool on both straightforward and complicated cases, adjusted its outputs to match the house style, and issued clear guidance to colleagues before wider rollout.

Paraplanner manager Bradley Sheridan said Assist has removed the bottleneck of repetitive work, so reports are turned around faster and clients receive quicker service. He said the firm uses Aveni as a report writer, not a financial planning thinker, and reviews and personalises every piece before it goes to a client. Aveni chief revenue officer Ana Nedava said BRI is a good example of adopting AI thoughtfully, bringing every team along while keeping people and clients at the centre. BRI said that although it is still looking for further efficiencies, its priority is to use technology to reinforce client relationships rather than substitute for them. Sheridan advised firms considering the tool to be clear about which repetitive tasks they want to remove and equally clear about what they want to keep in human hands.

Articles.Title: BRI Wealth cuts report times by 75% with Aveni AI

stories.Headline: No more ‘heads-up’ tracking: Chinese university scraps AI attention system amid privacy backlash
stories.Summary:
Nanjing University said on Wednesday that it had stopped tracking how often students looked up during class, after an AI-powered "smart classroom" system drew widespread attention online. The controversy began when students received a notice that the school would use its newly upgraded system to monitor attendance in certain courses over a one-week period. A screenshot then circulated online showing surveillance footage alongside data on late arrivals, attendance rates and the proportion of students looking up. Concerns grew after a teacher reportedly told a class group chat that attendance data could affect participation grades or even lead to exam results being cancelled.

Cover News reported that the university awarded a contract worth more than 31.52 million yuan, or about 4.4 million dollars, to upgrade 113 classrooms at its Xianlin campus. Tender documents listed technical requirements including facial detection, facial recognition, AI-based headcounts and tracking of how often students looked up. Some students told media the university had not sought their consent before introducing the system, raising concerns that their facial data could be accessed by the university or technology companies. Others said that even without facial recognition, having their attention monitored made them uncomfortable.

In a statement, the university's undergraduate education office and IT department denied that attendance was linked to grades or that the system was introduced in response to inspections by higher-level authorities. The university said the system did not collect biometric data such as facial features or use facial recognition technology. It said the project aimed to modernize teaching facilities, support livestreamed lectures and cross-campus interactions, and allow lessons to be recorded and replayed, and that it was reviewed by experts and went through public bidding under government procurement rules. The university said that without authorization the system does not collect facial or other biometric information or conduct facial recognition in teaching applications, and that it is currently no longer collecting data on the proportion of students looking up.

The university said images circulating online were personal screenshots taken during online teaching supervision at its Suzhou campus in May this year, rather than live surveillance footage from the current system. The controversy has fueled a broader debate over the growing use of AI in higher education, with critics questioning whether students' engagement can be measured by how often they look up. Critics warned that such technologies risk turning classrooms into spaces of constant algorithmic surveillance, according to the Paper. The university pledged to continue putting students first and to protect their privacy while using digital and intelligent technologies to support learning.

Articles.Title: No more ‘heads-up’ tracking: Chinese university scraps AI attention system amid privacy backlash - Global Times

stories.Headline: Former CENTCOM AI Adviser Warns Troops Asking AI the Wrong Question Could Point Them at the Wrong Target
stories.Summary:
Andrew Moore, founder and CEO of Lovelace AI, former head of Google Cloud AI and the first artificial intelligence adviser to U.S. Central Command, warned in an interview with Military.com published on November 4, 2026, that troops who ask AI to prove a theory can get a convincing but wrong answer. He described an analyst who suspects a black pickup truck and a house in a civilian neighborhood are tied to weapons production, then asks AI to find evidence supporting that theory. Within seconds the system could search billions of pieces of information and return what looks like 15,000 pieces of evidence, while ignoring anything irrelevant or contradictory. Moore said the AI may have done exactly what the human asked, and the house could still be the wrong one.

The Defense Department's 2026 AI strategy calls for an "Agent Network" to expand the use of AI agents for battle management and decision support, from campaign planning to "kill chain execution," and for rapid experimentation with AI-enabled warfighting capabilities. Moore said he does not believe the military should slow down, and that it may even be able to move a little faster, but that AI needs rigorous testing like any other military technology, comparing it to fielding a new helicopter. He said commanders have the right to expect corroboration from multiple independent sources, and that military AI needs to let analysts work backward from a conclusion and examine the information supporting it. He suggested better questions, such as asking for the pros and cons of targeting a house or what other independent sources could be checked, and said even a 92% probability might leave too much uncertainty for a commander to act.

Moore said he saw lower-stakes versions of the problem with commercial machine-learning systems, where bad actors could use fake reviews, fake sales and information from nonexistent shopping sites to influence what algorithms concluded, and that military AI needs to be "properly skeptical." He founded Lovelace AI in part to address that problem, and the company is developing technology intended to make AI-generated conclusions traceable to the underlying information. He estimated that perhaps 95% of the places AI could improve military operations involve functions like keeping an ammunition dump supplied, allocating resources and maintaining equipment rather than target selection. He said engineers cannot just tell people to be careful and must give them tools to help them be careful.

The articles say the Pentagon is accelerating its use of AI and that America's adversaries have access to increasingly powerful AI as well, creating an incentive not just to attack American AI systems but potentially to manipulate the information those systems consume. Moore said troops need opportunities to learn the difference between asking AI to build a case and asking it to test one during exercises, where asking the wrong question can result in a training failure rather than a real-world one. He said he has been impressed by junior service members finding creative ways to use technology to solve everyday problems, including the "spreadsheet jockeys" he encountered during his work with CENTCOM. The challenge, the article says, is making sure speed and seemingly overwhelming amounts of information do not create false confidence.

Articles.Title: Former CENTCOM AI Adviser Warns Troops Asking AI the Wrong Question Could Point Them at the Wrong Target

stories.Headline: AI Giants to Come Under Fresh Scrutiny But New Rules Unlikely
stories.Summary:
Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections, and they are now set to increase scrutiny of the companies building the most advanced artificial intelligence models. The shift gives the party a larger platform to contrast its approach with President Donald Trump's hands-off stance. Costs and risks tied to the AI boom became a kitchen-table issue during the midterms, possibly for the first time, and liberal candidates sought to address it. The article was published on November 4, 2026.

The change means more oversight attention on leading AI developers, though the article gives no specific bills, dates or figures. Democrats still face a steep path to putting an AI agenda in place because they have not found consensus on how to regulate the technology. Any legislation that might pass also faces the threat of potential vetoes by Trump. The article does not say what specific rules or requirements are being proposed.

Democrats in Congress are the ones responsible for the fresh scrutiny, according to the article. It says they are struggling to find agreement among themselves on how to regulate AI. It also says Trump's approach is hands-off and that his potential vetoes imperil any legislation. The article does not include direct statements from the parties involved.

The context is the midterm elections, where the costs and risks of the AI boom became an issue for voters. The article says Democratic control of Congress is poised to ratchet up scrutiny, but it does not say what happens next beyond the obstacles of internal disagreement and possible vetoes. It does not give a timeline for any action. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI Giants to Come Under Fresh Scrutiny But New Rules Unlikely

stories.Headline: From Copilot to agents: Inside KPIT’s AI-powered marketing transformation
stories.Summary:
Mohit Kochar, Chief Marketing Officer of KPIT Technologies, and his team began experimenting with AI to help marketers spend less time gathering information and more time acting on it. What started as a productivity initiative grew into a broader transformation, with Microsoft 365 Copilot helping the team research faster and make more informed decisions. Kochar said he believed AI would fundamentally reshape organizations and functions, including marketing. He said Copilot now acts as an assistant, researcher, analyst and strategic thinking partner.

The marketing function at KPIT covers market intelligence, investor communications, proposal support, thought leadership, research and brand strategy. More than a year before the article, much of that work depended on reviewing industry developments and analyzing market signals. Microsoft 365 Copilot became a key part of the journey because it works within KPIT's existing Microsoft environment and draws context from Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and PowerPoint. Kochar said security and governance are critical because the firm works with sensitive customer intellectual property, and that Copilot gives the protection and enterprise controls needed while still enabling innovation. He added that the team no longer starts with a blank page.

As adoption matured, the team moved beyond copilots to purpose-driven agents. One competitor intelligence solution, built with Copilot and Power Automate, monitors 14 competitors and generates monthly reports with recommendations and threat assessments. Another helps account teams prepare for OEM conversations by combining public evidence with internal knowledge into a revenue readiness report that ranks winnable opportunities and sets out a 30-60-90 day account plan. Copilot also helps the team mine a repository of more than 1,500 proposals produced each year. Kochar said this allows the team to identify competitive patterns, emerging technology trends, customer priorities and future skill requirements.

Kochar said the deeper shift is about people, because AI lowers barriers to knowledge and lets marketers contribute in ways that previously required years of specialized expertise. He said the promise of AI is not about replacing human capability but broadening it, and that Copilot is helping create a marketing function where generalists can come to the table with a point of view. He said the edge in B2B marketing lies in how quickly market signals become relevant customer conversations. He said the agent connects external OEM intelligence with KPIT's institutional knowledge, so the team spends less time gathering information and more time shaping proactive propositions.

Articles.Title: From Copilot to agents: Inside KPIT’s AI-powered marketing transformation

stories.Headline: Trump’s midterm defeat creates new uncertainty for AI stocks and Israel
stories.Summary:
The US midterm elections have delivered a severe defeat to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party, though vote counting is not yet complete. Democrats have won a majority in the Senate, and the House of Representatives appears to be heading the same way. Democrats currently hold 213 House seats and need just five more from the 96 races still undecided. After two years of unified Republican control, Trump will face a hostile Congress in January.

Markets reacted sharply, especially in Asia, where the sell-off centered on artificial intelligence stocks. Tokyo's Nikkei index fell more than 3% before moderating to about 1.5%, with SoftBank down about 7%, Advantest 6.4%, Tokyo Electron 5% and Kioxia 10%. Furukawa and Fujikura, suppliers to data centers, fell 9% and 8.2%, while Taiwan's exchange dropped 2.3% and Nasdaq futures retreated about 2%. Goldman Sachs' basket of AI stocks fell 15% in October and is more than 24% below its peak.

Investors fear a Democratic-controlled Congress could mean tighter regulation of AI and data centers, and a shift is also taking shape in Georgia, which with Texas accounts for about a third of data center investment. Technology investment accounts for about a third of US economic growth this year, reaching 36% in the second quarter, or about half under a broader definition that includes data center construction. Markets had priced a 77% probability of a December rate hike before the election. The 10-year Treasury yield fell 7 basis points to 4.89% overnight before climbing back to around 4.95%.

Trump told Fox News in a telephone interview that the US would end its annual aid to Israel, worth about $4 billion, by 2027, while continuing weapons sales. He said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had proposed the move and the two had reached an understanding some time ago. In the new Congress, 40 of the 47 Democratic senators voted last April to block a sale of bulldozers to the Israeli military, an indication of opposition to arms deals. The shekel has weakened about 3% since Israel's election day and trades above NIS 3.16.

Articles.Title: Trump’s midterm defeat creates new uncertainty for AI stocks and Israel

stories.Headline: Solving the wrong AI problem
stories.Summary:
The article on the Sandusky Register website, dated November 4, 2026, carries the headline "Solving the wrong AI problem." The page text does not describe any event, and it names no person or organization that did anything. Instead, it shows a notification saying the site could not verify a valid email address. It also tells the reader to visit a profile to update the email address or to disable notifications and hide the message. A further notice says the session could not be renewed and will expire in 0 seconds, with a link to try to renew it.

The page gives no requirements, changes, numbers or dates beyond the November 4, 2026 date and the 0 seconds figure. It names no responsible person and contains no statements from anyone about the subject in the headline. The only contact details are the paper's address at 314 West Market Street, Sandusky, Ohio 44870, and its phone number, 419-625-5500. The rest of the text is a copyright notice for The Sandusky Register.

The articles do not provide the context for the headline or say what happens next. They contain no information on who is responsible or what anyone said about artificial intelligence. Because the story is breaking and the available material is so limited, only what is known can be reported. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Solving the wrong AI problem

stories.Headline: Connecticut woman loses $7K in spoofing scam; expert warns of AI, payment apps
stories.Summary:
A 45-year-old woman from Windsor, Connecticut, said she lost more than $7,000 after a caller posing as a representative of 360 Federal Credit Union convinced her to transfer her savings through Apple Cash. The call appeared to come from the credit union’s real phone number, and the man said he worked in its fraud department. He told her that her banking information had been compromised and that her accounts needed to be secured. Over a weekend in August, she sent the money to an unknown account while believing she was following her credit union’s instructions. By Monday she found her account was negative and realized the money was gone.

The caller ID was apparently manipulated to show the credit union’s number, a practice known as spoofing. Steven Weisman, editor of Scamicide.com, said any unsophisticated scammer can do this and can hide the number they are actually calling from. The Federal Trade Commission said victims lost $3.5 billion through imposter scams in 2025, an increase of 300% since 2020. Weisman said scammers are also taking advantage of artificial intelligence and the ease of moving money through peer-to-peer payment services. The woman contacted Apple and Green Dot Bank, which provides Apple Cash services, to try to recover her money but was unsuccessful.

360 Federal Credit Union said it takes the security of its members and their financial information very seriously. It said it found no indication that the transaction resulted from a breach of its systems and that it has no evidence any transaction in the matter is the result of a cybersecurity incident. Green Dot Bank said it does not share details about specific customer accounts or circumstances, and that it uses real-time fraud warnings designed to help customers recognize common scams. The woman said she saw a warning message while making the payment, but the caller convinced her the alert was expected. Weisman said scam victims should not carry all the responsibility and that payment platforms should be held to protecting customers.

The credit union and Green Dot Bank both said customers should never share bank account information, passwords, PINs, verification codes, or other sensitive financial or security information based on unsolicited calls, texts, or emails. The articles advise people not to rely solely on caller ID to judge whether a call is legitimate. Before sharing sensitive information or transferring money, people should tell the caller they will hang up and call back, then find the organization’s legitimate phone number independently and contact it directly. The articles do not say what happens next in the woman’s case.

Articles.Title: Connecticut woman loses $7K in spoofing scam; expert warns of AI, payment apps

stories.Headline: Shadow AI: What Risks It Poses and How to Manage It in the Workplace
stories.Summary:
Telefónica published an article on November 4, 2026, about Shadow AI, which it describes as the use of artificial intelligence tools, models, or agents without the visibility, authorization, or control of an organization's technology, security, privacy, or compliance teams. The article says this use often does not come from malicious intent but from a desire to automate tasks, analyze information, or work more quickly. It presents a fictional story in which a CISO named Daniel, at a costume party, hears from colleagues dressed as Freddy Krueger, Dracula, Frankenstein, and Michael Myers about customer data uploaded to a public generative AI tool, sales forecasts entered into an AI assistant, an AI agent connected to a contract repository with access to everything, and an autonomous agent consuming millions of tokens. A CFO then appears with a five-figure bill, the head of legal asks about personal data processing, the CEO wants explanations, and a special audit is announced.

The article says entering personal data, financial forecasts, contracts, or other corporate information into unauthorized AI tools can make it difficult to control how that data is processed, accessed, stored, and potentially exposed. It says an AI agent with broad permissions can access more information than necessary, interact with different systems, and perform actions without sufficient oversight. It says AI tools and agents without limits on consumption, oversight, or authorization criteria can lead to unexpected costs and raise concerns about data protection, security, internal liabilities, and compliance with regulations including the General Data Protection Regulation and the European Artificial Intelligence Regulation. It says the solution is not to slow down AI adoption but to establish governance, security, and control mechanisms.

The article says companies can reduce the risks by gaining visibility into the tools being used, protecting sensitive information, implementing access controls, limiting permissions, monitoring connections, and tracking agent activity and usage. It says organizations should know which AI tools are used, for what purpose, what information they process, and which systems they can access, and should set clear criteria for approving tools and classify the information that can be entered into them. It says the principle of least privilege is especially important for AI agents, so each agent should have access only to the information and functions necessary for its task. It says Telefónica, using its cybersecurity capabilities and working with technology partners, supports companies with measures including visibility into AI tools, protection of sensitive information, controls over APIs and Model Context Protocol connections, limited permissions for AI agents, activity monitoring, and governance and compliance policies.

Articles.Title: Shadow AI: What Risks It Poses and How to Manage It in the Workplace

stories.Headline: Google defends school AI rules amid political criticism (GOOG:NASDAQ)
stories.Summary:
Google is facing political criticism over a new policy on the use of artificial intelligence in schools. The company set out its position in a blog post titled “Designing responsible AI for learning.” In that post, Google said it is bringing AI into its Classroom product. The criticism followed the introduction of the policy.

A report said Google will turn off Search for schools that reject AI. Google said schools control whether AI tools are enabled. Its response did not directly address whether Search access requires AI use. Google also said AI Mode and AI Overviews will give step-by-step guided learning through problems, which is meant to stop students from getting quick answers to schoolwork.

A Wall Street Journal investigation reported that students had become emotionally and academically dependent on AI. That finding came from interviews with teachers, school officials, parents, children and clinicians. Google is the company responsible for the policy and it defended the rules in its blog post. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Google defends school AI rules amid political criticism (GOOG:NASDAQ)

stories.Headline: Why taste, conviction, foresight, and courage are the traits we need in the age of AI
stories.Summary:
The article is an opinion piece by an author who has spent four decades building AI, published on fastcompany.com on November 4, 2026. The author argues that AI is not the Fourth Industrial Revolution but the first and last intelligence revolution, because the cost collapse now applies to cognition itself. The author recalls asking Hans Moravec, then director of the Mobile Robot Laboratory at Carnegie Mellon University, what would become of human meaning if machines grew smarter than people. Moravec replied by asking why the author assumed human meaning must rest on humans being the smartest. The article names four traits it says humans need in the AI era: taste, foresight, conviction, and courage.

For taste it points to Coco Chanel, who sensed that women's clothing of her era was confining and asked whether it could be as comfortable as men's clothing and still desirable. For conviction it points to Jeff Bezos, noting that Barron's ran a cover story titled "Amazon.bomb" in 1999 while he kept reinvesting profits. For foresight it points to Steve Jobs, from the personal computer and graphical interface to the iPod and the App Store, and for courage to Elon Musk, who put nearly all his PayPal money into Tesla, SolarCity, and SpaceX. The article says SpaceX failed three Falcon 1 launches in a row by 2008, and the fourth, its last chance, succeeded, leading to a $1.6 billion NASA contract a few months later. It says Tesla was days from bankruptcy in 2008 before a rescuing financing round on Christmas Eve.

The author says AI models tend toward the most acceptable answer, or the answer their user wants, and that alignment pushes them further toward a safe middle. The author adds that nothing happens to a model that was wrong, so it has no consequence and no courage. The article says these traits run counter to the machinery of AI and will remain human strengths. It acknowledges survivorship bias, noting that the named pioneers are generational and that many entrepreneurs with courage and conviction were wrong and faced ruin. It gives no further plans or next steps.

Articles.Title: Why taste, conviction, foresight, and courage are the traits we need in the age of AI

stories.Headline: 'We would use this dip to buy': A CIO says load up on these 8 beaten-down AI stocks poised to rebound
stories.Summary:
David Katz, the chief investment officer of Matrix Asset Advisers, said in comments to Business Insider on Tuesday that the recent pullback in AI stocks is a buying opportunity. The sell-off began in October and pushed the Nasdaq 100 toward correction territory. Katz said the de-risking was sentiment-driven and would soon reverse. He said the selling had created the opportunity and that his firm would use the dip to buy.

Katz named eight AI-related stocks he would buy for a potential rebound over 12 to 18 months. Four are picks-and-shovels plays: Applied Materials, Generac, Qualcomm and TE Connectivity. The other four are hyperscalers: Alphabet, Meta Platforms, Microsoft and Amazon. The article lists October 2026 returns for each, ranging from a 23.7% drop for Applied Materials to a 1.8% gain for Microsoft, along with 2027 estimated price-to-earnings ratios.

Katz said Applied Materials has a robust business and a pipeline of at least two to three years. He said Generac has added backup generators for data centers and scored two very large contracts. He said Qualcomm could be number two in robotics behind Tesla and SpaceX, and that its stock had fallen from about $235 to $165. He said TE Connectivity's business has kept growing despite concerns about a shift to fiber optic connections.

On the hyperscalers, Katz said Alphabet's management is trustworthy and spends wisely. He said he does not trust Meta's spending discipline as much, citing its Metaverse flub, but called its Muse AI agent a game changer given its 3 billion users. He said Microsoft and Amazon have responsible management and would benefit if AI spending pulls back. The article does not say what happens next beyond Katz's 12- to 18-month timeline.

Articles.Title: 'We would use this dip to buy': A CIO says load up on these 8 beaten-down AI stocks poised to rebound

stories.Headline: Tencent steps up AI investment to create broader social value
stories.Summary:
Tencent increased its research and development spending to 27.28 billion yuan, or about 4.1 billion dollars, in the second quarter of 2026, up 35 percent from a year earlier. Capital expenditure rose 176 percent year-on-year and 65 percent quarter-on-quarter to 52.78 billion yuan, which the company linked to more investment in artificial intelligence. By the end of June 2026, Tencent had published more than 98,000 patent applications and secured over 55,000 patent grants across major countries and regions. These patents cover AI, cloud computing, mobility and instant messaging.

Tencent uses a dual-track strategy of proprietary development and open source for its models. Since rebuilding its infrastructure in February 2026, its Hunyuan large language model has released a major update about every two months, including Hy3 preview, the official Hy3 release and Hy4 preview this year. Hy3 has a smaller parameter size but performs comparably to flagship models with two to five times as many parameters, and since its July launch it has ranked among the world's top three models by token consumption. Hy4 preview expanded its model size, context length and training data, was fully open-sourced on release and keeps affordable pricing, and the next Hy4 model is expected soon.

Tencent aims to make AI agents digital companions for its 1.4 billion users and a new source of productivity across industries. Its productivity agents WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy are growing quickly, and according to Analysys, WorkBuddy recorded 85.34 million monthly visits in September 2026, leading China's desktop AI office agent market. Combined visits for the two products exceeded 110 million, and WorkBuddy launched an open platform covering hardware, Buddy apps, experts, skills and connectors with more than 100 partners at launch. WeCom has launched its AI assistant Dayuan, Weixin's native AI assistant Xiaowei is expanding closed beta testing, and Yuanbao Search is now available to individual developers and enterprises through Tencent Cloud.

Tencent has made promoting sustainable innovations for social value a core development strategy, using digital technology and its platforms to address social needs. With the Jingdezhen authorities it developed Digital Jingdezhen: Porcelain Craft Adventure, described as the world's first mini-game themed around a World Heritage nomination, launched on July 25, 2026. The simulation game recreates key stages of Jingdezhen's porcelain industry during the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties from 960 to 1911. It combines AI-generated 3D porcelain, interactive AI-powered non-player characters and AI-powered procedural content generation to recreate historical scenes, letting players explore traditional porcelain-making techniques and the city's ceramic heritage.

Articles.Title: Tencent steps up AI investment to create broader social value - China Daily

stories.Headline: Abnormal AI's new CMO says 'safe is boring' and is ditching the B2B marketing playbook
stories.Summary:
Abnormal AI told CMO Insider on Wednesday that it has appointed Don Jeter as its chief marketing officer. The cybersecurity startup, founded in 2018, made its name using behavioral AI to detect email security threats. It has since expanded the technology to spot unusual activity in employees' digital accounts and logins, and is increasingly applying the same approach to securing organizations' use of AI tools. The company was valued at $5.1 billion after a $250 million Series D funding round in 2024.

Jeter said he intends to throw out the traditional business-to-business marketing playbook, which often focuses on features and functions. Instead, he plans to create cultural moments aimed at consumers beyond Abnormal's CISO target audience. He said out-of-home advertising and other real-world activations are likely to play key roles, though he kept specific plans under wraps for now. He also said one of his near-term challenges is resetting the narrative that Abnormal is only an email security company.

Jeter said he wants his 14-year-old nephew and his parents to know Abnormal, and that he wants it to be the most talked-about cybersecurity company in 2027. He said trust and awareness must be built before the sales conversation starts, and that good brand marketing makes everything else easier. He said B2B marketing has played it safe for a very long time, and that safe is boring and boring is invisible. As CMO of cybersecurity startup Torq, he built the brand through deliberately offbeat campaigns, including sponsoring Monster Jam's nationwide tour and bringing a 20-foot inflatable skeleton and an on-site tattoo bus to the 2026 RSAC cybersecurity conference.

Steve Nottingham, CEO of the commerce experience agency RSM&, said a B2B buyer is still a person who remembers a great story, and that real-world connection gives people a reason to remember one brand over another. He said CMOs who want to execute these activations need a clear objective, an idea that could only come from their brand, a defined audience, a parallel content strategy and measurement that connects buzz to brand awareness and the sales pipeline. The article said B2B brands are increasingly taking a more business-to-consumer marketing approach, citing Salesforce and Adobe conferences, Autodesk's sports team partnerships and Las Vegas Sphere advertising, and a Ramp campaign with former pro skater Tony Hawk. Jeter will be competing for mindshare against trillion-dollar tech giants, buzzy frontier AI companies and other cybersecurity vendors jostling for chief information security officers' budgets.

Articles.Title: Abnormal AI's new CMO says 'safe is boring' and is ditching the B2B marketing playbook

stories.Headline: Smart Tech Is Not a Strategy: Why Relying on AI Alone Could Risk the Wealth You Built
stories.Summary:
Mark Clark, a certified financial planner, wrote an article published on 4 November 2026 by Kiplinger arguing that artificial intelligence is not a substitute for a sound financial strategy. He compared AI to a new golf club, saying better equipment cannot fix a bad swing. Clark said the tools are genuinely impressive and can model things like a Roth conversion or compare two funds in seconds.
