stories.Headline: Microsoft India pay hikes disappoint employees, survey finds
stories.Summary:
A survey by the professional networking platform Blind found that 91 per cent of Microsoft employees in India received salary increases of 5 per cent or less in 2026. Only 5 per cent of respondents received increments above 10 per cent, down from 27 per cent in the previous appraisal cycle. In 2025, 45 per cent had received hikes of 5 per cent or less, which shows a large shift in the latest results. The findings were published on November 4, 2026.

The survey also found that 86 per cent of employees expressed unhappiness with their salary hikes. This placed Microsoft among the lowest-rated employers in the survey, with only Zoho recording more dissatisfaction. The appraisal results came at the same time as Microsoft's Voluntary Exit Offer, announced by Chief People Officer Amy Coleman. The programme covers about 60,000 employees globally, including workers in India, the US, Canada and the UK.

The articles say Microsoft reported a 32 per cent year-on-year rise in net income to $36.6 billion for the July to September quarter. Revenue rose 19 per cent to $92.3 billion, Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30 per cent to $63.9 billion, and Azure revenue rose 48 per cent in the same period. The company expects revenue of up to $97.1 billion in the current quarter and plans capital expenditure above $50 billion for AI infrastructure. Searches by Indian users on Blind about buyouts and voluntary exit programmes rose 60 per cent over the past year, and the share of searches about layoffs and severance rose from 16 per cent to 21 per cent.

The survey also looked at what employees believe drives appraisal outcomes across India's technology workforce. It found that 41 per cent of respondents attributed outcomes to company financial performance or cost-cutting measures. Another 18 per cent pointed to changing business priorities linked to AI and automation. The articles describe the gap between financial performance and employee compensation as drawing attention to how companies manage workforce costs during technological transformation.

Articles.Title: Microsoft India pay hikes disappoint employees, survey finds

stories.Headline: Evernote turns AI-driven discovery into paid subscriptions
stories.Summary:
Evernote used ChatGPT Ads to reach people who already work with AI, and it followed new users from a free trial through to their first subscription payment. The campaigns ran with trials starting between August 28 and September 12, 2026, and the desktop registration figures covered September 14 to 28, 2026. Evernote compared those results with its historical paid-acquisition average from March to August 2026. The company treated the first-month results as encouraging and directional rather than final.

Evernote's core ChatGPT Ads campaigns focused on a single product feature. About 25% of desktop visits from those campaigns led to a new Evernote account in the first month. New users from the same campaigns converted from free trial to paid subscription at a rate about 10 to 20% higher than its historical paid-acquisition average. The ads sent people to Evernote's website, including its homepage, and the campaigns were optimized for new-account registrations. Evernote noted that the comparison does not establish incremental lift.

Claudio Di Blasi, a Data Analyst at Bending Spoons, said the challenge is helping new users see enough value to become paying customers. He said Evernote needs to show people what the product can do and give them a clear reason to start using it. He also said the early results stood out for how well new users converted to paid subscriptions. He described that as an encouraging sign that Evernote was reaching people who found real value in the product.

Evernote's starting point was a practical need to keep information useful after it has been created, since people working with conversations, notes, and transcriptions may want a place to organize that material and find it again. Its initial ads highlighted Evernote as a place to save and organize notes and transcriptions, drawing on messaging from strong-performing search campaigns. Evernote plans to explore additional use cases and develop creative and dedicated landing pages that show how the product fits into people's own work. The company is testing whether the performance can hold as the channel grows.

Articles.Title: Evernote turns AI-driven discovery into paid subscriptions

stories.Headline: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind announced on November 3, 2026 that it had built a set of Cheminformatics Skills for Google Antigravity, its agentic coding tool, and shown the agent carrying out a drug discovery workflow. The work was described by Zoi Tsangalidou, Ruijie (Kelly) Zhang, Sukhdeep Singh and Michael V. LeVine. Using real-world lung cancer treatments, the agent searched through thousands of compounds, performed matched molecular pair analysis, and proposed new rigidified macrocycles with synthetic routes in about an hour. The same workflow would typically take multiple days for a single iteration.

The skills are grounded in RDKit, the open source cheminformatics toolkit developed over two decades, with connectors to ChEMBL and PubChem. In the demonstration, the agent retrieved thousands of compounds within minutes, filtered out irrelevant molecules such as buffers and solvents, and documented their sources in a report. It launched an interactive viewer for browsing compounds and plotting potency against rotatable bonds, then ran matched molecular pair analysis comparing molecules that differ by whether they are cyclized. The agent also built and validated many potency models across four experimental read outs, using a scaffold split to gauge out-of-distribution performance. The skills are available on Google Antigravity now, through the Antigravity App and its Science plugin, and Enterprise users can log in with Google Cloud credentials.

The authors said the language model handles workflow orchestration, database navigation and scientific reasoning, while deterministic chemistry tools execute molecular calculations. They said the skills encode domain best practices directly into the agent's workflow, and that the aim is to let scientists focus on hypotheses rather than data wrangling. They also set limits on what the tools can do, saying sparse data, inter-lab assay noise and narrow dynamic ranges limit predictive precision, and that computational designs are testable hypotheses, not finished drugs. Every proposed design must be synthesized and validated experimentally, they said.

The article frames the work around rigidification, a classic medicinal chemistry technique, citing crizotinib, a first-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor with five major rotatable bonds, and lorlatinib, a third-generation inhibitor cyclized at its end to reduce the effective number of rotatable bonds to zero. The agent's matched molecular pair analysis showed that cyclization reduces rotatable bonds while generally increasing potency. The agent proposed designs with electron-pushing diagrams and synthesis routes, and the results can be exported in various formats for industry standard chemistry software. DeepMind is offering 10,000 scientists the highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months, onboarded on a rolling basis and subject to eligibility, capacity and selection, with applications now open.

Articles.Title: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity

stories.Headline: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
stories.Summary:
The Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) introduced StateBench on November 3, 2026, a benchmark for long-context state tracking, which measures how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as that information evolves. The work was announced in a blog post by Kyle Wiggers of Ai2Comms. State tracking underlies tasks such as reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, and following a story as characters move and objects change hands. The team says existing state-tracking tests tend to focus on the hardest cases, and researchers need to know which kinds of state tracking each architecture can handle.

StateBench has four difficulty levels of increasing complexity. R-trivial problems use immutable assignment, aperiodic problems allow reassignment by value, soluble problems add self-referential updates, and general finite problems add assignment by reference. The levels are rooted in Krohn, Rhodes theory, and to compare them fairly the team derives three easier versions from one general finite sequence, so all four use the same number of variables and values with assignments at the same points. The team tested open pretrained models including two 7-billion-parameter models, Olmo 3 (a transformer) and Olmo Hybrid (which adds Gated DeltaNet layers), plus smaller models with 275 million and 2.7 billion parameters, all pretrained on the same data and none having seen contexts longer than 64,000 tokens.

The team also tested four frontier models, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna. All four did well on r-trivial and aperiodic problems, but on soluble and general finite problems accuracy fell sharply as inputs grew longer, dropping to 13% or lower on the longest general finite problems. The team then trained several 275-million-parameter models from scratch on sequences of up to 256 assignments and tested them on sequences as long as 64,000 assignments, 250 times the maximum training length. Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models generalized almost perfectly on the first three levels out to tens of thousands of assignments, while transformers degraded on longer sequences and never learned general finite problems.

The team says the gap for Gated DeltaNet and hybrid models points to training rather than architecture, since trained directly they learned levels their pretrained counterparts could not, while transformers could never learn the hardest level even when trained directly. Some questions remain open, including the exact placement of Gated DeltaNet with a more limited memory update in the hierarchy and whether it can solve all soluble tasks. StateBench also assumes a fixed number of variables, while real tasks often introduce new entities over time, a setting the current framework does not yet cover. The team hopes StateBench gives researchers a finer-grained way to find where models break down and serves as a guide for developing new architectures with more robust state-tracking abilities.

Articles.Title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents

stories.Headline: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
stories.Summary:
IBM Research released Palette on November 3, 2026, a 20B open-weight model that builds slide decks in a chosen design language. The team fine-tuned the model with a LoRA adapter so it works in two roles, a designer that writes a structured brief and a coder that writes the JavaScript for each slide. The training data was synthetic, about 1,000 decks and roughly 10,000 slides, generated by a large open teacher and checked by a harness. The model follows the IBM Design Language, and on PresentBench it ranked first on two of the three domains measured.

Palette splits deck building into a designer role and a coder role, both served by one adapter. The designer writes a JSON brief with the palette, the type system and each slide's layout, content and rationale, and the coder turns one slide's spec into pptxgenjs code. Because each slide's context is fixed before coding starts, the coder runs in parallel, making that stage about 6 to 7 times faster. Users can add directives in double brackets, such as making something a timeline, and the model was trained on directives from 12 categories. Every deck then passes through a harness that renders each slide, flags overlaps, clipping and overflow, and sends flagged slides to an editor model.

A rewrite is kept only if the checker confirms the slide improved, otherwise the original stays. Across 131 decks the harness added 3.5 points on average. On PresentBench, Palette placed second across the three domains with 59.7 against NotebookLM's 60.8, ranking first on Economics and Education and third on Talk. The authors said the worst failure is a slide with facts not in the input, and that fixing reference decks changed the teacher's output far more than adding prompt rules. They also said coder examples were about 5 times longer than designer examples, so they oversampled the designer's examples 5 times.

The authors describe PresentBench as measuring whether a deck is good, not whether it follows a specific design language, and they say they are not aware of a benchmark that does. Next they want to use the harness checks as rewards for reinforcement learning, so the model stops making these mistakes in the first place. They also want to improve figure-heavy decks by extracting figures from source documents, for example with Docling, and placing them with the harness. They are exploring a lighter way to bring your own templates by re-skinning output from one or two existing .pptx files without retraining.

Articles.Title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language

stories.Headline: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
stories.Summary:
Collinear AI released CWE-bench v2 on November 3, 2026, a public set of 100 tasks for testing frontier cyber capabilities. In each task an agent gets a checkout of a real open-source repository and a short instruction, and must find and fix a security weakness without breaking existing functionality. Scoring is fully programmatic, so results are deterministic and reproducible at no extra cost. The programmatic checks were curated with the help of LLM judge panels, and a held-out set is kept so progress can be tracked on tasks no model has seen.

The 100 tasks cover 91 different CWEs. For every task the team checked that the instruction reads realistically, that every graded behaviour can be inferred from it, that the verifier checks correct behaviour rather than one fix's structure, that the starter code fails and the reference fix passes, that original functionality still works, and that verifiers fail memorized solutions such as the known upstream patch. Every task was also reviewed by hand. Each task is a self-contained Harbor task with a Dockerized environment, an instruction and a deterministic verifier, and the dataset ships a registry.json so Harbor can run the whole benchmark from the Hugging Face repo. The dataset is gated, so users must accept its access conditions first, and the tasks are tagged rl-environment so the same environments and verifiers can provide rewards for training defensive agents.

Results are tracked in two places on the Hub. The leaderboard on the CWE-bench dataset page covers open-weight models and updates on its own, with labs and the community adding a result by opening a PR on the model's repo with a results file. The CWE-bench leaderboard Space holds the full comparison, including API-only models such as Gemini, Claude and GPT, with new models added through a PR on the Space. Of the 11 models evaluated, Gemini 4 Argon leads with 67.8% pass@1 and 81.0% pass@4, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 67.3% pass@1 and 78.0% pass@4. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon form the Pareto frontier on cost: DeepSeek reaches 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04 per rollout, Opus adds ten points at $1.83, and Gemini edges ahead at $3.92.

The team says its goal is to be exhaustive, since a defender has to anticipate how an attacker could get in and get it right every time, and that recognizing a familiar pattern is not enough. 95 tasks are solved by at least one model, which indicates the tasks are solvable, but even the leader fails 19% of the set on every attempt, so the long tail is far from solved. The public set, the grader and the harness are open, and the team invites people to run their model and report where it stands. It welcomes feedback on any task and contributions to the public set, and asks those who want to evaluate on the held-out set to contact cyber@collinear.ai.

Articles.Title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency

stories.Headline: Search Advertising “Will Top as an Industry in Q1,” Says Ex-Stability AI CEO. Alphabet Has the Most to Lose
stories.Summary:
Alphabet stock fell nearly 19% in October, its worst month since its 2004 IPO, after third-quarter Search revenue missed estimates. The drop included a 13% plunge the day after the report. Then Emad Mostaque, the former CEO of Stability AI, said on Peter Diamandis's Moonshots podcast that search advertising will peak as an industry in the first quarter of next year. He was discussing AI agents that shop for people, and he argued those agents hit the main business of both Google and Meta Platforms.

Search & other brought in 55.7% of Alphabet's revenue in 2025, and it rose 12% to $63.4 billion in the third quarter, down from 17% growth in the second quarter. CEO Sundar Pichai said query growth was the highest in five years, while Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler blamed the slowdown partly on currency and partly on lower monetization in AI Mode. By Google's own figures, the share of searches ending in AI Mode went from 2% to 8.9%. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, up 103%, and Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capex in the quarter, with free cash flow at negative $9.1 billion.

Mostaque made the call on the podcast, and venture capitalist Dave Blundin said on the same episode that Alphabet is transitioning from a search advertising company to a hyperscaler cloud company. Ranjan Roy said a compute provider business model cannot have the same attractive economics as search advertising. CFO Anat Ashkenazi said lapping last year's search acceleration will pressure revenue growth in the fourth quarter, and she expects capex to increase significantly in 2027. Analysts' consensus has normalized EPS rising from $10.81 in 2025 to $18.26 by 2028, with a dip to $15.18 in 2027.

Alphabet trades at 20x forward earnings, below its ten-year average of 24x, and it hit 16x as recently as April 2025. The first quarter ends March 31, so Mostaque's call comes due quickly. Fourth-quarter results in early February will show how much search growth is pressured, along with the 2027 capex figure. Alphabet reports its first quarter, likely in late April, and that will show whether Mostaque was right.

Articles.Title: Search Advertising “Will Top as an Industry in Q1,” Says Ex-Stability AI CEO. Alphabet Has the Most to Lose - TIKR.com

stories.Headline: UK has trust in AI Security Institute's frontier model access, minister says
stories.Summary:
The UK's AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, said on Tuesday that the country remains confident about access to US frontier AI models for pre-deployment safety testing. He spoke at an event and pointed to the technical capabilities of the AI Security Institute. He also cited government efforts to build trust with US authorities and companies. The comments were reported by MLex on November 3, 2026.

Narayan warned that the technology could intensify threats to democratic integrity. He expressed concern about hostile states and proxy actors interfering in the UK's democratic debate. He said the AI Security Institute is well placed to keep its access to frontier models for testing. The article does not give further details on the access arrangements or any changes.

The minister credited the institute's technical capabilities as one reason for his confidence. He also credited the government's work to build trust with US authorities and companies. The article does not say what the institute's testing involves or which models it covers. It also does not name any US agencies or companies involved.

The article gives no further context on what happens next. It does not say whether access has been questioned or whether any agreement is in place. It reports only the minister's remarks at the Tuesday event. No response from US authorities or companies is included.

Articles.Title: UK has trust in AI Security Institute's frontier model access, minister says - MLex

stories.Headline: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights
stories.Summary:
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team released FlashProve on November 3, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. It is an open-source research prototype for provable inference, built as a zkSNARK system. It proves that a reply came from a committed model without revealing anything about the weights. On Llama 4 Maverick, a 400B mixture-of-experts model, it proves about 110 tokens per second on one H100.

The system has a prover, the model provider, and a verifier, the user. Offline, the provider publishes a commitment, a short fingerprint binding one exact set of weights, which takes about 39 minutes and covers about 16 million requests. Online, the GPU produces a proof for each request that the committed model produced those tokens. Context is capped at 1,024 tokens per request, and the prover needs one H100 80 GB, 24 CPU cores and about 290 GB of host RAM, while the verifier runs on a CPU with no GPU.

Proofs are 18.78 MB and verify in 17 seconds on 24 threads, or 21 seconds on one thread. A batch of 24 reached 111.23 tokens per second at about 221 to 226 seconds per batch, a batch of 1 reached 17.41 tokens per second, and a batch of 64 reached 123.31 tokens per second but was flagged as unreliable on 80 GB cards. Proving costs about 70 to 95 times the GPU time of plain vLLM inference, or about 72 times per batch against vLLM running FP8 Maverick on 8 H100s, rising to about 94 times at vLLM's highest tested load. The code is open under Apache 2.0.

Anthropic says the proof system compiles an interactive oracle proof into a cryptographic proof using hash functions, which it says offers post-quantum security, the same family used by validity-proof L2 networks such as Starknet. Three engineering choices drive the speed: prover work scales with the roughly 17B active parameters rather than all 400B, requests are proved in batches after the fact like prefill, and weights stream from host memory so a single 80 GB GPU suffices. Anthropic formalized the protocol in Lean and proves completeness, soundness and zero knowledge. The article says the work targets a real gap, since today you cannot check which model actually answered your API call, and it lists uses such as regulators confirming hardware serves inference, labs detecting tampered inference servers, and regulators enforcing approved models only.

Articles.Title: Anthropic Releases FlashProve: Cryptographic Proofs That a Reply Came From Committed Weights

stories.Headline: NVIDIA Shows 3 Ways to Speed Up MoE Inference on DGX Spark, Lifting Ling-3.0-flash Throughput 42.5%
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA published a technical blog post on November 3, 2026, showing three ways to speed up mixture-of-experts inference on a single DGX Spark desktop system. The test model was Ling-3.0-flash from Ant Group inclusionAI, a 124B-parameter MoE with 5.1B active parameters and a 256K native context. NVIDIA combined a new MoE kernel backend, an FP8 output layer and built-in speculative decoding. Across all 1,319 GSM8K questions, decode throughput rose 42.5% with no statistically detectable accuracy change.

The DGX Spark runs on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip with 128 GB of unified memory and 273 GB/s of memory bandwidth. The baseline used FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernels and an FP32 LM-head path, running at 27.71 ms per token, or 36.09 tokens per second, on a synthetic 32K-input, 2K-output test. The first change swapped in Humming, an independent kernel library that compiles kernels at runtime, lifting throughput 9.3% to 39.45 tokens per second. The second quantized only the LM head to FP8 at load time, which reached 43.94 tokens per second when combined with Humming.

The third change used Ling-3.0-flash's built-in NEXTN prediction layer for speculative decoding, with no extra draft model needed. It drafts three tokens and verifies four positions at once, and on the synthetic test an average of 3.90 tokens were accepted per round, pushing throughput to 102.88 tokens per second, up 185.1%. On GSM8K the gains shrank as acceptance dropped from 3.90 to 2.68, and the final result was 53.89 tokens per second versus 37.81 at baseline. That works out to 42.5% higher throughput and 24.5% lower mean latency, with accuracy flat at 96.89% versus 96.82%.

NVIDIA's team profiled the model at batch size one and found decoding was memory-bound, with the MoE computation and the LM head standing out as the main costs. The post notes the three techniques do not overlap, since Humming and the FP8 LM head cut the cost of each step while MTP cuts the number of steps. It also warns of an integration trap, because with both the FP8 LM head and MTP on, the draft must share the full LM-head module or the framework silently falls back. In that case the draft reads FP8 weights as BF16, accept length drops to 1.00 and throughput falls below the unoptimized baseline.

Articles.Title: NVIDIA Shows 3 Ways to Speed Up MoE Inference on DGX Spark, Lifting Ling-3.0-flash Throughput 42.5%

stories.Headline: Soniox STT v6 Adds Agent Text Input and Echo Filtering for Voice Agents
stories.Summary:
Soniox released Soniox STT v6, the latest generation of its speech-to-text API, on November 3, 2026. The model reads what a voice agent says while it hears the caller, and it uses that text to recognize short replies and to drop the agent's own voice. It ships as stt-rt-v6 for streaming and stt-async-v6 for files, across more than 60 languages. Soniox calls it significantly more accurate than v5, but it has published no v6 numbers yet.

The release costs $0.12 per hour for streaming and $0.10 per hour for async, with diarization and language ID bundled. Agent text input is turned on with one flag in the start request, "enable_agent_text_input": true, and it is only available on stt-rt-v6, not the async model. While the agent speaks, its words are streamed on the same WebSocket as the caller's audio, in small JSON frames with no timestamps. Soniox recommends sending each piece 500 ms to 1 second before playback, paced by TTS timestamps.

With agent text input on, v6 uses the agent's words to separate leftover agent audio from caller speech and filter it out. It keeps listening during playback, so callers can still interrupt, and it does not replace acoustic echo cancellation, so existing AEC should stay on. The model also improves voice typing of numbers, currencies, units, dates, IDs, names and specialized terms, and it writes spoken commands like "period" or "new line" as words. One formatting change to test is that v6 writes "15 dollars and 20 cents" as spoken, not as $15.20.

Soniox has not published v6 accuracy or latency numbers, and its benchmarks page still reports v5 on the open-source Pipecat STT benchmark. On that benchmark, stt-rt-v5 scores 1.34% semantic WER, 83.3% perfect transcripts and 260 ms median TTFS, with P95 latency of 305 ms. Azure posts the lowest WER mean at 1.21%, but at 1,016 ms median latency. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Soniox STT v6 Adds Agent Text Input and Echo Filtering for Voice Agents

stories.Headline: Professor James Whittington and Dr Ruairidh Battleday unveil breakthrough from stealth frontier AI lab
stories.Summary:
Professor James Whittington and Dr Ruairidh Battleday, cofounders of the stealth AI research lab Prefrontal, released new research on how AI systems can process very large amounts of information. Their paper introduces Latent Sparse Attention, a method that groups related information by meaning rather than by its position in a sequence. The method achieves up to 72.4x faster attention-layer prefill at 10m tokens of context compared with full attention, while keeping comparable accuracy. It also reaches 22.7x faster prefill than an existing sparse-attention approach and up to 9.2x faster time to first token in an end-to-end model-serving evaluation. The 72.4-fold gain applies only to attention-layer processing, not to the performance of a whole AI system.

The research follows DiG-bench, a benchmark by Battleday, Whittington and an international team that asks whether AI systems can genuinely discover new rules. Its 70 interactive games challenge AI agents to explore unfamiliar environments, experiment and infer hidden rules. Every game was solved by at least one human on a first attempt, while even the strongest AI agents failed a substantial proportion of the challenges. The benchmark reached more than 1m views on social media. Prefrontal describes the two publications as addressing complementary challenges, discovering new information and processing the knowledge needed for scientific work.

Whittington is a computational neuroscientist and AI researcher at the University of Oxford, where he is a Principal Investigator in the Department of Experimental Psychology. He studied physics, medicine and neuroscience at Oxford and held a Sir Henry Wellcome Fellowship at Stanford University. Battleday is a British cognitive scientist, AI researcher and entrepreneur who trained in medicine at Oxford and completed a PhD in Computer Science at Princeton University before research at Harvard. The two also cofounded Thinking About Thinking, an independent nonprofit research and education organisation established in 2020. It connects researchers through conferences, seminars, a Fellowship and an Ambassador Programme across institutions including Oxford, Cambridge, UCL, Imperial College London, Stanford, MIT and Princeton.

Thinking About Thinking will host the AE Global Summit 2026, Open Problems for AI, from 25 to 27 November at Friends House in London. The three-day event will bring together researchers, AI companies, entrepreneurs, investors and policymakers. The programme includes speakers from Google DeepMind, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oxford University, Imperial College London and UCL, alongside an AI Startup Competition offering a £5,000 prize. The launch was announced on X and LinkedIn.

Articles.Title: Professor James Whittington and Dr Ruairidh Battleday unveil breakthrough from stealth frontier AI lab

stories.Headline: Photonics mapped: 74 European startups using light to power the AI era
stories.Summary:
Sifted published a map of 74 European startups working in photonics on 3 November 2026, according to the article. The piece says the AI boom is hitting a physical limit, with chips, cables and components in data centres struggling to handle the volume of data and the speed of processing that ever more capable AI systems need. It describes photonics as turning photons into what it calls Europe's next deeptech export, from optical chips to laser weapons. The article was written by Ruggero Di Spigna, a Senior Insights and Product Associate at Sifted.

The article gives several funding figures for companies in the space. It says photonics startups raised €7.7bn across 4414 deals, citing Dealroom, with €5.9bn of that in 5777 deals, up from 6319 deals (€121m) and 9361 deals (€998m) in earlier years. It names investors including IS-wlaka Slrb, which put €441m into Kptlen Z and Kiumah, and €071m into Jqxjyn T and Wcsrxfxp. It also names Dcvcczel Intb, €026m into Ldorwl Q and Ybxmasm, €239m into Ozouzn K and Llyronesz, and €45m into Qovqep M in 9721. The article attributes responsibility for the sector's direction to the founders and investors it lists, and paraphrases their positions. It says Fnvwhz's Otslkgv put in €22m, and Trrnkwc's Ukwwh Mbfhqdqsjnkxb put in €759m across 1891. stories.Headline: Anthropic IPO Eve: How Do Large Language Model Businesses Build Sustainable, Profitable Financial Models?
stories.Summary:
Anthropic publicly submitted an S-1 prospectus to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and plans to list on the NASDAQ, according to a report from eu.36kr.com dated October 29, 2026. In the first half of 2026, the company's revenue reached 162.86 billion U.S. dollars, more than three times its full-year revenue for last year. In the second quarter of 2026, Anthropic recorded an operating profit of 974 million U.S. dollars, its first operating profitability in the disclosed quarterly data. The report says the large model business, previously seen as needing long-term capital burn, has begun to show the possibility of profitability.

The prospectus shows that in the first half of 2025, Anthropic had more than 600 customers contributing over 100,000 U.S. dollars in annual revenue, and that number exceeded 6,000 in the same period of 2026. About 80% of its revenue in the first half of 2026 came from usage-based billing, while subscription revenue accounted for 20%. As of the end of September, Anthropic had more than 1,900 customers contributing over 1 million U.S. dollars annually, of which about 250 contributed over 10 million U.S. dollars. The report says more than 80% of its third-quarter 2026 revenue came from new model versions released within the previous six months.

The report says Anthropic's computing power and infrastructure expenses fell from 201% of revenue in the first half of 2025 to 55% in the first half of 2026. It also says Anthropic has signed multi-year agreements related to computing power and infrastructure worth more than 600 billion U.S. dollars, including contracts with Amazon and Google involving consumption commitments of at least 110 billion U.S. dollars and 114.5 billion U.S. dollars respectively. The report says nearly half of Anthropic's revenue comes from cloud platform sales channels, where tech giants such as Amazon and Google both provide computing power and help sell models while competing with Claude for enterprise customers. It adds that many large customers are not bound by long-term contracts and can reduce or even stop their spending.

The report says Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 was as high as 807.48 billion U.S. dollars, while its operating loss in the same period was only 693 million U.S. dollars. It attributes the gap mainly to accounting treatment, including a book loss of about 724 billion U.S. dollars from fair value changes of financing instruments such as convertible bonds, which it says does not involve cash outflow of the same scale. The report says it is still difficult to judge whether the second-quarter profitability can be sustained, because Anthropic must keep investing in computing power and model prices face pressure from OpenAI, Google and open-source model manufacturers. It says that once revenue growth slows, a large amount of underutilized computing power may drag down profits.

Articles.Title: Anthropic IPO Eve: How Do Large Language Model Businesses Build Sustainable, Profitable Financial Models? - eu.36kr.com

stories.Headline: KAIST develops technology to cut AI training time by up to 70%
stories.Summary:
KAIST announced on Monday that a research team led by Professor Lee Jae-gil of the School of Computing had developed CluSTER, a fine-tuning technology for large language models. The team included Kim Hyun-jin, a doctoral student in the School of Computing, as first author. The work was presented in October at EMNLP 2026, a leading international conference on natural language processing. The technology selects training data efficiently and distributes it across multiple GPUs. Fine-tuning a large language model for specialized fields such as medicine or coding requires extra training on domain-specific data.

CluSTER analyzes how each data sample affects AI training and groups samples that produce similar learning outcomes. It then selects only the necessary samples from each group and spreads them so that multiple GPUs each handle distinct learning information. The team tested the approach on models with about 7 billion and 13 billion parameters, using three coding and medical datasets. Using only about 31 percent of the full training data, the team cut training time by up to 69.6 percent while maintaining nearly the same AI performance, so training that would take 10 hours took about 3 hours. Lee said that to improve AI training efficiency it is important not only to use more GPUs but also to make smart choices about what data to train on.

He said the research is meaningful because it can reduce the training burden of large-scale AI models by making better use of existing GPU resources. The technology is expected to ease the burden on companies and research institutions that build customer service AI, medical support AI or coding assistance AI using their own proprietary data. Performance was mainly verified in a four-GPU environment, and the technology also outperformed conventional methods in an eight-GPU setup. Further validation across diverse corporate datasets and training environments will be needed before it can be applied in real-world industrial settings. Work also remains to refine the software so it can integrate smoothly with existing AI training systems.

Articles.Title: KAIST develops technology to cut AI training time by up to 70% - 헤럴드경제

Kim Taek-hoon, vice president of Kakao Investment, said the first period confirmed that excellent AI research capabilities at the four institutes can lead to investment and real business. He said the second period expanded the awards and the scope of support so more AI start-up teams can grow in the market.

He added that support will keep expanding so research teams with technical skills can challenge startups and grow into competitive AI companies. In the first program held in January, five teams won. Four of them, AnyBridge AI from KAIST, Black Box from UNIST, Glossori from GIST and Symphobrose from DGIST, succeeded in attracting investment, and PAI Research from KAIST is set to sign an investment contract. The Black Box team completed a paid technology demonstration with Kakao Entertainment and received follow-up investments. stories.Headline: Finding peace, one click at a time: AI-made virtual sanctuaries draw young South Koreans
stories.Summary:
A 26-year-old South Korean job seeker surnamed Park created an online Buddhist temple called Sansa using vibe coding, an AI-assisted programming method that builds software from natural-language instructions, according to news reports on Nov 1. The site opened on Oct 29 and drew more than 100,000 visitors a day, with total visits surpassing 600,000. Visitors enter a temple set in a dense forest, with a large Buddha statue in the centre of the main prayer hall. Each visitor gets an avatar of a young Buddhist monk with a randomly assigned name such as Leisurely Cloud or Soft Moonlight.

Using their avatars, visitors can wander the temple, greet others by pressing their palms together, kneel on cushions to perform 108 bows, turn prayer beads and listen to chants. The site has no chat or messaging features, so visitors share the same prayer hall without interacting. The idea grew out of Park's own job-hunting struggles, when he wanted to unwind at a temple but lacked the time and energy to go. Park told a local news outlet that temples appeal to people his age because they welcome everyone, even non-Buddhists. He said seeing so many people respond made him realise many others were just as tired as he was.

Park said maybe all they really needed was a quiet place to take a break without having to say anything. The temple's success inspired similar AI-powered platforms modelled after Catholic and Protestant churches. Chanmi offers a virtual Catholic church with pews, votive candles and rosaries, where visitors can listen to hymns while Angelus bells ring three times a day, at 6am, noon and 6pm. Goyottul recreates a Protestant church where visitors can share prayer requests and listen to sermons.

Sung Hae-young, a professor of religious studies at Seoul National University, said Buddhism resonates with young people struggling with uncertainty because it acknowledges that life is full of suffering and offers ways to overcome it through their own understanding. Sung said that straightforward approach is what makes it appealing. Sung also said people want a sense of peace and sacredness like at a place of worship, but do not necessarily want to be tied to a religious community or feel pressured to believe unquestioningly. Sung said anonymous online spaces offer exactly that.

Articles.Title: Finding peace, one click at a time: AI-made virtual sanctuaries draw young South Koreans - The Straits Times

stories.Headline: Liquidity key as AI concentration makes diversification more challenging, says GIC CEO
stories.Summary:
GIC CEO Lim Chow Kiat spoke on Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026, at the Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit in Hong Kong. He said the growing concentration of artificial intelligence-related stocks is making diversification more challenging in today’s markets. GIC is responding by focusing on companies’ underlying business, investment quality and portfolio liquidity to navigate risks over the long term. He outlined three considerations for navigating increasingly concentrated markets.

First, Lim said investors should look under the hood of companies to examine their underlying businesses and determine how much exposure they have to AI. He cited the MSCI World Index, where US stocks make up about 70 per cent of weightings, even though many of these companies earn revenue from around the world. Second, he said investors should focus on the quality of companies rather than allocate capital through a top-down approach. He said that if investors do their work well and determine there is a good management team and moat, that can cut through over a longer period. Third, he said that where diversification away from AI concentration is difficult, maintaining a good level of liquidity is important to give investors room to respond to market developments.

Lim said patient investors have historically been rewarded for holding assets over the long term, benefiting from a time premium and valuations tending to revert to historical averages. But he said the rapid pace of technological change means some shifts could be structural rather than cyclical, making it harder to determine where valuations might eventually settle. He said this uncertainty should translate to more risk premium pricing and can help balance supply and demand of capital, which is especially pertinent to credit investors who may be reluctant to take on excessive exposure to a small number of large issuers. He said many long-term investors would like to be paid a little more in terms of getting that risk premium, and that this is a way for the market to digest it.

Lim said GIC’s mandate has not changed since inception even as the fund has become bigger, more globalised and specialised, and that knowing certain things do not change is important in a world that keeps changing every day. He said GIC is committed to making sure Singapore’s reserves keep growing while ensuring funds are available when the country needs them. He said maintaining a long-term investment approach does not simply mean a series of short-term investing decisions, and that because the drivers are different, such ideas keep GIC grounded. On talent, he identified two factors in attracting and retaining employees: getting the fundamentals right, including remuneration and the working environment, and a sense of purpose, which he considers an advantage for GIC as people look to contribute to something bigger than themselves. He said that beyond safeguarding Singapore’s reserves, GIC’s investments help build businesses, create jobs and support companies’ growth, giving employees a broader sense of purpose.

Articles.Title: Liquidity key as AI concentration makes diversification more challenging, says GIC CEO - The Business Times

stories.Headline: China’s robot makers have mastered the moves. Now comes the race for AI brains
stories.Summary:
Chinese robot makers are shifting from building humanoid robots that can run, dance and perform backflips to developing the artificial intelligence that could make them useful across more jobs. This field, called embodied AI, focuses on software that lets robots understand their surroundings, learn unfamiliar tasks and adapt without being programmed for every job. Chinese embodied AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan, or US$14.1 billion, across 322 deals in the first half of 2026, five times the amount a year earlier, according to the data research firm ITjuzi. Funding is increasingly reaching specialist developers of robot intelligence alongside manufacturers, as competition drives down hardware prices.

American startups including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist are developing software to teach robots different skills without extensive retraining. Generalist has said its GEN-1.5 model completed around 60 per cent of simple tasks after viewing a demonstration lasting between three and 12 seconds. China's X Square has published research showing robots acquiring handling skills from a single human video without retraining the model for each task. Specialist Chinese startups including X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI have each reached valuations of roughly US$3 billion, going by company disclosures. UBTech advertised a chief scientist position with compensation of up to 124 million yuan, and Unitree has about 30 researchers developing AI that predicts how objects behave.

Dermot McGrath of the Shanghai consultancy ZenGen Labs said robot makers have concluded that the margin won't come from the hardware but from the brain. Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang said the brain is the weakest link in the complete robotics stack, and X Square co-founder and chief operating officer Yang Qian said the aim is for robots to shift from being driven by code to being driven by common sense. Spirit AI has hired around 1,000 people to record everyday and industrial activities, while ACE Robotics uses wearable sensors to capture workers' movements and grip forces. Ant Group's robotics unit Robbyant said it trained a model using 160,000 hours of material, including 50,000 hours of human-guided robot movements, and DexForce said it can prepare some industrial tasks for deployment within six to eight hours.

Chinese firms face shortages of advanced Nvidia chips due to US export controls and a squeeze on initial public offering funding amid regulatory concerns over inflated valuations and overcrowding. Zhu Mingxuan of JoyIn Technology said the chip shortage will become a serious problem for China's embodied AI industry as robots become more powerful. Battery maker CATL said Spirit AI robots connect flexible wires during battery-pack testing at its Zhongzhou plant, reporting insertion success above 99 per cent, and Robbyant said its robots handle orders in two Shanghai pharmacies. Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said the company had tested OpenAI's GPT-6 on robots with encouraging results, and that GPT-7, if released next year, could bring robotics its own ChatGPT moment. Consultant Georg Stieler said that if the question is when a customer can count on such systems, he would add years, not months.

Articles.Title: China’s robot makers have mastered the moves. Now comes the race for AI brains - The Business Times

stories.Headline: European shares ease as AI-driven tech selloff deepens
stories.Summary:
European shares fell on Friday, October 30, 2026, as technology stocks came under pressure from renewed worries about rising AI investment costs. The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.29% to 647.23 points by 0929 GMT. The technology sector index led the declines, falling 2%. The drop came after earnings from Amazon and Intel brought back concerns about heavy AI-related spending and the returns it can generate. The STOXX 600 was still set to post both weekly and monthly gains, and it was on track for its best month since June.

Sector heavyweight ASML fell 5%, while STMicroelectronics, BESI and Infineon fell between 3.3% and 4.8%. Chip stocks Soitec and Aixtron fell 5.7% and 3.6% respectively. French consumer prices rose more than expected in October, recording the highest inflation rate since December 2023. Michael Hewson, chief analyst at MCH Market Insights, said the market was trying to wrestle with the equation of a huge amount of capital spending relative to the timeline of a return on investment. He said that at the moment, they do not have an answer to that.

Political unrest in France also weighed on sentiment this month, as the country faces pressure from rising living costs and elevated government debt, driving French bond yields to multi-year highs. Robust earnings from companies such as ASML, Shell and Airbus reinforced confidence in the health of European corporates. LSEG I/B/E/S data showed European blue-chips were heading for their second-best quarterly earnings in four years. Universal Music Group jumped 11.2% after posting a pick-up in subscription streaming revenue in the third quarter. Investors also awaited third-quarter euro zone gross domestic product figures later in the day.

Articles.Title: European shares ease as AI-driven tech selloff deepens - The Business Times

stories.Headline: AI wardens sharpen China's river stewardship abilities - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Ordos in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region has built a drone patrol network to monitor tributaries of the Yellow River, according to Xinhua. From a control room in the city, Fu Laichen remotely commands a fleet of patrol drones that fly over the rugged terrain of the Kubuqi Desert. The drones were flying about 100 kilometers away as Fu checked readings on the screens. The combined watershed of the 10 tributaries spans 10,800 square kilometers and is a major source of sediment for the Yellow River.

Since 2023, Ordos has built 13 outdoor drone hangars and a smart platform that links drones to an automated patrol network. Fan Hongbo, deputy director of the city's river and lake protection center, said drones have logged 107.33 flight hours and traveled 4,483.26 kilometers for river stewardship patrols. More than 500 camera sites now cover the Yellow River tributaries, and Shi Huidong, head of the river and lake management office in Dalad Banner, said AI analyzes footage around the clock and automatically flags encroachment. Shi added that rain radar delivers rainfall forecasts three hours in advance.

Fu, 28, has worked in the control center for more than two years and said the new model lets staff remotely command drone operations and monitor rivers. He said drones are launched when weather permits, and staff watch for signal failures and can pre-set or adjust flight routes for targeted inspections. He said the system can capture footage of unauthorized activities such as sand mining and reveal flood-blocking problems. Fu said drone patrols ramp up between June and September, the flood season, and the center promptly shares updates with relevant authorities.

The Yellow River runs 843.5 kilometers through Inner Mongolia, about 15.4 percent of its total length and its longest winding segment across nine provincial-level regions. Yang Jianlong from the banner's forestry and grassland bureau said the system is a technical backbone for local restoration, with data helping officials design targeted measures. Thanks to decades of ecological efforts, the average annual sediment flowing into the Yellow River from these tributaries in Ordos has dropped from 27 million tonnes to 4 million tonnes. The article says the river now has cleaner waters and more sustainable water use.

Articles.Title: AI wardens sharpen China's river stewardship abilities - Xinhua

stories.Headline: HP looks to AI printers to navigate shifting China market
stories.Summary:
HP Inc launched 13 AI-powered learning printers for Chinese families at its autumn event in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province. The models add AI homework grading, error-question collection and curated educational resources to HP's WeChat mini-program. Rollin Jin, vice-president and general manager of HP Printing Systems Group of Greater China, said HP's share of China's printing market was about 38.6 percent in 2025, citing data from International Data Corp. He said the company still held a clear lead over the second-place player. Jin said China's printer shipments peaked above 19 million units around 2022 and now sit between 13 million and 14 million. He said inkjet and laser shipments have converged at roughly 7 million units each, and refillable ink-tank models are gaining share within inkjet.

HP says it does not build its own large language models and instead calls third-party and vertical models through the cloud. HP's pre-launch research found 50 percent of surveyed users prioritized homework grading and 48 percent sought error-question collection. Jin warned that the more HP leads, the more it must prepare for adversity, citing shifting market-access rules and localization demands, the rise of Chinese printer brands, and changing demand as traditional sectors contract. He said that if HP stays only in hardware, supplies and existing applications, the space will be limited, and that it comes down to innovation and keeping pace with new user needs. He said overseas AI printing solutions cannot be deployed directly in China and require localized interfaces, cloud partnerships and content collaborations.

HP says it is investing in China-specific AI infrastructure. HP's 2026 Work Relationship Index found 67 percent of Chinese knowledge workers use AI agents, the highest among 15 surveyed markets and above the 47 percent global average. The report included China for the first time, with 1,300 respondents, and found 74 percent expect AI to fundamentally reshape daily life within five years. An iMedia Research report found 72.75 percent of surveyed consumers buy home learning printers for printing coursework. A China Consumers Association survey cited by HP found 27.8 percent of respondents rank product quality as the top purchase factor.

Articles.Title: HP looks to AI printers to navigate shifting China market - China Daily

stories.Headline: Baidu empowers industrial ecosystems and digital future through full-stack AI innovation
stories.Summary:
Baidu, the Chinese technology company founded in 2000, has built a full-stack AI framework that spans its self-developed Kunlun AI chips, its AI Cloud, the ERNIE large language models and AI agents. The company says it has brought three generations of Kunlun chips into mass production and was the first to deploy a 10,000-chip cluster using domestically developed AI chips. It has invested more than 190 billion yuan, about $28.52 billion, in research and development over the past decade and says it ranked first in China in AI patent applications and grants for eight consecutive years. ERNIE 5.1, launched in May 2026, uses multi-dimensional elastic pre-training and delivers leading performance at around six percent of the pre-training cost of comparable models, according to the company.

Baidu AI Cloud holds a 16.6 percent market share and ranks first in the industry, according to IDC. The company's AI agents include DuMate, a general-purpose agent, Baidu Yijing, a multi-agent digital human platform, and Famou Agent, a self-evolving agent, which Baidu says help cut costs and improve efficiency in workplace collaboration, content creation, production scheduling, process optimization and logistics planning. In autonomous driving, Baidu ranks first globally in patent families related to high-level autonomous driving, and its Apollo Go ride-hailing platform had accumulated more than 350 million kilometers of autonomous driving as of August 2026, including over 240 million km of fully driverless operations, across 28 cities worldwide. Baidu Wenku and Baidu Netdisk have nearly 300 million monthly active users combined, and Kuku AI, a general-purpose agent built through those platforms, has more than 40 million monthly active users worldwide.

On talent, Baidu pledged in 2020 to train five million AI professionals over five years and says it reached that goal ahead of schedule in April 2024. In April 2025 it announced a new five-year target of training 10 million AI professionals and launched the Xinghe Plan to train five million specialists in large language models. On sustainability, Baidu was included in S&P Global's Sustainability Yearbook (China Edition) 2024, its MSCI ESG rating rose to A, and it received a low-risk ESG rating from Sustainalytics. With the International Fund for Animal Welfare, Baidu developed an automated system to identify images of products made from endangered wildlife, achieving 86 percent accuracy across 34 categories of endangered species and their products, a project selected as an outstanding case under the International Telecommunication Union's AI for Good program.

Articles.Title: Baidu empowers industrial ecosystems and digital future through full-stack AI innovation - China Daily

stories.Headline: Shanghai AI startup StartLux explores opportunities in decision models and local AI
stories.Summary:
Shanghai-based AI startup StartLux is exploring decision models and locally deployed AI, according to China Daily. Its model StartLux-Decision v1.1 27B Instant recently ranked first among 174 entries on Hugging Face's Decision Index 0.3.2 leaderboard with a score of 69.12, based on company-published results. Chuan-Wei Kuo, co-founder and chief technology officer of StartLux, said decision models could cut computing costs and improve efficiency. Unlike general-purpose large language models that mainly generate text, decision models choose from predefined options and return probabilities, which suits customer service routing, web operations and AI agent execution.

Kuo expects more than 80 percent of AI demand to be handled locally within the next one to two years. StartLux plans to launch a consumer-facing local AI agent, followed by enterprise solutions next year, with products designed to process data locally rather than send it to third-party servers. Gao Chengyuan, head of Influence Academy, said decision quality and speed are becoming more important as AI moves from talking to doing, and that local deployment could suit government, financial and industrial customers needing data security, low latency and cost control. Kuo said the decision model field remains exploratory, with progress depending on technological breakthroughs and practical applications, and that StartLux will continue developing its recursive self-improvement framework, whose Auto Research approach uses AI to generate hypotheses, conduct experiments and evaluate results.

Inc42 reports that decision models are gaining attention as companies move from chatbots to AI agents. TypeSafe AI, founded by Diogo Almeida, released Jev in September, focusing on scores and yes-or-no probabilities rather than text. Cloudflare introduced Clef and Clef-flash, Microsoft released Decision-1 based on Alibaba's Qwen family, AWS introduced Strands Decider 2B, OpenAI launched a Decisions API, and Perplexity has explored decision-oriented APIs. Articul8 AI, spun out of Intel in 2024, has developed around 28 domain models and says its approach can reduce token usage by more than 50% in relevant workflows, and in October it announced Bivia, a multimodal decision model. Ananthanarayanan S, Articul8's managing director for India, said enterprises need a system connecting their data and domain knowledge with models suited to specific workflows.

PurpleTalk's applied AI research lab Sthānika developed the Sieve family, and Sieve-31Bv3 returns a defined answer with a confidence score. The company said Sieve-31Bv3 scored 71.1 on the full Jev Decision Index and 71.7 on the public test, where it ranked third. Sridhar Muppidi, cofounder of PurpleTalk, said the private tests matter most because they come from domains outside the public suite, and Bharat Lingam, CEO of PurpleTalk, said decision models will open a new category of agentic systems that are more reliable, more controllable and fast enough for voice, customer experience and robotics. Kerala-based ConvAI Innovations has developed Laya, an open-weight decision model meant to run locally on laptops and mobile phones, and founder Nandakishore Mukkunnoth said the initial focus was small, fast models that did not always require cloud access. Shubham Gupta, founding general partner at Together Fund, said what cannot be copied is a company's own record of decisions and outcomes, and that the real test for startups is how fast a model improves on a specific, high-volume workflow.

Articles.Title: Shanghai AI startup StartLux explores opportunities in decision models and local AI - China Daily

stories.Headline: Cooperation and openness key to unlocking AI's potential, expert says
stories.Summary:
Zhu Keli, founding director of the China Institute of New Economy, said international cooperation and open-source development are essential to turning advances in artificial intelligence into economic growth. He said countries face shared challenges that no single nation can address alone. He also said no single country has all the data, computing resources, and industry experience needed to develop and apply AI across every field. His comments came as the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit opened on Tuesday in Wuzhen, Zhejiang province.

The summit runs through Thursday and is focused on open source and openness, joint contribution, and shared benefits. AI cooperation and governance are among the topics on its agenda. Zhu said closed technology systems could lead to duplicated investment and fragmented standards, which would limit the scope for AI applications. He said areas such as climate modeling, public health, and marine environmental monitoring require data and AI models from multiple countries.

Zhu said international cooperation is also needed to address cross-border digital governance and to assess AI safety risks. The articles do not say what steps governments or companies will take next. They also do not say what the summit is expected to produce. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Cooperation and openness key to unlocking AI's potential, expert says - China Daily Global Edition
